STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r28.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r28.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r28.claim: Verse 172 presents a universal, pretemporal covenant in which all human beings are bound to recognize God's Lordship; it grounds subsequent covenants between God and humanity mediated through prophets.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r28.anchor:
the universal, pretemporal covenant between God and all human beings
obligating them to recognize God’s Lordship

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p136.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p136.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p136.claim: The surah's closing section returns to Quraysh, using the primordial covenant of all Adam's descendants about God's oneness and providence to deny them an excuse of ignorance; a messenger now reminds them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p136.anchor: first reminded of the covenant found in human nature. It was made by with all the progeny of Adam (sws) by the Almighty regarding His oneness and providence.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p136.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p136.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p136.claim: Because Arabs had received no scripture, arguments addressed them through familiar history and evident facts of human nature and intellect; the preceding historical accounts prepared that argument.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p136.anchor: debate with them could either have been based on the history well-known to them or on the obvious facts drawn from human nature and intellect.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p136.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p136.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p136.claim: The preceding accounts of local nations and Israelites show that God sends messengers and establishes earthly judgment: rejecters are destroyed, believers succeed, and Quraysh now face this decisive phase.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p136.anchor: Whenever these messengers came, they set up His court of justice on this earth. Nations who denied their respective messengers were destroyed and those who attested to them were successful.

BURSEVI:v3p208/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p208/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p208/r3.claim: The passage tells Muhammad to recall to the Children of Israel when God took their covenant from Adam's descendants.
BURSEVI:v3p208/r3.anchor: {وإذ أخذ ربك} أي : واذكر يا محمد لبني إسرائيل وقت أخذ ربك

BURSEVI:v3p208/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p208/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p208/r4.claim: Children of Adam means Adam and his offspring, a name for the human kind; the intended descendants are those who would have children, excluding the infertile, unmarried, or those who died young.
BURSEVI:v3p208/r4.anchor: أي : آدم وأولاده كأنه صار اسما للنوع كالإنسان والبشر والمراد بهم الذين ولد لهم

BURSEVI:v3p208/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p208/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p208/r5.claim: Their backs means their fathers' loins, indicating that the covenant was taken while they remained in their fathers' loins, before being placed in mothers' wombs.
BURSEVI:v3p208/r5.anchor: {من ظهورهم} بدل من بني آدم بدل البعض ، أي من أصلابهم وفيه تنبيه على أن الميثاق قد أخذ منهم

BURSEVI:v3p208/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p208/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p208/r6.claim: Their offspring is the object of taking: God brought generations from one another through the succession of loins, wombs, periods, and stages until the last child born.
BURSEVI:v3p208/r6.anchor: {ذريتهم} مفعول أخذ ، أي : نسلهم قرنا بعد قرن

BURSEVI:v3p208/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p208/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p208/r7.claim: Each descendant was made to testify for himself, not another, establishing God's complete lordship, exclusive servitude, and its associated obligations.
BURSEVI:v3p208/r7.anchor: {وأشهدهم على أنفسهم} أي : أشهد كل واحد من أولئك الذريات المخصوصين المأخوذين من ظهور آبائهم على نفسه

BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r1.claim: Am I not your Lord is spoken with an implied verb of saying and means the absolute master and nurturer of their affairs, with no one else involved.
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r1.anchor: {ألست بربكم} على إرادة القول ، أي : قائلا ألست بربكم ومالك أمركم ومربيكم على الإطلاق

BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r2.claim: Their answer, yes, we testify, affirms that God is their Lord and deity and that they have no other lord.
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r2.anchor: {بلى شهدنآ} أي : على أنفسنا بأنك ربنا وإلهنا

BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r3.claim: Bala affirms what follows a negative and thus means you are our Lord, whereas naam confirms the preceding negative and would mean you are not our Lord, hence disbelief.
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r3.anchor: والفرق بين بلى ونعم أن بلى إثبات لما بعد النفي ، أي : أنت ربنا فيكون إيمانا ونعم

BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r4.claim: The scene is figurative: signs in the horizons and souls and an innate capacity for knowledge are represented as testimony-taking, and their recognition as confession; no literal extraction or dialogue occurred.
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r4.anchor: وهذا تمثيل وتخييل نزل تمكينهم من العلم بربوبيته بنصب الدلائل الآفاقية والأنفسية وخلق الاستعداد فيهم منزلة الإشهاد

BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r5.claim: God's address to heaven and earth and their obedient reply illustrate how figurative representation is common in scripture, hadith, and eloquent speech.
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r5.anchor: قال الله تعالى : {فقال لها وللارض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتآ أتينا طآااعين}

BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r6.claim: The covenant prevents people from pleading at resurrection that they were unaware of God's oneness and its obligations, since their innate disposition and latent knowledge leave them no such excuse.
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r6.anchor: {أن تقولوا} مفعول له لما قبله من الأخذ والإشهاد ، أي فعلنا ما فعلنا كراهة

BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r7.speaker: حواشي سعدى لبى
BURSEVI:v3p208#2/r7.claim: The Hashiyat Sa'di Labi argues that even if the testimony were literal and God later erased its memory, people still could not say they were unaware.

BURSEVI:v3p210/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p210/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p210/r1.claim: The Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya distinguishes created taking, which draws an existing thing from an existing thing, from God's creation of what is nonexistent out of nonexistence, as in the covenant scene.
BURSEVI:v3p210/r1.anchor: في الآية إشارة إلى أن أخذ المخلوقين يكون أخذ الشيء الموجود من الشيء الموجود وأن أخذ الخالق تارة هو أخذ الشيء المعدوم من العدم

BURSEVI:v3p210/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p210/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p210/r2.claim: God brought into existence the nonexistent progeny, backs, and ancestors by His power, giving them an existence suited to that primordial state.
BURSEVI:v3p210/r2.anchor: فكان بنو آدم معدومين وظهورهم معدومين وذرياتهم معدومين فأخذ بكمال قدرته ذرياتهم المعدومة إلى يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v3p210/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p210/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p210/r3.claim: God extracted particles of descendants from Adam and successive loins; souls then stood in three ranks: the forerunners, the people of the right, and the people of the left.
BURSEVI:v3p210/r3.anchor: والأرواح في تلك الحالة جنود مجندة في ثلاثة صفوف : الصف الأول : أرواح السابقين

BURSEVI:v3p210/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p210/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p210/r4.claim: The forerunners heard God spiritually, witnessed His beauty, loved Him, answered from love, and pledged to love and worship Him alone.
BURSEVI:v3p210/r4.anchor: فسمع السابقون بسمع نوراني روحاني خطابه وشاهدوا بأبصار نورانية جماله وأحبوه بأفئدة روحانية ربانية نورانية

BURSEVI:v3p210/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p210/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p210/r5.claim: The people of the right heard and witnessed spiritually, believed, answered as servants, and pledged to worship God alone.
BURSEVI:v3p210/r5.anchor: وسمع أصحاب الميمنة بسمع روحاني خطابه وطالعوا بأبصار

BURSEVI:v3p210/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p210/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p210/r6.claim: The people of the left heard from behind the veil of divine might, with blocked ears, veiled sight, and sealed hearts, and answered reluctantly under a covenant of servitude.
BURSEVI:v3p210/r6.anchor: وسمع أصحاب المشأمة خطابه بسمع روحاني من وراء حجاب العزة ، وفي آذانهم وقر الغرة

BURSEVI:v3p210/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p210/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p210/r7.claim: Differences between disbelief and faith among people ultimately reflect differences in their spiritual and divine preparedness.
BURSEVI:v3p210/r7.anchor: فالآن يرجع التفاوت بين الخليقة في الكفر والإيمان إلى تفاوت الاستعدادات الروحانية والربانية

ELMALILI:7:172-181/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:172-181/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:172-181/r1.claim: The Turkish rendering presents the primordial testimony as God making people witnesses against themselves and asking whether He is their Lord.
ELMALILI:7:172-181/r1.anchor: onları nefislerine karşı şâhid tutarak “Rabbiniz değil miyim?” diye işhâd ettiği vakit

ELMALILI:7:172-181#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:172-181#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:172-181#2/r1.claim: Every human descendant is given a valid human nature capable of witnessing, and an innate covenant to recognize God’s oneness and lordship; the verse invokes God’s testimony in 3:18.
ELMALILI:7:172-181#2/r1.anchor: her zürriyetin üzerinde fıtraten böyle bir taahhüd bulunduğuna

ELMALILI:7:172-181#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:172-181#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:172-181#2/r2.claim: Human self-awareness and possession of spirit and consciousness entail accepting God’s lordship and unity; one’s own existence bears witness to God.
ELMALILI:7:172-181#2/r2.anchor: kendimizi duymanın kendi varlığımızın Senin vücûb-i vücûduna, vahdâniyetine, rubûbiyetine bir şâhid bulunduğunu şu‘ûr-ı sarih ile duymuyorduk.

ELMALILI:7:172-181#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:172-181#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:172-181#2/r3.claim: God recalled the otherwise hidden covenant clearly so that people could not excuse themselves at Judgment by claiming they were unaware or had received no explicit reminder.
ELMALILI:7:172-181#2/r3.anchor: Hafî olan bu taahhüdü bize sarâhaten tezkir ve iş‘âr lütfunda da bulunmadın diye

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r1.claim: The first human responsibility is to affirm God’s existence and oneness and worship Him alone; accountability would lack a just basis if people lacked adequate information or the capacity to attain it, and these verses explain how God equipped them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r1.anchor: Bu iki âyette insanların Allah tarafından böyle bir bilgi veya yetenekle donatıldığı haber verilmekte ve bunun gerekçesi açıklanmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r2.claim: The first interpretation says that before creating the world God gathered all future human souls in the spirit realm, made them witness His existence and affirm His lordship, and took a covenant from them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r2.anchor: Allah Teâlâ dünyayı yaratmadan önce dünyaya gelecek olan bütün insanların ruhlarını –sonraları âyetin lafzından hareketle “rûz-i elest, bezm-i elest” şeklinde terimleşen– ruhlar âleminde bir araya getirerek onları kendi varlığına tanık kılmış; kendisinin onların rabbi olduğunu yine onlara onaylatmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r3.claim: On this interpretation, the people themselves witnessed the covenant, some witnessed for others, or God and the angels were declared its witnesses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r3.anchor: onların bizzat kendilerini şahit tutmuş veya bir kısmını diğerleri hakkında tanık göstermiş ya da –bir başka yoruma göre– bizzat kendisinin ve meleklerin bu sözleşmeye şahit olduklarını onlara bildirmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r4.claim: The covenant blocks people from pleading ignorance of their responsibility or excusing inherited unbelief and idolatry as their ancestors’ invention.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r4.anchor: insanların, “Bizim böyle bir sorumluluğumuz olduğunu bilmiyorduk” diyerek yahut inkârcılık veya putperestliği kendilerinin icat etmediğini, bunu atalarından miras aldıklarını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r5.claim: This precreation reading was held by early Salaf and Sufi scholars and by most Sunni and Shi‘i theologians.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r5.anchor: İlk dönem Selef âlimleriyle sûfî âlimler, Sünnî ve Şiî kelâm bilginlerinin çoğunluğu âyeti böyle yorumlamışlardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r6.claim: The second interpretation takes the covenant figuratively: it occurs as each human body is created, rather than before the world.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r6.anchor: Burada belirtilen sözleşme mecazi anlamda olup bu olay, dünya yaratılmadan önce değil, her insanın kendi bedeninin yaratılması sırasında gerçekleşmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r7.claim: Accounts place this endowment either during creation of offspring in the father’s loins or during formation in the womb; God implants in human nature the capacity to recognize and understand His existence and oneness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r7.anchor: Bir görüşe göre zürriyetlerin baba sulbünde yaratılışı esnasında, başka bir görüşe göre anne rahmine yerleşip organik oluşumunu tamamlaması sürecinde Allah Teâlâ insanoğlunun doğasına ya da fıtratına kendisinin varlık ve birliğini tanıma, kavrama ve dolayısıyla kendisine inanma yeteneğini yerleştirmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r8.claim: God gives each person sufficient mental and psychological capacity to believe and creates many inner and outer signs of His existence and oneness; the covenant scene figuratively portrays this capacity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r8.anchor: İnsanın doğasındaki iman kabiliyeti bu âyetlerde temsilî bir dille anlatılmış bulunmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r9.speaker: Zemahşerî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r9.claim: Zamakhshari supports the figurative, innate-capacity interpretation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r9.anchor: İnsanın doğasındaki iman kabiliyeti bu âyetlerde temsilî bir dille anlatılmış bulunmaktadır (Zemahşerî, II, 103).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r10.claim: Mu‘tazilite and Maturidi scholars, some Ash‘arite and Shi‘i scholars, and apparently Fakhr al-Din al-Razi hold the second interpretation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r10.anchor: Mu‘tezile ve Mâtürîdî âlimleriyle bazı Eş‘arî ve Şiî âlimlerinin de bu görüşte oldukları bildirilmekte, Fahreddin er-Râzî’nin de bu görüşte olduğu anlaşılmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r11.speaker: İbn Teymiyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r11.claim: Later Salafis, especially Ibn Taymiyya, understand the covenant as God giving people the psychological capacity to recognize His existence and oneness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r11.anchor: Başta İbn Teymiyye olmak üzere sonraki Selefîler, Allah’ın insandan ahid ve mîsâk almasını, insanın psikolojik muhtevasına kendi varlık ve birliğini tanıma kapasitesi vermesi şeklinde anlamışlardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r12.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r12.claim: The Prophet’s hadith that every newborn is born upon fitra also describes this innate capacity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r12.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in, “Her doğan çocuk fıtrat üzere doğar” anlamındaki hadisi de (Buhârî, “Cenâiz”, 93; Ebû Dâvûd, “Sünnet”, 18) bunu anlatmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r13.claim: Accepting the first interpretation entails that souls were created before bodies, while proponents of the second deny this.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r13.anchor: İlk görüş doğru kabul edildiğinde ruhların bedenlerden önce yaratıldığını da kabul etmek gerekmektedir. Ancak ikinci görüşü benimseyenler bunun doğru olmadığını savunurlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r14.claim: Because the matter belongs to the unseen and exceeds human knowledge, one should affirm that a covenant was taken without insisting on its precise nature; the duty is to believe humans can know God’s lordship and to keep their pledge, as 7:174 indicates.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:172/r14.anchor: Konu insanın bilgi alanını aştığı ve gayb alanına girdiği için âyetlerde bildirileni tasdik ederek insanlardan bir şekilde iman sözü alındığına inandıktan sonra bunun mahiyetinin ne olduğu hususunda kesin bir görüşü kabul etmek gerekli değildir.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p53/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p53/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p53/.claim: Before Adam entered the world, God secured his exclusive worship and obedience; the later account of this covenant is in 7:172–173.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p53/.anchor: Before sending Adam (sws) in this world, He actually took a promise from him to worship and obey Him only.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.claim: After the covenant reminder, the Israelites’ example warns Quraysh against ingratitude toward God’s favors.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.anchor: After they are reminded of the above-mentioned covenant, the example of the Israelites is presented before them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.claim: Islahi says idh reminds listeners of a definite incident even if they have forgotten it or departed from it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.anchor: serves to remind people of an incident that they accept as a certain happening regardless of having forgotten it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.claim: With contextual indications, a singular address can encompass a plural audience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.anchor: in the presence of concomitant indications an address in the singular encompasses plurality

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.claim: In this context, the singular speaker addresses each person in the group individually.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.anchor: is addressing every person of the group individually

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.claim: Islahi parses “from their loins” as a badal, or appositive, to the preceding expression.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.claim: The pledge concerns all Adam’s descendants through the Day of Judgement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.anchor: it relates to all his progeny that will be born until the Day of Judgement

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.claim: The event occurred before the descendants’ spirits were breathed into their bodies.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.anchor: was done at the time before these spirits were blown into their bodies

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.claim: The pledge required accepting God as Lord as well as God, not merely acknowledging Him as deity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.anchor: God did not take a promise from the progeny of Adam (sws) that merely he was their God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.claim: Arabs accepted God as deity but had other lords, although the pledge acknowledged God’s providence alone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.anchor: the Arabs never rejected him being God; however, they had many Lords besides God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.claim: A word meaning “lest” is omitted before the excuse clauses, yielding the precise sense of the passage.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p141.anchor: a word to the effect y (lest) is suppressed before

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.claim: Everyone is accountable for monotheism and innate guidance on the basis of the pledge, whether or not they received a prophet’s message.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.anchor: them on the basis of the afore-mentioned pledge whether he has received the message of a prophet or not

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.claim: Receiving a prophet’s message adds proof and makes accountability twofold.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.anchor: In case he did, it will be a further burden of proof on him and his accountability will become two-fold

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.claim: Without a prophet’s message, a person still has no excuse regarding the obvious innate guidance of human nature.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.anchor: a person will not have an excuse regarding the obvious innate guidance he was provided by his nature

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.claim: The Qur’an presents the pledge as a real happening, grounding accountability before God in His providence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.anchor: mentioned this incident as a real happening

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.claim: Human beings need not recall when or where; their innate cognizance of the pledge remains, while God reveals its unseen occasion, which only He knows, making this natural knowledge conclusive proof.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.anchor: its cognizance is found within human nature

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.speaker: modern philosophers
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.claim: Modern philosophers claim humanity began with polytheism, driven by fear of unseen forces amid calamities; as knowledge grew, people abandoned imagined deities and accepted one God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.anchor: our modern philosophers say that human beings began their religion with polytheism

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.claim: Islahi rejects this philosophical account and says he refuted it in his commentary on al-Fātiḥah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p142.anchor: I have refuted this view of these philosophers

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.claim: Religious awareness begins with gratitude: fear arises only after people recognize blessings they possess and value their provider, so humanity began by thanking and worshipping God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.anchor: awareness of favours and their provider and the zeal to express gratitude for them comes before fear

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.speaker: One group
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.claim: One group treats the newborn as a blank slate, with later cognizance and environmental influences writing on it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.anchor: when a person is born, his nature is like a clean slate

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.claim: Against the blank-slate view, Islahi argues that environmental traditions themselves arise from human nature; innate good and just facts become evil when unrestrained desires overpower them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.anchor: Whatever good and bad traditions and currents are found in the environment are themselves the consequence of human nature itself

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.claim: Recognition of one God alone belongs to true human nature, a point on which monotheists and polytheists agree.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.anchor: In true human nature, there exists only the acknowledgement of a single God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.claim: Since other deities lack an innate basis, proponents of polytheism bear the burden of proof; the Qur’an repeatedly demands evidence for their invented gods.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.anchor: the onus of proof for the existence of other deities lies with the proponents of polytheism

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.claim: The Qur’an’s teachings are reminders of guidance already innate in people, which they neglect for immediate gains and pleasures.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.anchor: whatever beliefs and deeds it instructs people about and whatever sins it stops people from are not externally imposed on them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.claim: Islahi rejects Marxist and Freudian reductions of human belief and conduct to hunger and sexual desire, which he says recast religion and morality around those appetites.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p143.anchor: all the philosophy and ideology of human beings revolve around these two things

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r1.claim: These readers use the singular form dhurriyyatahum in the phrase from their backs.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي من ظهورهم ذريتهم واحدة.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r2.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r2.claim: These readers use the plural form dhurriyyatihim.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر: ذرياتهم* جماعة .

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r3.claim: Dhurriyya can denote one person, as in Zechariah’s request for a righteous child and the promise of Yahya.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r3.anchor: فمما جاء فيه ذرية يراد به الواحد قوله: هنالك دعا زكريا ربه

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r5.claim: The singular-reading argument treats dhurriyya as a collective applying to everyone, so it needs no plural ending.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r5.anchor: فمن أفرد جعله جمعا؛ فاستغنى عن جمعه بوقوعه على الجميع.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r6.claim: The plural is defensible whether dhurriyya is singular or already collective, since broken plurals themselves can be pluralized.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r6.anchor: وإن كان جمعا فجمعه أيضا حسن، لأنك قد رأيت الجموع المكسرة قد جمعت نحو: الطرقات، والجزرات ، وصواحبات يوسف.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r7.claim: The singular can remain unchanged because, like bashar, dhurriyya denotes either one or many.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r7.anchor: كما أن قوله: بشر تقع على الواحد والجميع، فالجميع كقوله: أبشر يهدوننا

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r8.claim: One proposed derivation makes dhurriyya a faʿūlūla form from dharr, with final rāʾ replaced by yāʾ, as in dahdhiya.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r8.anchor: فأما مثال ذرية من الفعل فيجوز أن يكون فعلولة من الذر، فأبدلت من الراء التي هي اللام الأخيرة ياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r9.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r9.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r9.claim: Another proposal derives dhurriyya as faʿīla from dharr, with rāʾ replaced by yāʾ to resolve doubling despite an intervening consonant.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r9.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون فعيلة منه، فأبدلت من الراء الياء، كما تبدل من هذه الحروف للتضعيف، وإن وقع فيها الفصل

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r10.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r10.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r10.claim: A further proposal treats it as a nisba form from dharr, with the expected fatḥa changed to ḍamma, as in dahri and sahli.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r10.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون فعلية نسبا إلى الذر، إلا أن الفتحة أبدلت منها الضمة، كما أبدلوا في الإضافة إلى الدهر دهري، وإلى السهل: سهلي

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r11.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r11.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r11.claim: It may instead derive from dharaʾa, with contraction as in al-bariyya.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون فعيلة من ذرأ الله الخلق، اجتمع على تخفيفها، كما اجتمع على تخفيف البرية*.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r12.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r12.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r12.claim: The text also begins a possible derivation from the verb in the phrase about winds scattering things.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p104/r12.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون فعيلة من قوله: تذروه الرياح [الكهف/ 45]

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r1.claim: Abu Amr alone reads both verbs with yāʾ, keeping the clause in third-person narration.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ أبو عمرو وحده: أن يقولوا* أو يقولوا بالياء جميعا

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r2.claim: The yāʾ reading fits the preceding third-person account and the later report that they said yes.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r2.anchor: أن الذي تقدم من الكلام على الغيبة، وذلك قوله: وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r3.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r3.claim: The other readers use tāʾ for both verbs, prompted by the direct address in the covenant dialogue.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r3.anchor: حجة من قرأ بالتاء: أنه قد جرى في الكلام خطاب فقال : ألست بربكم، قالوا: بلى شهدنا

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r4.claim: Both person choices are sound because the people described in the third person are the same people addressed in meaning.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#2/r4.anchor: وكلا الوجهين حسن، لأن الغيب هم المخاطبون في المعنى.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r1.claim: ذريتهم is read singular or plural: singular is one in form but collective in meaning, supported by أو الطفل; plural matches the preceding plural ظهورهم.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r1.anchor: ودليله قوله تعالى ﴿ أو الطفل ﴾ والحجة لمن جمع أنه طابق بذلك بين اللفظين

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r2.claim: The author explains the covenant as God wiping Adam's back, bringing forth humanity like tiny ants, and taking their pledge through intellect placed within them.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r2.anchor: أن الله مسح ظهر آدم فأخرج الخلق منه كأمثال الذر فأخذ عليهم العهد بعقل ركبه فيهم

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r3.claim: At maturity each person can reason that God created him and infer God's existence from that knowledge.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r3.anchor: فكل أحد إذا بلغ الحلم علم بعقله أن الله عز وجل خالقه واستدل بذلك عليه

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r4.claim: The author says prophets were sent to clarify the proofs and reinforce the evidence against people.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r4.anchor: فإن قيل فما وجه بعث الرسل فقل إيضاح للبراهين وتأكيد للحجة عليهم

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r5.claim: أن تقولوا is read with yāʾ or tāʾ; the author refers to explanations of analogous readings rather than repeating their arguments.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r5.anchor: يقرا بالياء والتاء وقد ذكر من الحجة في نظائره ما يدل عليه ويغني عن إعادته

IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r2.claim: They read ذريتهم as singular; Nafi, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read it as plural.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r2.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائى ﴿ من ظهورهم ذريتهم ﴾ واحدة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r3.claim: Abu Amr alone reads أن يقولوا and أو يقولوا with yāʾ; the remaining readers use tāʾ in both.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r3.anchor: فقرأ أبو عمرو وحده / أن يقولوا . . أو يقولوآ / بالياء جميعا

QIRAAT-ER:7:172:10#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:172:10#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:172:10#1/r1.claim: The plural dhurriyyāt makes offspring groups explicitly multiple rather than collective singular.
QIRAAT-ER:7:172:10#1/r1.anchor: emphasizing multiplicity of distinct offspring groups

QIRAAT-ER:7:172:22#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:172:22#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:172:22#1/r1.claim: A third-person plural yāʾ replaces second-person tāʾ, changing the excuse-makers from the addressed audience to reported third parties.
QIRAAT-ER:7:172:22#1/r1.anchor: changes the excuse-makers from the addressed audience to a reported third party

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p242/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p242/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p242/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God passed His hand over Adam’s loins, drew out all his descendants through the Last Day, and took their covenant that He is their Lord; accordingly, anyone asked who his Lord is answers Allah.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p242/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى ﴿ وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم ﴾ قال مسح الله على صلب آدم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p242/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p242/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p242/r2.claim: Al-Hasan is reported to have given the same account of the primordial covenant.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p242/r2.anchor: وقال معمر وكان الحسن يقول مثل ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p218/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p218/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p218/r13.claim: A hadith transmitted through multiple routes describes God drawing Adam's descendants from his back and taking their pledge that He alone is Lord and God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p218/r13.anchor: روي في الحديث من طرق أخذ من ظهر آدم ذريته وأخذ عليهم العهد بأنه ربهم وأن لا إله غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p218/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p218/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p218/r14.claim: Reports differ about how, in what form, where, and when the descendants were extracted; Abū Ḥayyān says their apparent wording conflicts with the verse and attempts to reconcile them are strained.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p218/r14.anchor: واختلفوا في كيفية الإخراج وهيئة المخرج والمكان والزمان وتقرير هذه الأشياء محلها ذلك الحديث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p218/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p218/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p218/r15.claim: He prefers al-Zamakhsharī's figurative account: God installed rational signs of His lordship and unity, so minds and consciences effectively testified to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p218/r15.anchor: وأحسن ما تكلم به على هذه الآية ما فسره به الزمخشري قال من باب التمثيل والتخييل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the exchange as representation, like God's command to a thing to be and the earth and heaven's response; the cited verses and Arabic poetry portray meaning without literal speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r1.anchor: ونظيره قول الله عز وجل إنما قولنا لشيء إذا أردناه أن نقول له كن فيكون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r2.claim: He parses وأن تقولوا as a purpose clause: the installed proofs prevent people from pleading ignorance at the Resurrection or blaming ancestral shirk.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r2.anchor: وأن تقولوا مفعول له أي فعلنا ذلك من نصب الأدلة الشاهدة على صحتها العقول كراهة أن تقولوا يوم القيامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī identifies the ancestors as Jews who said Ezra was God's son, and their descendants as contemporaries of the Prophet who followed them; the filial-shirk clause supports this reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r3.anchor: عني ببني آدم أسلاف اليهود الذين أشركوا بالله تعالى حيث قالوا: عزير ابن الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r4.claim: He links the passage's Jewish setting to the surrounding passages about the town, a dissenting group, God's warning, the raised mountain, and the man given signs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r4.anchor: والدليل على أنها في اليهود الآيات التي عطفت عليها هي والتي عطفت عليها وهي على نمطها وأسلوبها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says some read the verse as describing a worldly event: God brought people into existence and made them testify when they matured and received understanding and signs of the Creator; he attributes this to al-Zajjāj.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطية: قال قوم الآية مشيرة إلى هذا التأويل الذي في الدنيا وأخذ بمعنى أوجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r6.claim: Taking the hadith literally opens the door to transmigration, so Abū Ḥayyān says it must be interpreted figuratively.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r6.anchor: والقول بظاهر الحديث يطرق إلى القول بالتناسخ فيجب تأويله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r7.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r7.claim: Al-Ḥawfī takes ذريتهم as the direct object of أخذ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r8.claim: Alternatively, أخذ has an understood object, “the covenant”; ذريتهم is apposition to the pronoun in ظهورهم, and من ظهورهم apposition to بني آدم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r8.anchor: ويحتمل في قراءة الجميع أن يكون مفعول أخذ محذوفا لفهم المعنى وذريتهم بدل من ضمير ظهورهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r9.claim: The omitted object can be supplied as a covenant, as in the scriptural expressions “we took from them a solemn covenant” and “we took the covenant of the Children of Israel.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p219/r9.anchor: والمفعول المحذوف هو الميثاق كما قال: وأخذنا منهم ميثاقا غليظا وإذ أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل لا تعبدون إلا الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r1.claim: He reconstructs the sense as God taking from Adam's descendants a covenant of monotheism and exclusive worship; the burden and binding force of a covenant are pictured as weight carried on the back.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r1.anchor: وتقدير الكلام: وإذ أخذ ربك من ظهور ذريات بني آدم ميثاق التوحيد لله وإفراده بالعبادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r2.claim: The testimony is effected through the proofs God set within people, as though He asked whether He was their Lord and they answered yes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r2.anchor: وأشهدهم على أنفسهم بما نصب لهم من الأدلة قائلا ألست بربكم قالوا بلى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r3.speaker: العربيان ونافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r3.claim: The two readers called العربيان and Nāfiʿ read ذرياتهم in the plural; its grammatical analysis was discussed earlier.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r3.anchor: وقرأ العربيان ونافع: ذرياتهم بالجمع وتقدم إعرابه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r4.speaker: باقي السبعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r4.claim: The other seven readers use the singular ذريتهم with fatḥa on tāʾ, parsed as the object of أخذ with an omitted annexation: “the covenant of their descendants.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r4.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة ذريتهم مفردا بفتح التاء ويتعين أن يكون مفعولا بأخذ وهو على حذف مضاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r5.claim: The covenant is attributed to Adam's descendants because Adam's immediate children were not idolaters; shirk arose in later generations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r5.anchor: وإنما كان أخذ الميثاق من ذرية بني آدم لأن بني آدم لصلبه لم يكن فيهم مشرك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r6.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says “we have testified” is God speaking against them, or God together with the angels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r6.anchor: أي قال الله شهدنا عليكم أو قال الله والملائكة قاله السدي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r7.claim: Another reported interpretation makes the angels the speakers of “we have testified.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r7.anchor: شهدنا أن تقولوا يوم القيامة إنا كنا عن هذا غافلين. أي قال الله شهدنا عليكم أو قال الله والملائكة قاله السدي، أو قالت الملائكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r8.claim: A further interpretation is that people testified against one another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r8.anchor: أو شهد بعضهم على بعض أقوال ومعنى عن هذا عن هذا الميثاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r9.claim: In this clause, “about this” means about the covenant and acknowledgment of God's lordship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r9.anchor: ومعنى عن هذا عن هذا الميثاق والإقرار بالربوبية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r10.claim: The testimony forecloses two excuses: being unaware of the covenant and merely following idolatrous forefathers; otherwise, people could claim they had no messenger or pledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p220/r10.anchor: لكانت لهم حجتان إحداهما: كنا غافلين والأخرى: كنا أتباعا لأسلافنا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r1.claim: The verse is attached to the preceding passage by an implied verb and binds Jews through a universal covenant, after their particular covenant and scriptural and rational arguments against imitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r1.anchor: وهو معطوف على ما قبل مسوق لإلزام اليهود بمقتضى الميثاق العام

ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r2.claim: Some read the verse as a generalizing conclusion after the specific covenant at the mountain, showing the Jews' continuing transgression; Alusi says this is more apparent from the wording, especially if the general group is restricted to polytheists.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r2.anchor: وبعضهم جوز أن يكون تذييلا تعميما بعد التخصيص وإظهارا لتمادي هؤلاء اليهود في الغي

ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r3.claim: Another view takes the verse to establish a pre-world covenant with all humanity, the foundational basis of obligations, without coercion, and an answer to contemporary polytheists' excuses.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r3.anchor: إن الآية مسوقة لبيان أخذ ميثاق سابق من جميع الخلق مؤمنهم وكافرهم قبل هذه النشأة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r4.claim: The passage's placement among verses about Jews may be a digression linked by subject, but Alusi follows the majority of later exegetes in taking it as a universal covenant addressed to people generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r4.anchor: لكن الأول وهو الذي جرى عليه أكثر متأخري المفسرين أي واذكر لهم أو للناس إذ أخذ ربك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r5.claim: “Children of Adam” means all people born generation after generation, believers and unbelievers, except those never born; Alusi rejects restricting it to Jewish ancestors who called Ezra God's son.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r5.anchor: المراد بهم الذين ولد لهم مؤمنين كانوا أو كفارا نسلا بعد نسل سوى من لم يولد له بسبب من الأسباب

ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r6.claim: Using “took” rather than “brought out” dignifies the covenant and its recipients, signals selection, supports the later question, and suits the language of covenant; “Lord” recalls the effects of lordship.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r6.anchor: وإيثار الأخذ على الإخراج للإيذان بشأن المأخوذ إذ ذاك لما فيه من الأنباء عن الاجتباء والاصطفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r7.claim: Some infer from the change of style around this verse that it is a digression; Alusi notes the different wording from the mountain-covenant passage and the following account of the man given signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r7.anchor: واستأنس بعضهم بمغايرة أسلوب هذا الكلام بما فيه من الالتفات لما قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r8.claim: “From their backs” is parsed as a partitive apposition to “Children of Adam” through repetition of the preposition; Abu al-Baqa instead treats it as an apposition of inclusion.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r8.anchor: من ظهورهم ) بدل من بني آدم بدل البعض من الكل بتكرير الجار

ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r9.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r9.claim: Abu al-Baqa's inclusion-apposition analysis relates taking the descendants from the backs to taking Adam's descendants through their bodies and members; Alusi questions its rationale and prefers the partitive analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r9.anchor: وإليه ذهب أبو البقاء وبينه بعضهم بأن بدل الاشتمال ما يكون بينه وبين المبدل منه ملابسة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r10.claim: Both occurrences of “from” indicate origin, further clarify the phrase by moving from general to specific, and may suggest the covenant was taken while people remained in their fathers' loins.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r10.anchor: في الموضعين ابتدائية وفيه مزيد تقرير لابتنائه على البيان

ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r11.claim: The object “their descendants” is delayed because it contains a pronoun referring back to the object and because delaying it preserves its primacy and creates anticipation.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r11.anchor: ذريتهم ( مفعول ( أخذ ) أخر عن المفعول بواسطة الجار

ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r12.speaker: نافع وأبو عمر وابن عامر ويعقوب
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r12.claim: These readers recite the word as a plural; it means their children generally, while interpreters who restrict the verse to Jewish ancestors restrict it to their descendants, a limitation Alusi rejects.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمر وابن عامر ويعقوب ( ذرياتهم ) والمراد أولادهم على العموم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r13.claim: The objection that all people are both Children of Adam and their descendants is resolved by taking the verse as the ordered emergence of branches from roots through birth; no restriction to Jews is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p99#2/r13.anchor: والإشكال المشهور هو أن كل الناس يصدق عليه بنو آدم وذريته فيتحد المخرج والمخرج منه مدفوع بظهور أن المراد إخراج الفروع من الأصول

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r1.claim: Each descendant was made witness against himself, establishing God's complete lordship over him.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r1.anchor: أشهد كل واحد من أولئك الذرية المأخوذين من ظهور آبائهم على أنفسهم لا على غيرهم تقريرا لهم بربوبيته سبحانه وتعالى التامة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r2.claim: The question calls God their unrestricted master and nurturer, with no one else involved in their affairs.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r2.anchor: أي مالك أمركم ومربيكم على الإطلاق من غير أن يكون لأحد مدخل في شأن من شؤنكم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r3.claim: Their answer means they acknowledged God as their Lord and no one else as lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r3.anchor: أي على أنفسنا بأنك ربنا لا رب لنا غيرك والمراد أقررنا بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r4.speaker: القاضي شريح
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r4.claim: Shurayḥ invoked a relative's testimony when addressing a confessor.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r4.anchor: أن القاضي شريح قال لمقر عنده شهد عليك ابن أخت خالتك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r5.speaker: الجلال السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r5.claim: Al-Suyūṭī treats the verse as a basis for legal acknowledgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r5.anchor: ومن هنا قال الجلال السيوطي : إن هذه الآية أصل في الإقرار

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r6.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r6.claim: Most grammarians consider the alif in بلى original; بلى answers negation and cancels it, including a negative question used for confirmation.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r6.anchor: وتختص بالنفي فلا تقع إلا في جوابه فتفيد إبطاله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r7.speaker: جمع
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r7.claim: Another grammatical account derives بلى from بل and treats its alif as added.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r7.anchor: وقال جمع : الأصل بل والألف زائدة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r8.speaker: بعض أولئك
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r8.claim: Some grammarians treat the alif as a feminine ending, or otherwise as an augmentative letter.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r8.anchor: إنها لتأنيث الكلمة كالتاء في ثمت وربت لأنها أميلت

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r9.speaker: جماعة من الفقهاء
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r9.claim: Jurists disagree whether answering بلى or نعم to a creditor's negative question establishes the debt; some distinguish them, others follow customary usage for both.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r9.anchor: قال جماعة من الفقهاء : لو قال أليس لي عليك ألف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r10.speaker: الرضي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r10.claim: Al-Raḍī records disagreement over whether بلى may answer a plain affirmative, with some allowing it on the basis of a cited poem.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r10.anchor: فقد حكي الرضي الخلاف فيه وذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r11.speaker: السهيلي وجماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r11.claim: They dispute Ibn ʿAbbās's claim that نعم would be disbelief, arguing a confirmatory question is affirmative and can be affirmed with نعم.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r11.anchor: ونازع السهيلي وجماعة في المحكي عن الحبر وغيره متمسكين بأن الاستفهام التقريري موجب

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r12.speaker: ابن هشام
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r12.claim: Ibn Hishām objects that بلى cannot answer an affirmative statement, though the discussion cites Prophetic questions answered with بلى.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r12.anchor: قال ابن هشام : ويشكل عليهم أن بلى لا يجاب بها الإيجاب وذلك متفق عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r13.claim: Reports in al-Bukhārī and Muslim use بلى after bare questions, but the opposing grammarians say such rare usage cannot establish Qurʾānic usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r13.anchor: ففي صحيح البخاري أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال لأصحابه : أترضون أن تكونوا ربع أهل الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r14.speaker: البدر الدماميني
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r14.claim: Al-Damāmīnī resolves the dispute by distinguishing an answer to the negative wording from one affirming the whole proposition, including its interrogative force.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101/r14.anchor: أجاب البدر الدماميني بأنه لا إشكال في الحقيقة فإن هؤلاء راعوا صورة النفي المنطوق به

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the poem using بلى after a plain affirmative is anomalous, as al-Raḍī had noted.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r1.anchor: ولا يخفى أن البيت شاذ كما صرح به الرضي

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r2.speaker: الشلوبين
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r2.claim: When a negative is preceded by a real question, answer as to bare negation; with a confirmatory question, most follow its wording, while in an unambiguous case one may follow its sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r2.anchor: إن كان على حقيقته فجوابه كجواب النفي المجرد وإن كان مرادا به التقرير فالأكثر أن يجاب بما يجلب به النفي

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r3.speaker: ابن عصفور
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṣfūr says replies to confirmatory questions follow the surface negation to avoid ambiguity about whether نعم affirms wording or intended meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r3.anchor: أجرت العرب التقرير في الجواب مجرى النفي المحض وإن كان إيجابا في المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers reading نعم in Jaḥdar's poem as answering the immediately preceding statement about their meeting.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r4.anchor: والأحسن أن تكون نعم في البيت جوابا لقوله : فذاك بنا تدانى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r5.speaker: ابن هشام
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r5.claim: Ibn Hishām concludes that نعم would not adequately confess to ألست بربكم, since it could follow either the spoken negation or the intended affirmation.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r5.anchor: ثم قال ابن هشام : ويتحرر على هذا أنه لو أجيب ( ألست بربكم ) بنعم لم يكف في الإقرار

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r6.speaker: ابن هشام
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r6.claim: He compares this ambiguity with saying لا إله إلا الله using nominative إله, which may deny unity rather than other gods.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r6.anchor: ولهذا لا يدخل في الإسلام بقوله لا إله إلا الله برفع إله لاحتماله لنفي الوحدة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī suggests Ibn ʿAbbās meant نعم would fail to give an unambiguous, sufficient confession of lordship.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r7.anchor: ولعل ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما إنما قال : إنهم لو قالوا : نعم لم يكن إقرارا وافيا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r8.speaker: الشلوِيّين
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the interpretation that Ibn ʿAbbās meant نعم would amount to disbelief, since takfīr cannot rest on ambiguity.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r8.anchor: وفيه نظر لأن التكفير لا يكون بالاحتمال

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r9.speaker: جمع
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r9.claim: Some interpreters take the exchange as a figurative portrayal of humanity's primordial readiness to infer God's oneness from cosmic and inward signs, as in the fitra report.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r9.anchor: والكلام عند جمع تمثيل لخلقه تعالى الخلق جميعا في مبدأ الفطرة مستعدين للاستدلاال بالأدلة الآفاقية والأنفسية المؤدية إلى التوحيد

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r10.claim: The figurative reading compares God's enabling recognition and humanity's ready response to the address to heaven and earth, and to speech attributed to animals and inanimate things.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r10.anchor: في قوله سبحانه وتعالى : ( فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين )

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r11.claim: On this reading, أن تقولوا shifts address from the Prophet to contemporary Jews, or to them and their predecessors collectively; it gives the purpose of the taking and witnessing, or an implied act.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r11.anchor: وجعلوا قوله سبحانه وتعالى : ( ( أن تقولوا ( من تلوين الخطاب وصرفه عن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إلى معاصريه من اليهود

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r12.speaker: البصريون
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r12.claim: The Basran construal supplies فعلنا ما فعلنا كراهة أن تقولوا, while the Kufan construal understands لئلا تقولوا.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r12.anchor: والمعنى على ما يقول البصريون : فعلنا ما فعلنا كراهة أن تقولوا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r13.claim: The threatened excuse would be that they were unaware of the oneness of God's lordship when judgment reveals the truth and punishment surrounds the idolaters.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p101#2/r13.anchor: بمن أشرك ( إنا كنا عن هذا ( أي وحدانية الربوبية غافلين

ALUSI-FULL:v9p102/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p102/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p102/r1.claim: They cannot plead ignorance because the signs alerted them and prepared them fully to recognize the truth; denying this is obstinacy.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p102/r1.anchor: لأنهم نبهوا بنصب الأدلة وجعلوا متهيئين تهيأ تاما لتحقيق الحق وإنكار ذلك مكابرة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī says al-Bayḍāwī's distinction between extraction from Adam by hadith and from his descendants by the verse does not fit the hadith's context.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r1.anchor: من آدم بالحديث ومن بنيه بالآية لايطابق سياق الحديث كما لا يخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r2.speaker: شهاب الدين التوربشتي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r2.claim: Al-Turbushtī argues that a literal covenant leaves people able to plead that their compelled or divinely protected acknowledgment did not continue; therefore the covenant must mean the reason and insight God implanted in them.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r2.anchor: فقالوا : إن كان هذا الإقرار عن اضطرار حيث كوشفوا بحقيقة الأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī answers that those pleading lost certainty would be called liars and reminded that successive messengers woke them from heedlessness.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r3.anchor: إذا قالوا شهدنا يومئذ فلما زال علم الضرورة ووكلنا إلى آرائنا كان كذا أيها الكذابون متى وكلتم إلى آرائكم ألم نرسل رسلنا تترا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r4.claim: He adds that the alternative appeal to intellect and insight faces the same objection: people could ask what benefit these faculties gave if divine guidance was withheld.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r4.anchor: فإذا حرمنا اللطف والتوفيق فأي منفعة لنا في العقل والبصيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r5.speaker: محيي السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r5.claim: Muḥyī al-Sunna answers that clear signs and truthful messengers make deniers obstinate covenant-breakers, and that forgetting the covenant cannot invalidate proof conveyed by a truthful informant.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r5.anchor: إن الله تعالى قد أوضح الدلائل على وحدانيته وصدق رسله فيما أخبروا به فمن أنكره كان معاندا ناقضا للعهد

ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds a flaw in Muḥyī al-Sunna's answer that people are bound by a covenant no one remembers.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r7.claim: One grammatical solution attaches أن تقولوا to an implied act of recalling and explaining the covenant, or to an implied command to mention it, rather than to the witnessing itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r7.anchor: بأن قوله تعالى : ( أن تقولوا ) الخ ليس مفعولا له لقوله تعالى : ( وأشهدهم )

ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r8.claim: For the other reading, the clause can be a purpose for an implied command to recall the earlier covenant, preventing excuses of ignorance or imitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r8.anchor: أما على القراءة الأخرى فهو مفعول له لنفس الأمر المضمر العامل في ( إذ أخذ )

ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r9.claim: If شهدنا is God's speech rather than the descendants', God is the subject of أن تقولوا and will deny their later excuse, removing the problem.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p104#2/r9.anchor: فأما على تقدير كونه من كلام الله تعالى فهو العامل في ( أن تقولوا ) ولا محذور أصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds the implied-verb solution elegant, but says the apparent syntax still attaches the purpose clause to the witnessing and its consequences.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r1.anchor: إلا أن الظاهر تعلقه بالإشهاد وما يتفرع عليه وأرى الجواب مع عدم العدول عنه لا يخلو عن العدول عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r2.claim: A report transmitted through Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, and other Companions places the covenant before Adam's descent: God extracts bright and dark progeny, assigns their destinations, then takes their pledge; God and angels testify.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r2.anchor: من طريق السدي عن أبي مالك وعن أبي صالح

ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r3.claim: This report conflicts with the earlier Ibn ʿAbbās report, which locates the covenant at Nuʿmān and appears to place it after Adam's descent.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r3.anchor: وفيه مخالفة لما روي عن الحبر أولا من أن الأخذ كان بنعمان إذ هو ظاهر في كون ذلك بعد الهبوط

ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r4.speaker: رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r4.claim: An Abū Umāma report places the covenant while God's Throne was over the water: both groups answer God's call and affirmation, and then are mixed together.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r4.anchor: عن أبي أمامة أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال :

ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r5.speaker: بعضهم وآخرون
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r5.claim: Other reports locate the event in India or at the Kaʿba, where Adam's particle-like descendants encircled him; al-Ālūsī says these locations lack a dependable basis.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r5.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أنه كان بالهند حيث هبط آدم عليه السلام وآخرون أنه كان في موضع الكعبة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r6.speaker: السادة الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r6.claim: The Sufi masters reconcile conflicting reports by proposing multiple covenant-taking events, though al-Ālūsī says their language suggests different kinds of covenant.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105/r6.anchor: إلا أن يقال بتعدد أخذ الميثاق وإليه ذهب السادة الصوفية قدس الله تعالى أسرارهم لكن يشعر كلامهم باختلاف النوع

ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r1.claim: Some people recall six covenantal stations before the Alastu covenant; a teacher accepts this if they mean universal categories, and Dhū al-Nūn says the covenant is as if still in his ear.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : رأيت من يستحضر قبل ميثاق ( ألست ) ستة مواطن أخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r2.claim: Thus the claim that nobody remembers the covenant is too broad; it may mean that no idolater remembers it.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r2.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال مراده من تلك السالبة لا أحد من المشركين يذكر ذلك الميثاق لا لا أحد مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r3.speaker: قطب الحق والدين العلامة الشيرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r3.claim: Al-Shīrāzī reconciles the verse and Umar report as a wise redirection: the Prophet was asked about the present, rational covenant but answered by revealing a primordial verbal covenant.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r3.anchor: وحاصله : أن جواب النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إذ سئل عن الآية من قبيل أسلوب الحكيم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r4.speaker: قطب الحق والدين العلامة الشيرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r4.claim: He distinguishes a present, rationally recognized covenant through signs from a verbal primordial covenant known through prophetic revelation; historical descendants are the same progeny extracted from Adam.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r4.anchor: أن سبحانه كان له ميثاقان مع بني آدم أحدهما تهتدي إليه العقول من نصب الأدلة الباعثة على الاعتراف الحالي

ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls this reconciliation good, but says eternity and futurity must be figurative: reproduction ends at the Resurrection, and created events cannot be eternal without contradicting Muslim consensus and doctrine.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r5.anchor: وهو حسن كما قالوا لكن ينبغي أن يحمل الأزل فيه ولا يزال على المجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r6.speaker: الخلخالي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r6.claim: Al-Khalakhālī says the interlocutors are eternal intelligible forms or fixed entities, whose replies are spoken through their primordial capacities rather than post-creation tongues.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r6.anchor: المخاطبون هم الصور العلمية القديمة التي هي ماهيات الأشياء وحقائقها ويسمونها الأعيان الثابتة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī says al-Khalakhālī's proposal rests on distinguishing subsistence from existence, a distinction he accepts despite its long dispute.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r7.anchor: وهو مبني على الفرق بين الثبوت والوجود وفيه نزاع طويل لكنا ممن يقول به

ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r8.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r8.claim: Another scholar identifies the extracted progeny with intellectual forms and fixed entities, and understands extraction and dialogue as divine manifestation and present potential readiness.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p105#2/r8.anchor: أن المراد بالذرية المستخرجة من صلب آدم عليه السلام وبنيه هو الصور العلمية والأعيان الثابتة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r1.speaker: الشيخ العارف أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r1.claim: Al-Sulamī transmits from Banān that God made the souls present in pre-eternity, summoned and taught them before human form, then created them and placed them in Adam's loins.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r1.anchor: الشيخ العارف أبو عبدالرحمن السلمي في الحقائق عن بنان حيث قال :

ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī says this reconciliation is far from the outward sense because it conflicts with apparent reports, and applying it to all people, both blessed and wretched, is difficult.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r2.anchor: ولا يخفى أن هذا التوفيق بعيد بمراحل عن ذوق أرباب الظاهر لمخالفته لظواهر الأخبار والمتبادر من الآثار

ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r3.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r3.claim: Ibn ʿArabī depicts the exchange as an echo: created existence is an erected fantasy, and the witnessing is mercy because God did not say “alone,” knowing people would associate partners through natural desire and receptivity to divine power.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r3.anchor: وذكر الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره أن الله تعالى أبدع المبدعات وتجلى بلسان الأحدية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects that leading exegetes and reports affirm God's exclusive oneness in both the question and the testimony.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r4.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن محققي المفسرين اعتبروا الوحدانية في الإشهاد وكذا في الشهادة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r5.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reports that all souls were gathered in forms, pledged that God alone is Lord and deity, and were warned that messengers and scriptures would remind them; Adam saw their differing conditions and asked why they were unequal, and God said He loved to be thanked.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p106/r5.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب أنه قال في الآية : جمعهم جميعا فجعلهم أرواحا في صورهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p297#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p297#2/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب عن النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p297#2/r7.claim: The Prophet said God first drew from Adam’s back descendants destined for Paradise and its deeds, then descendants destined for Fire and its deeds; a person is put to work in the deeds of the destiny assigned to him until death and recompense.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p297#2/r7.anchor: عن مسلم بن يسار الجهني أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه سئل عن هذه الآية: {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p297#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p297#2/r8.speaker: أبو عيسى
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p297#2/r8.claim: Abū ʿĪsā grades the report ḥasan, while noting that Muslim ibn Yasār did not hear from ʿUmar and that some include an intermediary.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p297#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو عيسى: هذا حديث حسن. ومسلم بن يسار لم يسمع من عمر، وقد ذكر بعضهم في هذا الإسناد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r1.speaker: مقاتل وغيره من أهل التفسير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r1.claim: They report that God drew white and black ant-like descendants from Adam’s right and left back, assigned them respectively to Paradise and Fire, and returned them to his loins until each was born from human parents.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل وغيره من أهل التفسير: إن الله مسح صفحة ظهر آدم اليمنى فأخرج منه ذرية بيضاء كهيئة الذر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r2.claim: Those who broke the first covenant are linked to the statement that God found most people without a covenant.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r2.anchor: قال الله تعالى فيمن نقض العهد الأول: "وما وجدنا لأكثرهم من عهد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r3.speaker: بعض أهل التفسير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r3.claim: Some exegetes say the blessed affirmed freely, while the wretched affirmed under compulsion; this is the sense of submission both willingly and unwillingly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r3.anchor: وقال بعض أهل التفسير: إن أهل السعادة أقروا طوعا وقالوا: بلى، وأهل الشقاوة قالوه تقية وكرها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās places the covenant at Wādī Nuʿmān, near ʿArafāt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r4.anchor:
قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: ببطن نعمان -واد إلا جنب
عرفة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r5.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās locates it at Dahnāʾ in India, where Adam descended.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r5.anchor:
قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: ببطن نعمان -واد إلا جنب
عرفة - (1) وروي عنه أيضا: أنه بدهناء من أرض الهند

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r6.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r6.claim: Al-Kalbī locates the covenant between Mecca and Ṭāʾif.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r7.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r7.claim: Al-Suddī says God brought Adam out of Paradise, before his descent from heaven, then stroked his back and extracted his descendants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r7.anchor: وقال السدي: أخرج الله آدم عليه السلام من الجنة فلم يهبط من السماء ثم مسح ظهره فأخرج ذريته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r8.claim: An unattributed report says God formed all descendants like ants, gave them understanding and speech, and addressed them face to face.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r8.anchor: وروي: أن الله أخرجهم جميعا وصورهم وجعل لهم عقولا يعلمون بها وألسنا ينطقون بها ثم كلمهم قبلا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r9.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj says it is possible that God gave ant-like beings understanding, as in the verse where an ant speaks to other ants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r9.anchor: وقال الزجاج وجائز أن يكون الله تعالى جعل لأمثال الذر فهما تعقل به، كما قال تعالى: "قالت نملة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r10.claim: Another report says God declared His oneness, warned them against association, promised messengers and revealed Books, received their testimony and covenants, recorded their lifespans, provisions, and afflictions, then returned them to Adam’s loins.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r10.anchor: وروي أن الله تعالى قال لهم جميعا: اعملوا أنه لا إله غيري وأنا ربكم لا رب لكم غيري فلا تشركوا بي شيئا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r11.claim: In the same report Adam saw differences in wealth and appearance and asked why they were not made equal; God replied that He loves to be thanked.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r11.anchor: فنظر إليهم آدم فرأى منهم الغني والفقير وحسن الصورة ودون ذلك، فقال: رب لولا سويت بينهم؟ قال: إني أحب أن أشكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r12.claim: The phrase means that God took descendants from the backs of Adam’s descendants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r12.anchor: فذلك قوله تعالى: "وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم" أي: من ظهور بني آدم ذريتهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r13.speaker: أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r13.claim: They read dhurriyyātihim in the plural with kasra on the tāʾ; the others read dhurriyyatahum in the singular with fatḥa on the tāʾ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p298/r13.anchor:
قرأ أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو وابن عامر: "ذرياتهم" 
بالجمع وكسر التاء، وقرأ الآخرون "ذريتهم" على التوحيد، ونصب التاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r1.claim: Although the verse says ‘from their backs,’ God drew each generation from the backs of the preceding generation, as children descend from fathers; mentioning Adam’s back is unnecessary because all are known to be his children and to have come from his back.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r1.anchor: قيل: إن الله أخرج ذرية آدم بعضهم من ذرية آدم بعضهم من ظهور بعض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r2.claim: ‘He made them bear witness concerning themselves’ means that He made some testify against others.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r2.anchor: وأشهدهم على أنفسهم ألست بربكم قالوا بلى} أي: أشهد بعضهم على بعض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads both ‘that they say’ and the following ‘and they say’ with yāʾ, in the third person; the others use tāʾ in both.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r3.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو: "أن يقولوا" ويقولوا بالياء فيهما، وقرأ الآخرون بالتاء فيهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r4.speaker: السدي
