BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says ‘We testified’ reports that God and His angels bore witness to the descendants’ acknowledgment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r4.anchor: قال السدي: هو خبر من الله عن نفسه وملائكته أنهم شهدوا على إقرار بني آدم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r5.claim: Another view takes ‘We testified’ as the descendants’ own answer after God made them witness against one another.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي: ذلك من قول الملائكة، وفيه حذف تقديره: لما قالت الذرية: بلى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r6.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r6.claim: Al-Kalbī says the angels speak: after the descendants say ‘Yes,’ God tells the angels to witness, and they say ‘We testified’; an omitted clause is understood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r6.anchor: وقال الكلبي: ذلك من قول الملائكة، وفيه حذف تقديره: لما قالت الذرية: بلى قال الله للملائكة: اشهدوا، قالوا: شهدنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r7.claim: The purpose clause means ‘so that you would not say’ or ‘lest you say’ on the Resurrection Day that you were unaware of the covenant and acknowledgment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r7.anchor: أن يقولوا" يعني: وأشهدهم على أنفسهم أن يقولوا، أي: لئلا يقولوا أو كراهية أن يقولوا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r8.claim: With the second-person reading, God addresses them directly with ‘Am I not your Lord?’ so they cannot claim on Judgment Day to have been unaware.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r8.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتاء فتقدير الكلام: أخاطبكم: ألست بربكم لئلا تقولوا: {يوم القيامة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r9.claim: Though people may not remember the covenant, God has made proofs of His oneness and messengers’ truth clear; rejecting them is defiant covenant-breaking, and forgetting does not cancel the proof once a truthful messenger with a miracle informs them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p299/r9.anchor: فإن قيل: كيف تلزم الحجة على أحد لا يذكر الميثاق؟ قيل: قد أوضح الله الدلائل على وحدانيته وصدق رسله

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:171-172/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:171-172/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:171-172/r10.claim: God brought Adam's descendants from their forefathers' loins, generation after generation; from their backs is a partitive apposition to children of Adam.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:171-172/r10.anchor: أخرج من أصلابهم نسلهم على ما يتوالدون قرنا بعد قرن

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:171-172/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:171-172/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:171-172/r11.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Yaʿqūb read ذرياتهم in the plural form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:171-172/r11.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر ويعقوب «ذرياتهم»

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:171-172/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:171-172/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:171-172/r12.claim: God furnished proofs of His lordship and reason with capacities to recognize them, making their potential knowledge and acknowledgment like a direct testimony; this is figurative representation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:171-172/r12.anchor: ونصب لهم دلائل ربوبيته وركب في عقولهم ما يدعوهم إلى الاقرار بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:172-173/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:172-173/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:172-173/r1.claim: Their excuse that they were heedless means they had not been alerted by evidence.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:172-173/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:172-173/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:172-173/r6.claim: A reported account says God drew Adam's descendants out like specks, gave them life, reason, and speech, and inspired their acknowledgment; it is associated with a report from ʿUmar.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:172-173/r6.anchor: وقيل لما خلق الله آدم أخرج من ظهره ذرية كالذر وأحياهم

SULAMI:v1p247#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r1.claim: Abu Sa'id al-Kharraz says believers encountered God in tranquility, recognized Him, and became calm, while unbelievers encountered overwhelming majesty, lost their reason, and scattered from Him.
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r1.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الخراز في هذه الآية قال : تراءى لأهل الإيمان بالسكون فعرفوه وسكنوا واطمانوا

SULAMI:v1p247#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r2.speaker: يوسف
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r2.claim: Yusuf says God addressed them while they existed only through His bringing them into being; they apprehended the Real independently of their own existence, in a way known and found only by Him.
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r2.anchor: وقال يوسف في هذه الآية : قد أخبر أنه خاطبهم ربهم وهم غير موجودين إلا بايجاده لهم

SULAMI:v1p247#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r3.claim: Some say the primordial response began without direct witnessing; after unveiling, they witnessed the realities addressed to them and said, 'We bear witness.'
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم في قوله : ﴿ ألست بربكم قالوا بلى ﴾ من غير مشاهدة ، ثم كوشفوا فشهدوا ما خوطبوا به

SULAMI:v1p247#5/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r4.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r4.claim: Al-Husayn says the particles spoke faith willingly and under compulsion; after God showed them His reality, divine power spoke for them without their participation.
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r4.anchor: وقال الحسين : انطق الذر بالإيمان طوعا . وكرها أنطقتهم بركة الآخذ أحدهم عنهم

SULAMI:v1p247#5/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r5.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r5.claim: A special form of tawhid is for the servant's secret to stand before God while His governance and decrees carry him through unity, effacing the self as the Real sustains him.
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r5.anchor: وقيل : إن توحيد الخاص أن يكون العبد قائما بسره بين يدي ربه ، يجري عليه تصاريف تدبيره

SULAMI:v1p247#5/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r6.speaker: النصر آباذي
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r6.claim: Al-Nasrabadi contrasts an earlier primordial taking with a later appointed taking through lineages, embryos, and clots; the passage's wording is difficult, so the relation is uncertain.
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r6.anchor: قال النصر آباذي رحمه الله في هذه الآية : مؤيل الأكبر ومالف الأعظم ، معافون من السلالة والطين

SULAMI:v1p247#5/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r7.speaker: النصر آباذي
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r7.claim: Al-Nasrabadi says God's taking is not merely tenderness and generosity but majesty, greatness, independence, and self-sufficiency.
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r7.anchor: وقال النصر آباذي : أخذ ربك تلطفا وتكرما بل أخذه جلالة وعظمة ، بل أخذه غنى واستغناء

SULAMI:v1p247#5/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r8.speaker: النصر آباذي
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r8.claim: Al-Nasrabadi says the taking was for proof rather than need, and God kept creatures from seeing even a particle of the proof's meanings.
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r8.anchor: وقال النصر آباذي : أخذ ربك تلطفا وتكرما بل أخذه جلالة وعظمة ، بل أخذه غنى واستغناء . وقال أيضا : أخذ لا للحاجة بل للحجة

SULAMI:v1p247#5/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r9.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r9.claim: Abu Uthman al-Maghribi defines creatures as forms on which the decrees of divine power operate, and describes God's taking as moving them from one source or substance to another.
SULAMI:v1p247#5/r9.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان المغربي : وسئل عنه ما الخلق ؟ قال : قوالب تجري عليها أحكام القدرة ، وقال : أخذ ربك من معدن إلى معدن ومن معدن للمعدن

SULAMI:v1p248/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p248/r1.speaker: الجريري
SULAMI:v1p248/r1.claim: Al-Jariri says God made Himself known to each group through the knowledge He bestowed, and each affirmed Him; the cited verses say God, not human effort, united hearts.
SULAMI:v1p248/r1.anchor: وقال الجريري في قوله : ﴿ ألست بربكم ﴾ قال : تعرف إلى كل طائفة من الطوائف بما منحها من معرفته

SULAMI:v1p248/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p248/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
SULAMI:v1p248/r2.claim: Al-Kharraz says only divine power, effective decree, and complete will could have answered; the people were merely traces of the Sovereign's decrees, as they remain forms under His governance.
SULAMI:v1p248/r2.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الخراز في قوله ' بلى ' قال : من قال حين قال : من أين أجابوا عنهم إلا القدرة والنافذة والمشيئة التامة

SULAMI:v1p248/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p248/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p248/r3.claim: Some call the primordial address a matter of power set forth in the very eye of nonexistence.
SULAMI:v1p248/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : خطب منصوب القدرة في عين العدم

SULAMI:v1p248/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p248/r4.speaker: ابن بنان
SULAMI:v1p248/r4.claim: Ibn Bannan says God addressed them while they existed only by His bringing them into being, in a divine mode of existence and perception that belongs to Him alone; he clarifies that they existed in God's power while absent from witnessing existence and unity.
SULAMI:v1p248/r4.anchor: قال ابن بنان في هذه الآية : قد أخبرك أنه قد خاطبهم وهم غير موجودين إلا بوجوده لهم

SULAMI:v1p248/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p248/r5.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p248/r5.claim: Some say their answer accorded with surrender and was a station of annihilation; the world remains under divine subjection in the grip of the Real.
SULAMI:v1p248/r5.anchor: قيل : إنما أجيب عنهم على حسب الاستسلام فهذا مقام الفناء

SULAMI:v1p248/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p248/r6.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v1p248/r6.claim: Al-Husayn says even the nearest angels do not know how creation began or ends; since no created sense had perceived the event, God Himself was both questioner and respondent.
SULAMI:v1p248/r6.anchor: قال الحسين : لا يعلم أحد من الملائكة المقربين ما أظهر الخلق وكيف الانتهاء والابتداء

SULAMI:v1p248/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p248/r7.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v1p248/r7.claim: Al-Husayn interprets 'Yes' as spoken by someone other than the hearers and answered by someone other than them: they vanished, while the One who always was remained.
SULAMI:v1p248/r7.anchor: وقال الحسين في قوله : ' بلى ' : القائل عنكم سواكم والمجيب غيركم

SULAMI:v1p248/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p248/r8.speaker: علي بن عبد الرحيم
SULAMI:v1p248/r8.claim: Ali ibn Abd al-Rahim says they existed in divine power while hidden from witnessing existence.
SULAMI:v1p248/r8.anchor: وسئل علي بن عبد الرحيم عن قوله : ﴿ وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ﴾ قال : كانوا موجودين في القدرة

SULAMI:v1p249/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p249/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p249/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti reads 'Am I not your Lord?' followed by 'Yes' as an affirmation cast in the form of a question.
SULAMI:v1p249/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه في قوله : ﴿ ألست بربكم ﴾ قالوا بلى : ' قال : هو تقرير في صورة السؤال

SULAMI:v1p249/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p249/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p249/r2.claim: Some say divine power itself answered the question of divine power.

SULAMI:v1p249/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p249/r3.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p249/r3.claim: Some say they heard God's speech that nothing resembles Him, received life from that light, and were sustained by that word; a poem says hearers would fall prostrate before its might.
SULAMI:v1p249/r3.anchor: وقيل في قوله : ' بلى ' قالوا : سمعوا كلامه أن ^ ( ليس كمثله شيء ) ^ وخلق حياتهم من ذلك النور

SULAMI:v1p249/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p249/r4.speaker: ابن بنان
SULAMI:v1p249/r4.claim: Ibn Bannan says God selected a pure elect for guardianship and honor, giving them worldly bodies, luminous spirits, spiritual minds, and unseen abodes; He called them in pre-eternity and they answered, then brought them into Adam's loins by His will, so their existence and response depended on Him.
SULAMI:v1p249/r4.anchor: قال ابن بنان : لله خالصة من خلقه ، انتخبهم للولاية واستخلصهم للكرامة وأفردهم به له ، فجعل أجسادهم دنياوية وأرواحهم نورانية

BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r6.claim: The covenant theme expands to all humanity: reason and clear signs make God's unity evident, yet in mercy God delayed accountability until sending messengers with books and further explanations; greater knowledge brings greater blame.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r6.anchor: في عموم هذا النوع الآدمي من العقول ونصب من الأدلة الوضحة للأمر إيضاح المشهود للشاهد

BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r7.claim: The wording emphasizes strong covenants: descendants are taken from the stronger human kind, males, and from the strongest bodily part, each father's back; their constitution gives capacity to obey, so the command is within ability.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r7.anchor: ذكر أخذ الذرية من أقوى نوعي الآدمي , وهمالذكور فقال : { من بني آدم } وذكر أنه من أمتن الأعضاء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r8.claim: God's making people witnesses means presenting proofs through their intellect, the heavens and earth, and messengers supported by miracles, which testify that He alone is Lord.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r8.anchor: ومن إرسال الرسل المؤيدين بالمعجزات ما كانوا كالشهود بأنه لا رب غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r9.speaker: الإمام حجة الإسلام الغزالي
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r9.claim: Al-Ghazālī explains the verse as the souls' assent rather than a spoken response: souls are naturally disposed to recognize realities and, on recognizing God's oneness, lordship, and mercy, are moved by fear and hope to obey.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r9.anchor: الإمام حجة الإسلام الغزالي في الكلام على العقل من باب العلم من الإحياء فإنه قال معنى هذه الآية : والمراد إقرار نفوسهم , لا إقرار الألسنة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r10.claim: The answer 'yes, we bear witness' is witnessed knowledge: after the proofs they reached a point where no other answer was possible, as though they had uttered it.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p147/r10.anchor: قالوا بلى شهدنا } أي كان علما شهوديا , وذلك لأنهم وصلوا بعد البيان إلى حد لا يكون فيه الجواب إلا ذلك فكأنهم قالوه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r1.claim: The verses about all creatures submitting to God (13:15 and 16:49) illustrate the prior testimony: the scene is representation, making the ability to infer like actual witnessing.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r1.anchor: ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r2.claim: The purpose of this testimony is to prevent people pleading at Judgment that they lacked evidence of God's unity or merely followed their idolatrous ancestors without a messenger to alert them.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r2.anchor: فعلة كراهة { أن يقولوا يوم القيامة } أي إن لم ينصب لهم الأدلة { إنا كنا هن هذا }

BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r4.speaker: أنس
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r4.claim: Anas's report in the Ṣaḥīḥ says that the least-punished person in Hell would ransom himself with all earthly possessions, but God had asked him in Adam's loins for the easier act of avoiding association and he refused.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r4.anchor: حديث أنس في الصحيح ( يقول الله لأهون أهل النار عذابا : لو أن لك ما في الأرض من شيء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r5.claim: The author takes the covenant in Adam's loins as the installation of evidence and presentation of truth in a form enabling sound reasoning, which explains why mention of ancestral imitation conflicts with a literal spoken pledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r5.anchor: والأخذ وهو في الصلب إنما هو بنصب الأدلة وتقرير الحق على و جه مهيئ للاستدلال بتركيب العقل

BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r6.claim: This interpretation does not contradict reports of an actual address in the realm of atoms, if those reports are sound; the author cites many routes and names Companions and Successors who transmitted them.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r6.anchor: وهذا الذي وقع تأويل الآية به لا يعارضه حديث الاستنطاق في عالم الذر على تقدير صحته

BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r7.claim: In Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's version, after eliciting their testimony God calls the seven heavens, earth, and Adam as witnesses, warns them not to associate partners, promises messengers and books, and they affirm that He alone is their Lord and God.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r7.anchor: منها في الموطأ ومسند أحمد وإسحاق بن راهويه ومحمد بن نصر المروزي وأبي يعلى الموصلي ومستدرك الحاكم وكتاب المائتين لأبي عثمان الصابوني عن صحابة وتابعين مرفوعا وموقوفا - منهم عمر وأبي بن كعب

BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r8.claim: The author concludes that two covenants were taken: an inward, rational one through evidence and an outward, verbal one conveyed by messengers, reflecting special care for humanity and its honored, serious purpose.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p148/r8.anchor: والحاصل أنه أخذ علينا عهدان : أحدهما حالي تهدى إليه العقول , وهو نصب الآدلة والآخر مقالي اخبرت به الرسل

TUSTARI:7:172/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172/r1.claim: God took the prophets from Adam's loins and then took each prophet's offspring as intelligent particles; He covenanted with the prophets to convey His commands and prohibitions.
TUSTARI:7:172/r1.anchor: أخذ الأنبياء من ظهر آدم عليه الصلاة والسلام، ثم أخذ من ظهر كل نبي ذريته كهيئة الذر، لهم عقول

TUSTARI:7:172/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172/r2.claim: God summoned all to acknowledge His lordship and displayed His power until they answered yes; their assent encompassed His purpose for creation and was a trial.
TUSTARI:7:172/r2.anchor: ثم دعاهم جميعا إلى الإقرار بربوبيته لقوله تعالى: { ألست بربكم } [172] وأظهر قدرته حتى { قالوا بلى } [172]

TUSTARI:7:172/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172/r3.claim: The prophets were made witnesses against them; God returned them to Adam's loins and later sent prophets to remind them of the covenant.
TUSTARI:7:172/r3.anchor: ثم أعادهم في صلب آدم عليه السلام، ثم بعث الأنبياء ليذكرهم عهده وميثاقه

TUSTARI:7:172/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172/r4.claim: God knew from the covenant which souls would deny or affirm it; the Hour will not come until every soul who took the covenant has emerged.
TUSTARI:7:172/r4.anchor: وكان في علمه يوم أقروا بما أقروا به من يكذب به ومن يصدق به، فلا تقوم الساعة حتى تخرج كل نسمة قد أخذ الميثاق عليها

TUSTARI:7:172/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172/r5.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172/r5.claim: A sign of misery is denying God's power; signs of felicity include a heart spacious with faith, inward wealth, protection in obedience, and success in asceticism.
TUSTARI:7:172/r5.anchor: إن من علامات الشقاوة إنكار القدرة، وإن من علامة السعادة أن تكون واسع القلب بالإيمان، وأن ترزق الغنى في القلب

TUSTARI:7:172/r6.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172/r6.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172/r6.claim: Learning proper conduct with God purifies the heart and brings felicity; preserving adab is exceptionally difficult.
TUSTARI:7:172/r6.anchor: ومن ألهم الأدب فيما بينه وبين الله تعالى طهر قلبه ويرزق السعادة، وليس شيء أضيق من حفظ الأدب

TUSTARI:7:172/r7.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172/r7.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172/r7.claim: He prescribes austere living: plain food and clothing, mosques as homes, natural light, water, cleanliness, caution, acceptance, and piety.
TUSTARI:7:172/r7.anchor: اجعلوا طعامكم الشعير، وحلواكم التمر، وإدامكم الملح، ودسمكم اللبن، ولباسكم الصوف، وبيوتكم المساجد

TUSTARI:7:172/r8.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172/r8.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172/r8.claim: His regimen also calls for eating at night, sleeping by day, remembrance in speech, reflection in silence, learning from what one sees, reliance on God, and patience until death.
TUSTARI:7:172/r8.anchor: وأكلكم بالليل، ونومكم بالنهار، وكلامكم الذكر، وصمتكم وهمتكم التفكر، ونظركم العبرة

TUSTARI:7:172#2/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r1.claim: Three signs of misery are missing congregational prayer while near a mosque, missing it while in the city, and missing pilgrimage while in Mecca.
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r1.anchor: ثلاث من علامات الشقاوة: أن تفوته الجماعة وهو بقرب من المسجد، وأن تفوته الجماعة وهو في المدينة

TUSTARI:7:172#2/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r2.claim: Sahl divides humanity's offspring into three orders.
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r2.anchor: قال سهل: والذرية ثلاث: أول وثاني وثالث

TUSTARI:7:172#2/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r3.claim: Before creation, God brought forth a light from Muhammad's light; its prostration produced a vast luminous column containing Muhammad's essence, where he served God and witnessed faith and certainty for a million years.
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r3.anchor: أظهر من نوره نورا، فلما بلغ حجاب العظمة سجد لله سجدة، فخلق سبحانه من سجدته عمودا عظيما كالزجاج من النور

TUSTARI:7:172#2/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r4.claim: God honored Muhammad with witnessing Him a million years before creation began.
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r4.anchor: فأكرمه الله تعالى بالمشاهدة قبل بدء الخلق بألف ألف عام

TUSTARI:7:172#2/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r5.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r5.claim: Iblis captures everyone except the prophets and truthful whose hearts witness their faith and know God's constant observation of them.
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r5.anchor: وما من أحد في الدنيا إلا غلبه إبليس لعنه الله فأسره، إلا الأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم، والصديقون الذين شاهدت قلوبهم إيمانهم

TUSTARI:7:172#2/r6.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r6.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r6.claim: The degree of their witnessing governs how they recognize trials and seek protection; their neediness toward God deepens their knowledge and understanding of benefit and harm.
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r6.anchor: فعلى قدر مشاهدتهم يعرفون الابتلاء، وعلى قدر معرفتهم الابتلاء يطلبون العصمة، وعلى قدر فقرهم وفاقتهم إليه يعرفون الضر والنفع

TUSTARI:7:172#2/r7.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r7.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r7.claim: No prophet was given as much service as Muhammad; every station of service granted to Adam's descendants was also granted to him.
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r7.anchor: ما حمل الله على أحد من الأنبياء ما حمل على نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم من الخدمة

TUSTARI:7:172#2/r8.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r8.claim: The Prophet said that his Lord fed and gave him drink in a special way.
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r8.anchor:
وقد سئل عن معنى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" إني لست كأحدكم إن ربي يطعمني ويسقيني "

TUSTARI:7:172#2/r9.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r9.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r9.claim: Sahl explains that the Prophet had no food or drink; his divine privilege was like eating and drinking, and if he had food he would have given it to his family and the people of the Suffa first.
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r9.anchor: ما كان معه طعام ولا شراب، ولكنه كان يذكر خصوصيته عند الله تعالى، فيكون كمن أكل الطعام وشرب الشراب

TUSTARI:7:172#2/r10.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r10.claim: A prophetic report says Muhammad's body was created from Adam's clay.
TUSTARI:7:172#2/r10.anchor: وخلق محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم، يعني جسده، من طين آدم عليه السلام

TUSTARI:7:172#3/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172#3/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172#3/r1.claim: The third order is Adam's descendants: God created those who seek Him from Adam's light and those chosen by Him from Muhammad's light.
TUSTARI:7:172#3/r1.anchor: والثالث: ذرية آدم. وإن الله عز وجل خلق المريدين من نور آدم، وخلق المرادين من نور محمد

TUSTARI:7:172#3/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:172#3/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:172#3/r2.claim: Ordinary people live through the mercy of the spiritually close, and the close through the mercy of those brought near; their light runs before them and to their right.
TUSTARI:7:172#3/r2.anchor: فالعامة من الخلق يعيشون في رحمة أهل القرب، وأهل القرب يعيشون في رحمة المقرب

DURR-FULL:v3p597/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r1.speaker: غير مذكور
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r1.claim: In the reported answers, today signifies work, yesterday an example, tomorrow a term, and the day after tomorrow a hope.
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r1.anchor: وأما اليوم: فعمل وأما أمس: فمثل وأما غد: فأجل وبعد غد فأمل

DURR-FULL:v3p597/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r2.speaker: غير مذكور
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r2.claim: Lightning is described as whips in angels' hands for striking clouds; thunder is the name of the angel who drives clouds, whose voice is a rebuke.
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r2.anchor: مخاريق بأيدي الملائكة تضرب بها السحاب

DURR-FULL:v3p597/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r3.speaker: غير مذكور
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r3.claim: The Milky Way is described as heaven's gates, from which the gates are opened.
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r3.anchor: وأما المجرة: فأبواب السماء ومنها تفتح الأبواب

DURR-FULL:v3p597/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r4.speaker: غير مذكور
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r4.claim: The mark in the moon is linked to God's effacing the night sign; without it, night and day would not be distinguishable.
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r4.anchor: وأما المحو الذي في القمر فقول الله {وجعلنا الليل والنهار آيتين فمحونا آية الليل} الاسراء الآية 12 ولولا ذلك المحو لم يعرف الليل من النهار

DURR-FULL:v3p597/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r5.speaker: قيصر
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r5.claim: After Muawiya sent the answers, Caesar said only a prophet or a member of a prophet's household could know them.
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r5.anchor: فبعث بها معاوية إلى قيصر وكتب إليه جواب مسائله فقال قيصر: ما يعلم هذا إلا نبي أو رجل من أهل بيت نبي

DURR-FULL:v3p597/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r6.claim: God created Adam, took a covenant that He was their Lord, wrote their lifespans, provisions, and afflictions, then brought his descendants out like particles and took their covenants too.
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم} الآية قال: خلق الله آدم وأخذ ميثاقه أنه ربه

DURR-FULL:v3p597/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r7.claim: God brought Adam's descendants out like particles, named each person and their future deeds, then took two handfuls and assigned one group to Paradise and one to Hell.
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم} الآية قال: لما خلق الله آدم أخذ ذريته من ظهره كهيئة الذر ثم سماهم بأسمائهم

DURR-FULL:v3p597/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r8.claim: God produced Adam's descendants like particles, asked who their Lord was and received the answer that God was their Lord, then returned them to Adam's loins until their births without increase or decrease.
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإذ أخذ ربك} الآية قال: إن الله خلق آدم ثم أخرج ذريته من صلبه مثل الذر

DURR-FULL:v3p597/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r9.claim: When Adam descended at Dahna, God wiped his back and brought out every soul destined until the Resurrection, asking them to affirm His lordship; the report continues that the pen was then sealed.
DURR-FULL:v3p597/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما أهبط آدم عليه السلام حين أهبط بدحناء فمسح الله ظهره

DURR-FULL:v3p598/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r1.claim: The continuation says the pen was thereby sealed with everything that would occur through the Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r1.anchor: فيومئذ جف القلم بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v3p598/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r2.claim: God wiped Adam's loins, brought out all descendants through the Resurrection, and took their covenant that He was their Lord; when asked, everyone answers that God is Lord.
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: مسح الله على صلب آدم فأخرج من صلبه ما يكون من ذريته إلى يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v3p598/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r3.claim: The descendants were taken from Adam's back as a comb passes through hair.
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو في قوله {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم} قال: أخذهم من ظهرهم كما يؤخذ بالمشط من الرأس

DURR-FULL:v3p598/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas describes Adam's descendants emerging from his loins like tiny particles amid water.
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: أخرج ذريته من صلبه كأنهم الذر في آذىء من الماء

DURR-FULL:v3p598/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r5.claim: God struck Adam's right shoulder and brought out pearl-like descendants for Paradise, then struck his left and brought out dark descendants for the Fire; Ibn Abbas connects this to 7:179.
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: إن الله ضرب بيمينه على منكب آدم فخرج منه مثل اللؤلؤ في كفه فقال: هذا للجنة

DURR-FULL:v3p598/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r6.claim: At Batn Nu'man by Arafah, God wiped Adam's back and brought out every future soul, took their covenant, and Ibn Abbas recited the following excuse clause with yāʾ: يقولوا.
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: مسح الله ظهر آدم وهو ببطن نعمان - واد إلى جنب عرفة - فأخرج منه كل نسمة

DURR-FULL:v3p598/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the clause about what people will say on Judgment Day as يقولوا, with the letter yāʾ.

DURR-FULL:v3p598/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r8.speaker: عبد الكريم بن أبي أمية
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r8.claim: The descendants emerged from Adam's back in a line like an ant trail.
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r8.anchor: عن عبد الكريم بن أبي أمية قال: أخرجوا من ظهره مثل طريق النمل

DURR-FULL:v3p598/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r9.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r9.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says the spirits affirmed faith and knowledge of God before their bodies were created.
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r9.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب قال: أقروا له بالإيمان والمعرفة الأرواح قبل أن يخلق أجسادها

DURR-FULL:v3p598/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r10.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r10.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b also says God created the spirits before the bodies and took their covenant then.
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r10.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب قال: خلق الله الأرواح قبل أن يخلق الأجساد فأخذ ميثاقهم

DURR-FULL:v3p598/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة (من طريق السدي)
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r11.claim: According to Ibn Masud and other Companions, before Adam's descent God wiped his right back and brought out pearl-white descendants, telling them to enter Paradise by His mercy.
DURR-FULL:v3p598/r11.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة في قوله تعالى {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم} قالوا: لما أخرج الله آدم من الجنة قبل تهبيطه من السماء

DURR-FULL:v3p599/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p599/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة (من طريق السدي)
DURR-FULL:v3p599/r1.claim: The same report says God drew dark descendants from Adam's left side, assigned them to the Fire, then took the covenant; witnesses were appointed so people could not plead ignorance or blame ancestral shirk, and all Adam's children know God as Lord.
DURR-FULL:v3p599/r1.anchor: ومسح صفحة ظهره اليسرى فأخرج منه ذرية سوداء كهيئة الذر فقال: ادخلوا النار ولا أبالي

DURR-FULL:v3p599/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p599/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p599/r2.claim: Umar reports that God created Adam, wiped his back, assigned one group Paradise and another Hell, and ordained their deeds and ends, including that some would be sealed by their worst deeds.
DURR-FULL:v3p599/r2.anchor: سألت عمر بن الخطاب عن قوله {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم} قال: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v3p599/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p599/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p599/r3.claim: Ubay says God made the descendants spirits in forms, made them speak, took their covenant, and called the heavens and Adam as witnesses so people could not plead ignorance; He commanded them not to associate partners with Him.
DURR-FULL:v3p599/r3.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب في قوله {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم} قال: إلى قوله {بما فعل المبطلون} جميعا فجعلهم أرواحا في صورهم

DURR-FULL:v3p600/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p600/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p600/r1.claim: The continuation says prophets were distinguished by a further covenant to convey their prophetic message; it connects that covenant to 33:7 and human creation to innate nature in 30:30, while citing 7:102 and 7:101 about broken covenants and prior rejection.
DURR-FULL:v3p600/r1.anchor: ورأى الأنبياء فيهم مثل السرج عليهم النور وخصوا بميثاق آخر في الرسالة والنبوة أن يبلغوا وهو قوله {وإذ أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم}

DURR-FULL:v3p600/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p600/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p600/r2.claim: The report says Jesus's spirit was among those covenanted in Adam's time; God sent him to Mary in human form, and Ubay adds that he entered her mouth.
DURR-FULL:v3p600/r2.anchor: فكان روح عيسى من تلك الأرواح التي أخذ عهدها وميثاقها في زمن آدم فأرسله الله إلى مريم في صورة بشر فتمثل لها بشرا سويا

DURR-FULL:v3p600/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p600/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p600/r3.claim: Ubay adds that Jesus's spirit entered Mary's mouth.

DURR-FULL:v3p600/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p600/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p600/r4.claim: The Prophet says God extracted two groups from Adam's back, one destined for Paradise and its deeds and one for Hell and its deeds; those destined for either are enabled to perform its deeds. Al-Tirmidhi graded the report good.
DURR-FULL:v3p600/r4.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عنها فقال أن الله خلق آدم ثم مسح ظهره بيمينه

DURR-FULL:v3p600/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p600/r5.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p600/r5.claim: God took the covenant from Adam's back at Na'man on Arafah, extracted every descendant, scattered them before Him like particles, and addressed them directly; al-Hakim graded this report sound.
DURR-FULL:v3p600/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن الله أخذ الميثاق من ظهر آدم بنعمان يوم عرفة

DURR-FULL:v3p601/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p601/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p601/r1.claim: The Prophet says the descendants were drawn from Adam's back as a comb passes through hair, then addressed about God's lordship with angels witnessing so they could not plead ignorance.
DURR-FULL:v3p601/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم}

DURR-FULL:v3p601/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p601/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p601/r2.claim: The Prophet says God brought every future soul from Adam, made Eve from a rib, took their covenant, and assigned afflictions; Adam asked about the ill and thanked God was desired, saw prophets and David, gave David forty years from his own lifespan, then denied it at death, as did his descendants.
DURR-FULL:v3p601/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن الله لما خلق آدم مسح ظهره فخرت منه كل نسمة هو خالقها إلى يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v3p601/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p601/r3.speaker: جويبر
DURR-FULL:v3p601/r3.claim: When the six-day-old son of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim died, al-Dahhak instructed that the boy's face be exposed and bonds loosened because the child would be seated and questioned about the covenant in Adam's loins.
DURR-FULL:v3p601/r3.anchor: عن جويبر قال: مات ابن الضحاك بن مزاحم ابن ستة أيام فقال: إذا وضعت ابني في لحده

DURR-FULL:v3p602/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p602/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p602/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the covenant in Adam's loins required worshipping God alone; God guaranteed provisions and returned descendants to Adam, and those who later affirm the covenant benefit from the first, while children dying before accountability die upon the original fitra.
DURR-FULL:v3p602/r1.anchor: فقلت: عم يسأل قال: عن ميثاق الذي أقر به في صلب آدم حدثني ابن عباس: أن الله مسح صلب آدم

DURR-FULL:v3p602/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p602/r2.speaker: سلمان
DURR-FULL:v3p602/r2.claim: God wrote future lifespans, provisions, deeds, misery, and happiness when He brought Adam's descendants out; the blessed do good and attend good gatherings, while the wretched do evil and attend evil gatherings.
DURR-FULL:v3p602/r2.anchor: عن سلمان قال: إن الله لما خلق آدم مسح ظهره فأخرج منه ما هو ذارىء إلى يوم القيامة فكتب الآجال والأرزاق والأعمال والشقوة والسعادة

DURR-FULL:v3p602/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p602/r3.speaker: أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p602/r3.claim: The Prophet describes God taking the covenant of the two groups with His right hand and other hand, both right; after both affirm, He mixes them, and one asks why, prompting a citation about people doing other deeds (23:63). The report continues next segment.
DURR-FULL:v3p602/r3.anchor: عن أبي أمامة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: خلق الله الخلق وقضى القضية وأخذ ميثاق النبيين

DURR-FULL:v3p603/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r1.claim: The Prophet says the two groups were returned to Adam's loins and that each group acts toward its destined home.
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r1.anchor: ثم ردهم في صلب آدم فأهل الجنة أهلها وأهل النار أهلها فقال قائل: يا رسول الله فما الأعمال قال: يعمل كل قوم لمنازلهم

DURR-FULL:v3p603/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r2.claim: After hearing that each group works toward its destined home, Umar says they should therefore strive.
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r2.anchor: فقال عمر بن الخطاب: إذا نجتهد

DURR-FULL:v3p603/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r3.claim: The Prophet says Adam's descendants emerged with lights between their eyes; Adam admired David, who would live sixty years, and gave him forty of his own years, then denied the gift when death came, and his descendants forgot and denied too.
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما خلق الله آدم مسح ظهره فسقط من ظهره نسمة هو خالقها من ذريته إلى يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v3p603/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r4.claim: Hasan says God extracted the people of Paradise from Adam's right side and the people of Hell from his left; seeing their afflictions, Adam asked for equality, and God said He wanted to be thanked before returning them to Adam's loins.
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r4.anchor: عن الحسن قال: لما خلق الله آدم عليه السلام وأخرج أهل الجنة من صفحته اليمنى وأخرج أهل النار من صفحته اليسرى

DURR-FULL:v3p603/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r5.speaker: قتادة والحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r5.claim: When Adam saw some descendants favored over others, he asked why they were not equal; God said He loves to be thanked, so the favored person sees his advantage and praises and thanks Him.
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r5.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن قالا: لما عرضت على آدم ذريته فرأى فضل بعضهم على بعض

DURR-FULL:v3p603/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r6.speaker: بكر
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r6.claim: Bakr reports the same account as the preceding narration about Adam seeing the differences among his descendants and God wanting to be thanked.
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r6.anchor: وأخرج أحمد في الزهد عن بكر مثله

DURR-FULL:v3p603/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r7.speaker: هشام بن حكيم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r7.claim: Asked whether deeds are begun or already decreed, the Prophet answers that God took Adam's descendants, made them testify, and held two groups, one for Paradise and one for Hell; the report continues with their deeds being made easy.
DURR-FULL:v3p603/r7.anchor: عن هشام بن حكيم أن رجلا أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: أتبتدأ الأعمال أم قد قضي القضاء

DURR-FULL:v3p604/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r1.claim: The continuation says Paradise's people are enabled for Paradise's deeds and Hell's people for Hell's deeds.
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r1.anchor: فأهل الجنة ميسرون لعمل أهل الجنة وأهل النار ميسرون لعمل أهل النار

DURR-FULL:v3p604/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r2.speaker: معاوية عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r2.claim: God drew Adam's descendants from his loins until they filled the earth; the Prophet illustrated their number by closing one hand over the other.
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r2.anchor: عن معاوية قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله أخرج ذرية آدم من صلبه حتى ملؤوا الأرض

DURR-FULL:v3p604/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r3.speaker: أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r3.claim: The Prophet says God granted that the children of polytheists serve the people of Paradise because they did not reach their parents' level of shirk and remained in the first covenant.
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r3.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سألت ربي فأعطاني أولاد المشركين خدما لأهل الجنة

DURR-FULL:v3p604/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r4.speaker: أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r4.claim: A man in Hell would ransom himself with everything on earth; God says He had asked him for the easier thing, not to associate partners with Him under the covenant taken from Adam, but he insisted on shirk.
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r4.anchor: عن أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يقال للرجل من أهل النار يوم القيامة:

DURR-FULL:v3p604/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r5.speaker: علي بن حسين
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r5.claim: Ali ibn Husayn practiced coitus interruptus and interpreted this verse in support of the practice.
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r5.anchor: عن علي بن حسين أنه كان يعزل ويتأول هذه الآية {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم}

DURR-FULL:v3p604/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r6.claim: On coitus interruptus, the Prophet says there is no need to avoid it: a life whose covenant God took will be brought forth regardless.
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن العزل فقال لا عليكم أن لا تفعلوا إن تكن مما أخذ الله منها الميثاق

DURR-FULL:v3p604/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r7.speaker: أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r7.claim: The Prophet says that if the semen from which a child is formed were poured on a rock, God would bring forth the life He had decreed.
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r7.anchor: عن أنس قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن العزل فقال لو أن الماء الذي يكون منه الولد صب على صخرة لأخرج الله منها ما قدر

DURR-FULL:v3p604/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r8.claim: Ibn Masud says that a soul covenanted from a man's loins would emerge even if its seed were poured onto smooth stone, so one may choose coitus interruptus or not.
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r8.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه سئل عن العزل فقال: لو أخذ الله ميثاق نسمة من صلب رجل ثم أفرغه على صفا لأخرجه

DURR-FULL:v3p604/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r9.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r9.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i says people used to say that a child decreed in the semen would be produced even if it fell on a rock.
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r9.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي قال: كانوا يقولون: إن النطفة التي قضى الله فيها الولد لو وقعت على صخرة لأخرج الله منها الولد

DURR-FULL:v3p604/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r10.speaker: فاطمة بنت حسين
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r10.claim: Fatima bint Husayn says God placed the covenant of Adam's descendants at the Corner, so touching the Stone fulfills God's covenant.
DURR-FULL:v3p604/r10.anchor: عن فاطمة بنت حسين قالت: لما أخذ الله الميثاق من بني آدم جعله في الركن فمن الوفاء بعهد الله استلام الحجر

DURR-FULL:v3p605/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r1.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r1.claim: Jaʿfar reports that the primordial acknowledgment was written in a book and placed in the Black Stone; touching it fulfills the pledge made by humanity.
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r1.anchor: عن جعفر بن محمد قال: كنت مع أبي محمد بن علي

DURR-FULL:v3p605/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God brought Adam’s descendants out like tiny particles, distinguishing the people of Paradise from those of Hell and summoning them to obey.
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: ضرب الله متن آدم فخرجت كل نفس مخلوقة للجنة بيضاء نقية

DURR-FULL:v3p605/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r3.claim: Umar said he kissed the Black Stone only because he had seen the Prophet do so, since he understood that a stone could neither harm nor benefit.
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r3.anchor: إني أعلم أنك حجر لا تضر ولا تنفع ولولا أني رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبلك ما قبلتك

DURR-FULL:v3p605/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r4.claim: Ali explains that the Black Stone benefits by bearing witness to the covenant God took from Adam’s descendants, whose record was placed in the stone.
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r4.anchor: قال له علي بن أبي طالب: يا أمير المؤمنين إنه يضر وينفع

DURR-FULL:v3p605/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r5.claim: The Prophet said the Black Stone will speak on Judgment Day and testify to the monotheism of those who touched it.
DURR-FULL:v3p605/r5.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول يؤتى يوم القيامة بالحجر الأسود وله لسان ذلق

DURR-FULL:v3p606/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God held all people like mustard seeds, turned them in His hand, returned them to their fathers’ loins, and later reminded them of the covenant in 5:7; he links their failure to keep it with 7:102.
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإذ أخذ ربك} الآية قال: أخذهم في كفه كأنهم الخردل الأولين والآخرين

DURR-FULL:v3p606/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that God shook Adam like a bag, extracted his descendants, and divided them into two handfuls destined for Paradise and Hell.
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: لما خلق الله آدم نفضه نفض المزود

DURR-FULL:v3p606/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r3.claim: The Prophet says God took humanity from Adam’s back and assigned some to Paradise and others to Hell; deeds follow the decreed allotment.
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r3.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول إن الله تبارك وتعالى خلق آدم ثم أخذ الخلق من ظهره

DURR-FULL:v3p606/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r4.claim: The Prophet describes white descendants emerging from Adam’s right shoulder and dark descendants from his left, assigning each group its destination.
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r4.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: خلق الله آدم حين خلقه فضرب كتفه اليمنى

DURR-FULL:v3p606/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r5.claim: The Prophet says God took two handfuls from Adam, placing the good in the right and the bad in the other, then returned them to Adam’s loins for successive generations.
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r5.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله جل ذكره يوم خلق آدم قبض من صلبه قبضتين

DURR-FULL:v3p606/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r6.claim: Abu Saʿid transmits the Prophet’s statement that one of the two primordial handfuls is destined for Paradise, without further qualification in this excerpt.
DURR-FULL:v3p606/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال في القبضتين هذه في الجنة ولا أبالي

DURR-FULL:v3p607/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r1.claim: The Prophet says the two primordial groups are destined respectively for their appointed outcomes; people then dispersed without disputing divine decree.
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال في القبضتين هؤلاء لهذه وهؤلاء لهذه

DURR-FULL:v3p607/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r2.claim: The Prophet says Adam’s descendants emerged from his right and left sides like dust and ashes, destined for Paradise and Hell respectively.
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما خلق الله آدم ضرب بيده على شق آدم الأيمن

DURR-FULL:v3p607/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r3.claim: A Companion called Abu ʿAbd Allah wept because he feared he might be in the handful assigned to Hell and did not know his fate.
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r3.anchor: يقال له أبو عبد الله دخل عليه أصحابه يعودونه وهو يبكي فقالوا له: ما يبكيك

DURR-FULL:v3p607/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r4.claim: The Prophet says God took one handful for Paradise by His mercy and another for Hell without qualification.
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r4.anchor: عن أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن الله قبض قبضة فقال: للجنة برحمتي

DURR-FULL:v3p607/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r5.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God extracted all future people from Adam as tiny particles, obtained their acknowledgment, and divided them into two groups for Paradise and Hell.
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: إن الله أخرج من ظهر آدم يوم خلقه ما يكون إلى يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v3p607/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj reads the covenant as preventing descendants from pleading ignorance or blaming their ancestors’ shirk and the deeds of those who falsified the truth.
DURR-FULL:v3p607/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {إن تقولوا يوم القيامة انا كنا عن هذا غافلين} قال: عن الميثاق الذي أخذ عليهم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r1.claim: Umar reports that the Prophet described God extracting Adam’s descendants, assigning some to Paradise and others to Hell, and guiding each to deeds matching that destination until death.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r1.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ان الله خلق ادم ثم مسح ظهره بيمينه

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the covenant was taken at Nuʿman, meaning ʿArafa: all descendants were drawn from Adam and scattered like atoms to answer that God is their Lord.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : اخذ الله الميثاق من ظهر ادم بنعمان يعني عرفة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r3.claim: Said ibn Jubayr is reported to give a similar account of the primordial covenant at ʿArafa.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r3.anchor: وروى عن سعيد بن جبير نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says God covenanted with Adam, decreed his lifespan, provision, and affliction, then extracted his descendants as atoms and assigned their lifespans, provisions, and afflictions.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1612#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : واذ اخذ ربك من بني ادم من ظهورهم ذريتهم قال : خلق الله ادم واخذ ميثاقه انه ربه وكتب اجله

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God named each descendant and their deeds, then divided them into two handfuls, one for Paradise and one for Hell.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : واذ اخذ ربك من بني ادم من ظهورهم ذريتهم واشهدهم قال : لما خلق الله ادم اخذ ذريته من ظهره كهيئة الذر

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r2.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr compares the extraction of Adam’s descendants from his loins to drawing a comb from an archer’s gear.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ، عن عبد الله بن عمرو واذ اخذ ربك من بني ادم من ظهورهم قال : استخرجهم من صلبه كما يستخرج المشط من الرامي

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r3.claim: Ubay ibn Kaʿb says God drew the descendants from Adam drop by drop, with the prophets’ faces shining like lamps.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r3.anchor: عن ابى بن كعب واذ اخذ ربك من بني ادم من ظهورهم ذريتهم قال : استخرجهم من صلبه نطفا نطفا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says God wiped Adam’s back and brought his descendants out in particles like dust in water.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : مسح الله ظهر ادم ، فاخرج ذريته من ظهره مثل الذرفي اذى من الماء

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r5.claim: The Prophet reports that God extracted every future soul from Adam, took their covenant, and created Eve from one of Adam’s ribs.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r5.anchor: عن ابى هريرة ، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ان الله تبارك وتعالى لما ان خلق ادم مسح ظهره

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r6.claim: God showed Adam his descendants’ assigned illnesses; when Adam asked why, God said this would lead them to thank His favor.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r6.anchor: فقال ادم : يا رب لم فعلت هذا بذريتي ؟ قال : كي تشكر نعمتي يا ادم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r7.claim: Adam saw luminous prophets, learned David would live sixty years, and gave him forty years from his own lifespan.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r7.anchor: يا ادم من ذريتك قال : فمن هذا الذين اراه اظهرهم نورا ؟ قال : هذا داود

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r8.claim: At death Adam denied giving David forty years, saying they remained; the Prophet’s report attributes forgetfulness and denial to Adam’s descendants as well.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r8.anchor: قال الم يبق من اجلي اربعون سنة ؟ قال : اولم تعطها ابنك داود ؟ قال : لا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra says Adam forgot and denied the gift, and his descendants inherited forgetfulness and denial.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r9.anchor: كان أبو هريرة يقول : فنسى ادم ونسيت ذريته ، وجحد ادم فجحدت ذريته

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r10.speaker: أبو حفص بن أبي العاتكة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r10.claim: Abu Hafs ibn Abi al-Atika says Adam lived one thousand years.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1613/r10.anchor: قال ابن شعيب : اخبرني أبو حفص بن ابى العاتكة قال : وعمره كان الف سنة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God returned each descendant to Adam’s loins until birth, with every person’s covenant fixed and none added or removed until the Hour.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : واذ اخذ ربك من بني ادم من ظهورهم ذريتهم قال : ان الله خلق ادم ثم اخرج ذريته من صلبه مثل الذر

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r2.claim: Ubay ibn Kaʿb says God assembled all future people, formed them in pairs, and elicited their testimony that He alone is Lord.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r2.anchor: عن ابي بن كعب رضى الله عنه في قول الله تعالى : واذ اخذ ربك من بني ادم من ظهورهم ذريتهم واشهدهم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r3.claim: Ubay’s account has God warn humanity against associating partners with Him and promise messengers and scriptures to remind them of the covenant.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r3.anchor: اعلموا ان لا اله غيري ولا رب غيري ، ولا تشركوا بي شيئا ، واني سارسل لكم رسلا ينذرونكم عهدي وميثاقي

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r4.claim: Adam sees descendants of different wealth and appearance, asks why they were not made equal, and God replies that He wishes to be thanked.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r4.anchor: قال : يا رب لو سويت بين عبادك قال : اني احببت ان اشكر

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r5.claim: Ubay says the prophets received a further covenant concerning messengership and prophethood, linked to God’s covenant with the prophets.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r5.anchor: وخصوا بميثاق اخر من الرسالة والنبوة فهو الذي يقول تعالى : واذ اخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r6.claim: Ubay links the primordial covenant to humanity’s fitra, the natural religion God created people upon.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r6.anchor: وهو الذي يقول : فاقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها لا تبديل لخلق الله

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r7.claim: Ubay links the covenant narrative to the declaration that this is a warner from the earlier warners.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r7.anchor: وفي ذلك قال : هذا نذير من النذر الاولى

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r8.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r8.claim: Ubay connects it with the statement that most people did not keep a covenant and were transgressors.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1614/r8.anchor: وفي ذلك قال : وما وجدنا لاكثرهم من عهد وان وجدنا اكثرهم لفاسقين

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1615/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1615/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1615/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says God extracted all future descendants from Adam as atoms, asked whether He was their Lord, and they affirmed; the angels witnessed so they could not claim ignorance.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1615/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك قال ان الله اخرج من ظهر ادم يوم خلقه ما يكون إلى يوم القيامة ، فاخرجهم مثل الذر ثم قال : الست بربكم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1615/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1615/r2.speaker: عبد الملك بن أبي يزيد ووهب بن منبه
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1615/r2.claim: Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Yazid and Wahb ibn Munabbih identify the ones addressed in the primordial covenant as the messengers.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1615/r2.anchor: عن عبد الملك بن ابى يزيد ووهب بن منبه في قول الله : واذ اخذ ربك من بني ادم من ظهورهم إلى قوله : الست بربكم قالا الرسل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r1.claim: The discourse shifts from Israel, who were not polytheists, to the Arab idolaters addressed throughout the sura; the mention of their fathers' associationism returns to the sura's opening concern and connects by analogy with the covenant at Sinai.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r1.anchor: هذا كلام مصروف إلى غير بني إسرائيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r2.claim: This covenant was a creative one, established by embedding its meaning in every soul's nature and innate disposition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r2.anchor: وهو عهد حصل بالخطاب التكويني أي بجعل معناه في جبلة كل نسمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r3.claim: The change in style is clear: direct address and an explicit antecedent from Adam make the admonition universal; this begins the rebuke of polytheists and prepares for the rest of the sura.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r3.anchor: وتبدل أسلوب القصة واضح إذ اشتملت هذه القصة على خطاب في قوله : { أن تقولوا يوم القيامة } إلى آخر الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r4.claim: Here إذ denotes past time without being adverbial; it is the object of an omitted command to remember.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r4.anchor: و { إذ } اسم للزمن الماضي ، وهو هنا مجرد عن الظرفية ، فهو مفعول به لفعل ( اذكر ) محذوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r5.claim: Taking offspring from Adam's descendants means God took each individual's offspring from each individual human, so every human acknowledged God's lordship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r5.anchor: فتعين أن يكون المعنى : أخذ ربك كل فرد من أفراد الذرية . من كل فرد من أفراد بني آدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r6.claim: Both مِن phrases, 'from the children of Adam' and 'from their backs,' indicate a point of origin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r6.anchor: و ( من ) في قوله : { من بني آدم } وقوله : { من ظهورهم } ابتدائية فيهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r7.claim: Dhurrīya is a collective noun for human offspring; its plural here emphasizes that all offspring are included.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r7.anchor: والذريات جمع ذرية ، والذرية اسم جمع لما يتولد من الإنسان ، وجمعه هنا للتنصيص على العموم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r8.claim: The covenant on descendants drawn from human backs entails, by a fortiori reasoning, a covenant on the descendants in Adam's back; otherwise Adam's immediate children would be excluded despite having greater claim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r8.anchor: وأخذ العهد على الذرية المخرجين من ظهور بني آدم يقتضي أخذ العهد عى الذرية الذين في ظهر آدم بدلالة الفحوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r9.claim: Many reports from the Prophet and Companions, of varying strength and each with a criticized transmitter, mutually support this inference.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r9.anchor: ومما يثبت هذه الدلالة أخبار كثيرة رويت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعن جمع من أصحابه ، متفاوتة في القوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r10.claim: In the clearest report, transmitted by Mālik in the Muwaṭṭaʾ from ʿUmar, God creates Adam, extracts descendants twice from his back, and says the first group is destined for Paradise and the second for the Fire; the author says it explains the verse's implication, not its explicit wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r10.anchor: روى مالك في ( الموطأ ) في ترجمة ( النهي عن القول بالقدر ) بسنده إلى عمر بن الخطاب قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسأل عن هذه الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r11.claim: The verse explicitly describes taking the descendants' acknowledgment of God's lordship; the hadith adds the distinction between the people of Paradise and Fire, perhaps completing the account in response to the question or because a transmitter reported only part of what he heard.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p165/r11.anchor: وجاء في الآية أن الله أخذ على الذريات العهد بالإقرار بربوبية الله ، ولم يتعرض لذلك في الحديث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r1.claim: Taking is metaphorical for bringing out and extracting, as in 6:46.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r1.anchor: والأخذ مجاز في الإخراج والانتزاع قال الله تعالى : { قل أرأيتم إن أخذ الله سمعكم وأبصاركم } ( الأنعام : 46 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r2.claim: 'From their backs' is an appositive part of 'the children of Adam'; the repeated preposition reinforces the apposition, as at 6:99.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r2.anchor: وقوله : { من ظهورهم } بدل { من بني آدم } أبدل بعض من كل ، وقد أعيد حرف الجر مع البدل للتأكيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r3.claim: Witnessing themselves can mean confession or making them confess; here it figuratively describes an unseen state known to God, with acknowledgment rooted in their innate nature. The pronoun refers to the descendants collectively.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r3.anchor: والإشهاد على الأنفس يطلق على ما يساوي الإقرار أو الحمل عليه ، وهو هنا الحمل على الإقرار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r4.claim: Their saying 'yes' is also figurative: their state shows that they acknowledge God's lordship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r4.anchor: والقول في { قالوا بلى } مستعار أيضا لدلالة حالهم على الإعتراف بالربوبية لله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r5.claim: 'Am I not your Lord?' is an omitted quotation explaining the witnessing: God established this acknowledgment by creative command, distributing it to each descendant individually.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r5.anchor: وجملة { ألست بربكم } مقول لقول محذوف هو بيان لجملة { أشهدهم على أنفسهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r6.claim: The interrogative is confirmatory: a person thought to deny is asked negatively, so an actual denier would answer no, while one not committed to denial rejects the negative and thereby confirms the truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r6.anchor: والاستفهام في { ألست بربكم } تقريري ، ومثله يقال في تقرير من يظن به الإنكار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r7.claim: The same confirmatory construction appears when unbelievers are asked whether the Fire is real at 46:34; the author also refers to his earlier discussion at 6:130.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r7.anchor: وعليه قوله تعالى : { ويوم يعرض الذين كفروا على النار أليس هذا بالحق } ( الأحقاف : 34 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r8.claim: The dialogue represents an unseen state in which God's creative command controls beings and their attributes; since it lies beyond ordinary experience, representation brings it near. God created in humans awareness of monotheism's evidence and the capacity to grasp it when corrupting influences are removed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p167/r8.anchor: والكلام تمثيل حال من أحوال الغيب ، من تسلط أمر التكوين الإلهي على ذوات الكائنات وأعراضها عند إرادة تكوينها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r1.claim: The answer قالوا بلى responds to a confirmatory question and is separated because it follows a dialogue pattern, as in 2:30.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r1.anchor: وجملة : { قالوا بلى } جواب عن الاستفهام التقريري ، وفصلت لأنها جاءت على طريقة المحاورة كما تقدم في قوله تعالى : { قالوا أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها في سورة البقرة ( 30 ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r2.claim: The attribution of speech is either literal and miraculous or figurative: their condition shows they are subject to God; the same figure occurs at 41:11 and in Abu al-Najm’s verse, as common Arabic usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r2.anchor: وأطلق القول إما حقيقة فذلك قول خارق للعادة ، وإما مجازا على دلالة حالهم على أنهم مربوبون لله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says answering نعم would risk disbelief because it can affirm either the negative or its negation; بلى unambiguously acknowledges God’s lordship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r3.anchor: وهذا معنى ما نقل عن ابن عباس في هذه الآية أنه قال : ( لو قالوا نعم لكفروا ) أي لكان جوابهم محتملا للكفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r4.claim: Nafi, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Abu Jaafar, and Yaqub read ذرياتهم in the plural; the remaining readers read ذريتهم in the singular.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، وأبو عمرو ، وابن عامر ، وأبو جعفر ، ويعقوب : { ذرياتهم } ، بالجمع ، وقرأ الباقون { ذريتهم } ، بالإفراد .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r5.claim: شهدنا reinforces the content of بلى, and testimony here also means acknowledgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r5.anchor: وقولهم : { شهدنا } تأكيد لمضمون { بلى } والشهادة هنا أيضا بمعنى الإقرار .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r6.claim: أن تقولوا is causal with an omitted لام; the intended reason is to prevent the excuse that they were unaware, with negation understood, or to forestall that claim if no testimony occurred, as at 6:156.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r6.anchor: والمقصود التعليل بنفي أن يقولوا { إنا كنا عن هذا غافلين } لا بإيقاع القول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r7.claim: Most readers use second-person تقولوا, shifting from third-person to address the people to make clear the covenant recalls innate monotheism; this is a change of addressee, not iltifat. Abu Amr alone reads third-person, referring to Adam’s descendants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p168/r7.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : أن تقولوا بتاء الخطاب وقد حول الأسلوب من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r5.claim: The opening is elliptic for remember when your Lord took; grammarians treat min ẓuhūrihim as an inclusive apposition to the children of Adam.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r5.anchor: التقدير واذكر إذ أخذ وقوله: من ظهورهم قال النحاة: هو بدل اشتمال من قوله: من بني آدم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r6.claim: The verse’s wording makes the taking from Adam’s descendants’ backs, without mentioning Adam by name.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r6.anchor: وألفاظ هذه الآية تقتضي أن الأخذ إنما كان من بني آدم من ظهورهم وليس لآدم في الآية ذكر بحسب اللفظة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r7.claim: Reports from the Prophet through ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, and others say that God drew Adam’s progeny from his back, in some accounts while Adam was created and in others after his descent; locations are variously placed in Sind or at Nuʿmān near ʿArafa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r7.anchor: وتواترت الأحاديث في تفسير هذه الآية عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من طريق عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه وعبد الله بن عباس وغيرهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r8.claim: The accounts vary on God’s action and the progeny’s form: He touched Adam’s back with His right hand or struck his shoulder and brought forth descendants like particles or mustard seeds; Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says they were souls given forms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r8.anchor: مسح على ظهره وفي بعض الروايات بيمينه وفي بعض الروايات ضرب منكبه فاستخرج منها أي من المسحة أو الضربة نسم بنيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r9.claim: Ibn ʿUmar transmits from the Prophet that the progeny were drawn from Adam like a comb through hair, given minds like Solomon’s ant, and covenanted to God as Lord with no other deity; they pledged and were told prophets would remind them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r9.anchor: وروى عبد الله بن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: أخذوا من ظهره كما يؤخذ بالمشط من الرأس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r10.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r10.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says the seven heavens witnessed the covenant, taken from everyone born through the Day of Resurrection at that place and time.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r10.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب وأشهد عليهم السماوات السبع فليس من أحد يولد إلى يوم القيامة إلا وقد أخذ عليه العهد في ذلك اليوم والمقام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r11.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r11.claim: Al-Suddī says the unbelievers gave the covenant then unwillingly, under dissimulation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474/r11.anchor: وقال السدي أعطى الكفار العهد يومئذ كارهين على وجه التقية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r1.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this a concise synthesis of the longer reports and says their wording does not fit the verse neatly; scholars have tried to reconcile them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: هذه نخيلة مجموع الروايات المطولة، وكأن ألفاظ هذه الأحاديث لا تلتئم مع ألفاظ الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the verse can refer to ordinary human reproduction: taking means bringing into existence, and recognition occurs at maturity through reason and the signs pointing to the Creator.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r3.claim: Although the wording permits the ordinary-reproduction interpretation, it conflicts with ʿUmar’s and Ibn ʿAbbās’s explanation by the prophetic report they transmitted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r3.anchor: لكن يرد عليه تفسير عمر بن الخطاب وابن عباس رضي الله عنهما الآية بالحديث المذكور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r4.speaker: الجرجاني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r4.claim: Al-Jurjānī develops the report’s account of God touching Adam and extracting his progeny.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r4.anchor: وطول الجرجاني في هذه المسألة ومدار كلامه على أن المسح وإخراج الذرية من أظهر آدم حسب الحديث،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r5.claim: The argument that taking from Adam’s back also means taking from descendants’ backs because branch and root are one is, in Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s view, too weak to withstand scrutiny.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r5.anchor: الذين هم الفرع إذ الفرع والأصل شيء واحد، إلى كلام كثير لا يثبت للنقد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r6.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r6.claim: Others understand the hadith’s touch, striking of the shoulder, and hand as expressions for creating the souls; the right hand means power, or the agent was an angel commanded by God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r6.anchor: وقال غيره: إن جميع ما في الحديث من مسح بيمينه وضرب منكبه ونحو هذا إنما هي عبارة عن إيجاد ذلك النسم منه، و «اليمين» عبارة عن القدرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r7.claim: On that reconciliation, the hadith adds Adam’s initial creation of the souls, while the verse describes the later covenant-taking.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r7.anchor: فتضمن الحديث صدر القصة وإيجاد النسم من آدم، وهذه زيادة على ما في الآية، ثم تضمنت الآية ما جرى بعد هذا من أخذ العهد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r8.claim: One syntactic explanation makes taking govern a covenant or pledge after descendants; from their backs describes ordinary reproduction, and their descendants is an apposition to the children of Adam.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r8.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون أخذ عاملا في عهد أو ميثاق تقدره بعد قوله ذريتهم ويكون قوله من ظهورهم لبيان جنس النبوة إذ المراد من الجميع التناسل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r9.claim: A second explanation says each soul already had a lineage to the back from which it would emerge, and taking means identifying them by that lineage, not creating them; their creation preceded the covenant as in the report.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p474#2/r9.anchor: والمعنى الآخر أنه لما كانت كل نسمة هنالك لها نسبة إلى التي هي من ظهرها كأن تعيين تلك النسبة أخذ من الظهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r1.speaker: الطرطوشي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r1.claim: Al-Ṭurṭūshī says the covenant binds people even when they do not remember it in this life, just as a divorce witnessed against someone still binds after he forgets it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r1.anchor: وقال الطرطوشي إن هذا العهد يلزم البشر وإن كانوا لا يذكرونه في هذه الحياة كما يلزم الطلاق من شهد عليه به وهو قد نسيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r2.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿĀmir read dhurriyyātihim in the plural intensive form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر: «ذرياتهم» جمع جمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read dhurriyyatahum; the singular here functions collectively.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي: «ذريتهم» والإفراد هنا جمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the discussion of the word dhurriyya has already appeared in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r4.anchor: وقد تقدم القول على لفظ الذرية في سورة آل عمران

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r5.claim: A story says the prophets appeared among the extracted souls like lamps; Adam admired David and gave him forty years from his own thousand-year lifespan, then disputed with the Angel of Death when he died at 960.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r5.anchor: وروي في قصص هذه الآية: أن الأنبياء عليهم السلام كانوا بين تلك النسم أمثال السرج وأن آدم عليه السلام رأى داود فأعجبه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r6.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says those who die young remain on the first covenant, while those who reach maturity receive the second covenant of this present life.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r6.anchor: قال الضحاك بن مزاحم: من مات صغيرا فهو على العهد الأول ومن بلغ فقد أخذه العهد الثاني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r7.speaker: الزجاج عن قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj transmits a view that each person’s birth and maturity bring a rational recognition of God through the signs, which constitutes the covenant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r7.anchor: وحكى الزجاج عن قوم أنهم قالوا إن هذه الآية عبارة عن أن كل نسمة إذا ولدت وبلغت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r8.speaker: author
