IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects that interpretation as weak and contrary to the transmitted reports.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r8.anchor: وهو قول ضعيف منكب عن الأحاديث المأثورة مطرح لها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r9.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says shāhidnā may be words spoken by some souls to others: they testified so people could not claim at the Resurrection that they lacked knowledge and faith; on this reading one should not pause at balā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r9.anchor: ذكره الطبري، وعلى هذا لا يحسن الوقف على قوله: بلى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r10.speaker: السدي وعبد الله بن عمر عن النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r10.claim: Alternatively, the angels say We have testified, which allows a pause at balā; al-Suddī explains the speakers as God and His angels, and Ibn ʿUmar transmits this from the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r10.anchor: قال السدي: المعنى قال الله وملائكته شهدنا، ورواه عبد الله بن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r11.speaker: القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r11.claim: All seven readers except Abū ʿAmr read an taqūlū, directly addressing those present; Abū ʿAmr reads an yaqūlū, narrating about absent people, also read by Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr, and Ibn Muḥayṣin; the readings suit the two interpretations.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r11.anchor: وقرأ السبعة غير أبي عمرو: «أن تقولوا» على مخاطبة حاضرين، وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده، «أن يقولوا» على الحكاية عن غائبين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r12.claim: The particle an is accusative as the object of an implied fear, meaning for fear that they would say this.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r12.anchor: وأن في موضع نصب على تقدير مخافة أن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports from the Prophet that God took the covenant from Adam at Nuʿman near Arafah, extracted all his descendants, scattered them before Him like ants, and addressed them face to face.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r1.anchor: روى ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال أخذ الله الميثاق من ظهر آدم بنعمان ونعمان قريب من عرفة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r2.claim: The phrase from their backs means from the backs of Adam's children, and grammatically substitutes for the children of Adam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r2.anchor: ومعنى الآية وإذا أخذ ربكم من ظهور بني آدم فقوله من ظهورهم بدل من بني آدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r3.claim: One explanation says the plural backs are used because some descendants were brought from others, making a separate mention of Adam's back unnecessary.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r3.anchor: وقيل إنما قال من ظهورهم ولم يقل من ظهر آدم لأنه أخرج بعضهم من ظهور بعض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir, Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read dhurriyyatahum in the singular; Nafi, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read the plural.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي ذريتهم على التوحيد وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر ذرياتهم على الجمع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r5.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r5.claim: Abu Ali notes that dhurriyya can be either a plural or a singular form.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو علي الذرية تكون جمعا وتكون واحدا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r6.claim: One view says God made them testify against themselves through their own confession; Muqatil holds this view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r6.anchor: أحدها أشهدهم على أنفسهم باقرارهم قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God showed them His oneness through His creation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r7.anchor: والثاني دلهم بخلقه على توحيده قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r8.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r8.claim: Ibn Jarir says God made some of them testify to the confession of others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p283#2/r8.anchor: والثالث أنه أشهد بعضهم على بعض باقرارهم بذلك قاله ابن جرير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r1.claim: The question means God said to them, 'Am I not your Lord?' and asks for confirmation; they answered that He is their Lord.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r1.anchor: ﴿ ألست بربكم ﴾ والمعنى وقال لهم ألست بربكم وهذا سؤال تقرير قالوا بلى شهدنا أنك ربنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says 'we testify' is God's report that He and the angels witnessed humanity's acknowledgment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r2.anchor: قال السدي قوله شهدنا خبر من الله تعالى عن نفسه وملائكته أنهم شهدوا على إقرار بني آدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r3.claim: It is good to pause after balā because the offspring's speech ends there.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r3.anchor: ويحسن الوقف على قوله بلى لأن كلام الذرية قد انقطع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r4.speaker: الكلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi says that after the descendants answered yes, God asked the angels to testify and they did.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r4.anchor: وزعم الكلبي ان الذرية لما قالت بلى قال الله للملائكة اشهدوا فقالوا شهدنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliya transmits from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that God gathered, paired, formed, and questioned them, then called the heavens, earth, and Adam as witnesses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r5.anchor: وروى أبو العالية عن أبي بن كعب قال جمعهم جميعا فجعلهم أزواجا ثم صورهم ثم استنطقهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says one group answered willingly and another answered unwillingly out of fear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p284/r6.anchor: وقال السدي أجابته طائفة طائعين وطائفة كارهين تقية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r1.claim: Abu Amr reads both occurrences of the verb with ya; the other readers use ta.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو أن يقولوا أو يقولوا بالياء فيهما وقرأ الباقون بالتاء فيهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r2.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r2.claim: Abu Ali supports Abu Amr's ya reading by the surrounding references to God taking the covenant and their saying yes; the ta reading follows the direct address to them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي حجة أبي عمرو قوله وإذ أخذ ربك وقوله قالوا بلى وحجة من قرأ بالتاء أنه قد جرى في الكلام خطاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r3.claim: The purpose clause means 'lest they say,' as in the expression 'lest it sway with you.'
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r3.anchor: ومعنى قوله يقولوا لئلا يقولوا مثله ﴿ أن تميد بكم ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r4.claim: One interpretation of 'we were heedless' refers to the covenant and acknowledgment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r4.anchor: وفي قوله ﴿ إنا كنا ﴾ قولان أحدهما أنه إشارة إلى الميثاق والإقرار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r5.claim: Another interpretation refers to knowing that God is the Creator.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r5.anchor: والثاني أنه إشارة إلى معرفة أنه الخالق قال المفسرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r6.claim: The verse reminds all accountable people of their covenant and argues against disbelievers who claim they forgot it; a truthful Prophet's report restores the proof, so forgetting does not defeat it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p285/r6.anchor: وهذه الآية تذكير من الله تعالى بما أخذ على جميع المكلفين من الميثاق واحتجاج عليهم لئلا يقول الكفار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r1.claim: God drew Adam's descendants from their ancestors' loins as witnesses that He is their Lord and master and that no deity exists but Him; He innately formed them this way.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى أنه استخرج ذرية بني آدم من أصلابهم، شاهدين على أنفسهم أن الله ربهم ومليكهم، وأنه لا إله إلا هو.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r2.claim: The Prophet teaches that every child is born upon the primordial disposition; parents make the child Jewish, Christian, or Zoroastrian, just as an animal is born whole.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r2.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "كل مولود يولد على الفطرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r3.speaker: عياض بن حمار عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r3.claim: In a report from God, the Prophet says God created His servants upright and Satan diverted them from their religion, prohibiting what God had made lawful.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r3.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم، عن عياض بن حمار قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يقول الله [تعالى] (3) إني خلقت عبادي حنفاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r4.speaker: الأسود بن سريع عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r4.claim: Al-Aswad reports that the Prophet rebuked people for taking children after killing combatants, saying every newborn begins on the primordial disposition and remains so until speech distinguishes them; parents then make them Jewish or Christian.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r4.anchor: عن الأسود بن سريع من بني سعد، قال: غزوت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أربع غزوات، قال: فتناول القوم الذرية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r5.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r5.claim: Al-Hasan invokes this verse as God's statement of the primordial disposition, in connection with the report from al-Aswad; Ibn Kathir notes parallel transmissions by Ahmad and al-Nasa'i.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p500/r5.anchor: قال الحسن: والله لقد قال الله في كتابه: {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم [وأشهدهم على أنفسهم] } (7) الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r1.claim: Reports describe God extracting Adam's descendants, distinguishing the people of the right from the left, and in some accounts making them testify that He is their Lord.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r1.anchor: وقد وردت أحاديث في أخذ الذرية من صلب آدم، عليه السلام، وتمييزهم إلى أصحاب اليمين و [إلى] (3) أصحاب الشمال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r2.claim: The Prophet says a person in Hell would surrender the whole earth to escape; God reminds him that He had required in Adam's back that he associate nothing with Him, but he refused.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r2.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يقال للرجل من أهل النار يوم القيامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r3.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r3.claim: The Prophet says God took the covenant from Adam's back at Na'man, meaning Arafah, brought forth all descendants, and addressed them with the testimony and warning in these verses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس [رضي الله عنهما] (8) عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن الله أخذ الميثاق من ظهر آدم، عليه السلام، بنعمان.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r4.speaker: الحاكم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r4.claim: Al-Hakim judges the Ibn Abbas narration's chain sound, although it is not included in the two Sahih collections.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p501/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers the more numerous and stronger transmissions that stop the covenant report at Ibn Abbas rather than raising it to the Prophet.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God brought Adam's descendants from his back as tiny particles while he was in a state described as being in water.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r1.anchor: عن أبي جمرة الضبعي، عن ابن عباس [رضي الله عنهما] (2) قال: أخرج الله ذرية آدم [عليه السلام] (3) من ظهره كهيئة الذر،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r2.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r2.claim: When his six-day-old son died, al-Dahhak instructed Jabir to uncover the child's face and loosen his shroud because the child would be seated and questioned.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r2.anchor: قال: مات ابن للضحاك بن مزاحم، [وهو] (4) ابن ستة أيام. قال: فقال: يا جابر، إذا أنت وضعت ابني في لحده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says Ibn Abbas taught that God drew every soul from Adam, took a covenant to worship Him alone, guaranteed provision, then returned them to Adam; fulfilling or failing a later covenant determines whether the first benefits a person, while a child dying before it remains on the first covenant and primordial disposition.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r3.anchor: قال: حدثني ابن عباس [رضي الله عنه] (7) ؛ أن الله مسح صلب آدم فاستخرج منه كل نسمة هو خلقها (8)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir concludes that these transmission routes together strengthen the report as a statement of Ibn Abbas, not a prophetic narration.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r4.anchor: فهذه الطرق كلها مما تقوي وقف هذا على ابن عباس، والله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r5.claim: The Prophet compares extracting descendants from Adam's back to combing hair from a head, then recounts their answer to God's question and the angels' testimony.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r1.claim: Ahmad ibn Abi Tayba was Abu Muhammad al-Jurjani, judge of Qumis, and was known for asceticism; al-Nasa'i included his narrations in his Sunan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r1.anchor: أحمد بن أبي طيبة هذا هو: أبو محمد الجرجاني قاضي قومس، كان أحد الزهاد، أخرج له النسائي في سننه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم الرازي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r2.claim: Abu Hatim says Ahmad ibn Abi Tayba's reports may be written down.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم الرازي: يكتب حديثه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r3.speaker: ابن عدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r3.claim: Ibn Adi says most of Ahmad ibn Abi Tayba's reports are oddities.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عدي: حدث بأحاديث أكثرها (14) غرائب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد عن عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r4.claim: A route through Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi transmits the account as Abdullah ibn Amr's own statement; Jarir also transmits it from Mansur.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r4.anchor: عن منصور، عن مجاهد، عن عبد الله بن عمرو، قوله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir considers the version stopping at Abdullah ibn Amr more authentic.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r6.claim: Answering Umar about the verse, the Prophet says God drew two groups from Adam: one destined for Paradise and its deeds, another for Fire and its deeds; each is enabled to perform the deeds by which they die and enter their destination.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p502#2/r6.anchor: فقال عمر بن الخطاب: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، سئل عنها، فقال: "إن الله خلق آدم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r1.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the Umar narration as hasan and notes Muslim ibn Yasar did not hear directly from Umar; Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'ah agree, and Abu Hatim adds Na'im ibn Rabi'ah between them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r1.anchor: قال الترمذي: وهذا حديث حسن، ومسلم بن يسار لم يسمع (7) عمر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r2.speaker: أبو داود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r2.claim: Abu Dawud's fuller chain identifies Na'im ibn Rabi'ah as the intermediary, present when Umar was asked about the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r2.anchor: زاد أبو حاتم: وبينهما نعيم بن ربيعة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r3.speaker: الدارقطني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r3.claim: Al-Daraqutni notes that Abu Firwa al-Rahawi corroborates Ibn Ja'tham and prefers both versions over Malik's version.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r3.anchor: وقد تابع عمر بن جعثم بن زيد بن سنان أبو فروة الرهاوي، وقولهما أولى بالصواب من قول مالك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir infers that Malik intentionally omitted Na'im because his status was unknown, and says Malik often omits narrators he does not accept, mursalizes raised reports, and disconnects connected ones.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r4.anchor: إنما أسقط ذكر "نعيم بن ربيعة" عمدا؛ لما جهل حاله ولم يعرفه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r5.claim: The Prophet says God wiped Adam's back, brought forth his descendants with light between their eyes, and showed them to Adam; Adam admired David, agreed to give him forty years of his own sixty, then denied the gift when death came, and his descendants inherited his forgetfulness and error.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p503/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة [رضي الله عنه] (1) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لما خلق الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r1.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhi calls the Adam-and-David narration hasan sahih and says it comes through multiple routes from Abu Hurayra.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r1.anchor: ثم قال الترمذي: هذا حديث حسن صحيح، وقد روي من غير وجه عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r2.speaker: الحاكم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r2.claim: Al-Hakim says the Abu Nu'aym transmission meets Muslim's conditions, though Muslim did not include it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r2.anchor: ورواه الحاكم في مستدركه، من حديث أبي نعيم الفضل بن دكين، به. وقال: صحيح على شرط مسلم ولم يخرجاه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r3.claim: An alternate report adds that Adam saw descendants with illnesses and asked why; God said this was so they would give thanks. Adam also saw the prophets' light, then the report recounts David's lifespan episode.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r3.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار، عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فذكر نحو ما تقدم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r4.speaker: هشام بن حكيم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r4.claim: Asked whether deeds are initiated or already decreed, the Prophet says God took Adam's descendants, made them testify, and divided them into groups for Paradise or Fire, each enabled for that group's deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r4.anchor: عن هشام بن حكيم، رضي الله عنه، أن رجلا سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله، أتبدأ الأعمال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r5.speaker: أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r5.claim: A weak report says God took the people of the right and left, had both affirm His lordship, then mixed them together; each would perform deeds, before all were returned to Adam's loins.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p504/r5.anchor: حديث آخر: روى جعفر بن الزبير -وهو ضعيف -عن القاسم، عن أبي أمامة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r1.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b describes God gathering all descendants through Judgment Day as spirits, forming and addressing them, taking their covenant and acknowledgment that He alone is God, and promising messengers and scriptures to remind them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية، عن أبي بن كعب [رضي الله عنه] (3) في قول الله تعالى (4) {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r2.claim: In Ubayy's account Adam sees descendants varied in wealth, poverty, and appearance, asks God to make them equal, and is told God loves to be thanked.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r2.anchor: فرأى فيهم الغني والفقير، وحسن الصورة ودون ذلك. فقال: يا رب، لو سويت بين عبادك؟ قال: إني أحببت أن أشكر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r3.claim: Ubayy's account says the prophets, seen shining like lamps, received a separate covenant of messengership and prophethood, linked to the covenant God took from the prophets.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r3.anchor: ورأى فيهم الأنبياء مثل السرج عليهم النور، وخصوا بميثاق آخر من الرسالة والنبوة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir connects the primordial disposition in this account with the command to follow the upright religion, and also invokes the earlier warning and the failure of most people to keep a covenant.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r4.anchor: وهو الذي يقول: {فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرة الله [التي فطر الناس عليها لا تبديل لخلق الله] }

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir says similar accounts are transmitted from Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and other early scholars.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p505/r5.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد، وعكرمة، وسعيد بن جبير، والحسن، وقتادة، والسدي، وغير واحد من علماء السلف، سياقات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir concludes that the reports show God extracted Adam's descendants from his loins and distinguished the people of Paradise from the people of Fire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r1.anchor: فهذه الأحاديث دالة على أن الله، عز وجل، استخرج ذرية آدم من صلبه، وميز بين أهل الجنة وأهل النار،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir says the explicit testimony that God is Lord appears only in the reports of Kulthum ibn Jabr from Ibn Abbas and Abdullah ibn Amr, and he has established that both stop at the Companion rather than the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r2.anchor: وأما الإشهاد عليهم هناك بأنه ربهم، فما هو إلا في حديث كلثوم بن جبر (1) عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r3.claim: Some early and later interpreters, including al-Hasan, understand the testimony as God creating people with innate monotheism, supported by the reports of Abu Hurayra, Iyad ibn Himar, and al-Hasan from al-Aswad ibn Sari'.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r3.anchor: ومن ثم قال قائلون من السلف والخلف: إن المراد بهذا الإشهاد إنما هو فطرهم على التوحيد، كما تقدم في حديث أبي هريرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r4.claim: The wording speaks of Adam's children and their descendants' backs, rather than Adam's single back; descendants means generation following generation, as in the cited verses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r4.anchor: ولهذا قال: {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم} ولم يقل: "من آدم"، {من ظهورهم} ولم يقل: "من ظهره"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir says making them testify can mean creating them as witnesses by their condition and words; testimony may be spoken or circumstantial, and questioning may likewise be verbal or by circumstance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r5.anchor: أي: أوجدهم شاهدين بذلك، قائلين له حالا وقالا. والشهادة تارة تكون بالقول،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r6.claim: He argues that if the testimony were a literal event everyone would remember it; since this verse stands as an independent proof against shirk, its force is the innate acknowledgment of God's oneness, while deniers would reject a report from the messengers anyway.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r6.anchor: فلو كان قد وقع هذا كما قاله من قال (6) لكان كل أحد يذكره، ليكون حجة عليه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r7.claim: The testimony prevents people from claiming ignorance of monotheism or blaming their fathers' association of partners for their own belief.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p506/r7.anchor: ولهذا قال: {أن يقولوا} (7) أي: لئلا يقولوا يوم القيامة: {إنا كنا عن هذا} أي: [عن] (8) التوحيد {غافلين أو تقولوا إنما أشرك آباؤنا} (9) الآية.

JISHUMI:v4p2772/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r1.claim: These readers pronounce the descendants word as a plural, with an alif and kasra on the tāʾ.
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: من ظهورهم ذرياتهم بالألف وكسر التاء على الجمع

JISHUMI:v4p2772/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r2.claim: These readers use the singular form, without an alif and with fatḥa on the tāʾ.
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي: ذريتهم بغير ألف وفتح التاء على الواحد

JISHUMI:v4p2772/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r3.claim: Abu Amr reads “that they say” with yāʾ as a report about them; the other readers use tāʾ for direct address in both instances.
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: شهدنا أن يقولوا بالياء على الخبر عنهم، وقرأ الباقون بالتاء فيهما على الخطاب

JISHUMI:v4p2772/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r4.claim: Dhurriyya is a collective whose plural is dhurriyyāt; it is also analyzed on the pattern faʿīliyya, like qamariyya, and linked to dharr because of smallness.
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r4.anchor: الذرية جمعها ذريات، وذرية قيل فعلية نحو قمرية، وأصله من الذر، شبه به لصغرهم

JISHUMI:v4p2772/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r5.claim: Another proposed etymology connects the descendants to their emergence from the loins like tiny ants.
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r5.anchor: وقيل: لأنهم يخرجون من الأصلاب كالذر

JISHUMI:v4p2772/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r6.claim: A further etymology derives the word from God's creating the creatures, using dharaʾa.
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو من ذرأ الله الخلق أي: خلقهم

JISHUMI:v4p2772/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r8.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r8.claim: The governing verb for “when” is omitted and understood as “remember.”
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r8.anchor: العامل في قوله: وإذ قيل محذوف، وتقديره: واذكر، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v4p2772/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r9.claim: The plural “their descendants” is genitive as the object of “took,” whereas the singular form is accusative.
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r9.anchor: وكسرنا ذرياتهم؛ لأنه مفعول (أخذ)، فيكسر في الجمع، وينصب في الواحد

JISHUMI:v4p2772/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r12.claim: One account links the verse to the monotheistic proofs before the prophetic narratives, including God's creation and sending the winds, then sees it as a return to proofs of oneness and condemnation of idolatry.
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r12.anchor: تتصل بدلائل التوحيد المذكورة قبل قصص الأنبياء

JISHUMI:v4p2772/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r13.claim: Another account connects this covenant with the preceding covenant requiring the Children of Israel to act by the Torah, then extends the covenant to all Adam's descendants.
JISHUMI:v4p2772/r13.anchor: يتصل بما قبله من أخذ الميثاق على بني إسرائيل بأن يعملوا بالتوراة، ثم عقبه بأخذ الميثاق على جميع بني آدم

JISHUMI:v4p2775/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r3.speaker: أصحاب الحديث
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r3.claim: Hadith transmitters report that God extracted Adam's descendants in two groups, assigning one to Paradise and one to Hell; in a prophetic report, a man asks what deeds are for, while Umar's version asks why people were sent, and the Prophet answers that each is facilitated for what he was created for.
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r3.anchor: يرويه أصحاب الحديث عن أسلافهم من الآثار موقوفة ومرفوعة ويجعلون ذلك تأويلا للآية

JISHUMI:v4p2775/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r4.claim: A report attributed to Abu Hurayra says every soul to be created until Resurrection fell from Adam's back; Adam was shown his descendants, saw David's light, gave him forty years of his own lifespan, then denied the recorded gift and his descendants denied it.
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r4.anchor: ورووا في حديث أبي هريرة: أنه مسح ظهره فسقط من ظهره كل نسمة هو خالقها إلى يوم القيامة

JISHUMI:v4p2775/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r5.claim: Another report says the descendants were made like ants and answered the divine question affirmatively and obediently.
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r5.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات أخذ مثل الذر فقال: ألست بربكم؟ قالوا: بلى طائعين طائعين

JISHUMI:v4p2775/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r6.claim: A report predicts that the Hour will not come until everyone whose covenant was taken has been born.
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r6.anchor: ورووا أنه لا تقوم الساعة حتى يولد كل من أخذ ميثاقه

JISHUMI:v4p2775/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r7.claim: One report has God extract white descendants from Adam's right side for Paradise by mercy and black descendants from his left for Hell, identifying them with the people of the right and left.
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r7.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار: أنه أخرج من صفحة ظهره اليمنى ذرية بيضاء، وقال لهم: ادخلوا الجنة برحمتي

JISHUMI:v4p2775/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r8.claim: One reported location for the covenant is ʿArafa.
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r8.anchor: واختلفوا في أي موضع كان، قيل: بعرفة

JISHUMI:v4p2775/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r9.claim: Another reported location for the covenant is India.

JISHUMI:v4p2775/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r10.claim: Another reported location for the covenant is heaven.

JISHUMI:v4p2775/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2775/r11.claim: Another reported location for the covenant is between Mecca and Taif.

NAHHAS:v2p161/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p161/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p161/r1.claim: Some interpret the covenant as God drawing Adam's descendants from one another's backs and showing them His oneness through creation, which every adult necessarily recognizes.
NAHHAS:v2p161/r1.anchor: قال قوم إن معنى وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذرياتهم أخرج من ظهور بني آدم بعضهم من بعضهم

NAHHAS:v2p161/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p161/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
NAHHAS:v2p161/r2.claim: In the report from ʿUmar, the Prophet says God wiped Adam's back, extracted a group destined for Paradise and another destined for Fire, and assigned each group its people's deeds.
NAHHAS:v2p161/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله جل وعز خلق آدم فمسح ظهره بيمينه فاستخرج منه ذرية فقال خلقت هؤلاء للجنة

NAHHAS:v2p161/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p161/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
NAHHAS:v2p161/r3.claim: Asked why deeds matter, the Prophet replies that God directs each person to the deeds of the destiny assigned to them until death and final entry into Paradise or Fire.
NAHHAS:v2p161/r3.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله إذا خلق العبد للجنة استعمله بعمل أهل الجنة حتى يموت على عمل أهل الجنة

NAHHAS:v2p161/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p161/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p161/r4.claim: Abū Jaʿfar says the verse remains difficult, then argues that the reported outcome is not injustice because God already knows what the person will do.
NAHHAS:v2p161/r4.anchor: قال أبو جعفر والآية مع هذا مشكلة ونحن نتقصى ما فيها قال بعض العلماء هي مخصوصة

NAHHAS:v2p161/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p161/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p161/r5.claim: Some scholars limit the verse by its wording about descendants from backs and by the following mention of ancestors who practiced idolatry.
NAHHAS:v2p161/r5.anchor: قال بعض العلماء هي مخصوصة لأن الله جل وعز قال من بني آدم من ظهورهم فخرج من هذا

NAHHAS:v2p161/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p161/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p161/r6.claim: Another view makes the verse universal: each person knows they were once a child, fed and raised, and therefore has a governor and creator; saying yes means this is incumbent on them.
NAHHAS:v2p161/r6.anchor: وقيل بل هي عامة لجميع الناس لأن كل أحد يعلم أنه كان طفلا فغذي وربي وأن له مدبرا وخالقا

NAHHAS:v2p161/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p161/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p161/r7.claim: A further view applies the covenant specifically to the descendants drawn from Adam's own loins.
NAHHAS:v2p161/r7.anchor: وقيل هذا لمن كان من ظهور بني آدم عليه السلام وقد علم أن ولد آدم عليه السلام لصلبه

NAHHAS:v2p161/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p161/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p161/r8.claim: The Medinans and Kufans read an taqūlū, while Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Muḥayṣin, ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read an yaqūlū.
NAHHAS:v2p161/r8.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وأهل الكوفة ( أن تقولوا ) بالتاء معجمة من فوق وقرأ عبد الله بن عباس

NAHHAS:v2p161/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p161/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p161/r9.claim: In both readings, an is accusative and means lest you say; the Kufans explain its force as so that you do not.
NAHHAS:v2p161/r9.anchor: و ( أن ) في موضع نصب في القراءتين جميعا بمعنى كراهة أن وعند الكوفيين بمعنى لئلا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r1.claim: 'From their backs' is a partitive apposition to 'the children of Adam.'
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r1.anchor: بدل من بني آدم بدل البعض من الكل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r2.claim: Taking their descendants from their backs means bringing offspring out of their loins and making them testify about themselves.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r2.anchor: إخراجهم من أصلابهم نسلا وإشهادهم على أنفسهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r3.claim: The dialogue is representational: God established proofs of His lordship and oneness, which the intellects and insights He built into people recognize.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r3.anchor: قوله : { ألست بربكم قالوا بلى شهدنا } من باب التمثيل والتخييلا ومعنى ذلك أنه نصب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r4.claim: Their reason and insight distinguish error from guidance, so it is as though God made them testify and ask whether He is their Lord.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r4.anchor: وشهدت بها عقولهم وبصائرهم التي ركبها فيهم وجعلها مميزة بين الضلالة والهدى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r5.claim: The imagined answer is an affirmation that God is their Lord and that they acknowledge His oneness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r5.anchor: وكأنهم قالوا : بلى أنت ربنا ، شهدنا على أنفسنا وأقررنا بوحدانيتك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r6.claim: Such representational speech is common in divine, Prophetic, and Arabic expression; the Qur'an's address to heaven and earth is another example.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r6.anchor: وباب التمثيل واسع في كلام الله تعالى ورسوله عليه الصلاة السلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r7.claim: The poetic image of bodily parts speaking likewise represents meaning rather than actual speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r7.anchor: إذ قالت الأنساع للبطن الحق قالت له ريح الصبا قرقار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r8.claim: The purpose of establishing rational proofs is to prevent people from claiming on Judgment Day that they were unaware of them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r8.anchor: أي فعلنا ذلك من نصب الأدلة الشاهدة على صحتها العقول ، كراهة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r14.claim: A reading has the singular ذُرِّيَّتَهُ; another reads أن يقولوا with yāʾ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p166/r14.anchor: وقرىء : ( ذريتهم ) على التوحيد . وأن يقولوا : بالياء

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r1.claim: One theory says God extracted the souls before bodies were created and gave them the knowledge needed to understand His address.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r1.anchor: أنه أخرج الأرواح قبل خلق الأجساد وجعل فيها من المعرفة ما علمت به من خاطبها

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r2.claim: On that theory, some place the event in Paradise before Adam's descent to earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r2.anchor: أنه كان في الجنة قبل هبوطه إلى الأرض

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r3.claim: Others place it after Adam had descended to earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r3.anchor: أنه فعل ذلك بعد هبوطه إليها

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r4.claim: A second theory holds that God created souls and bodies together on earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r4.anchor: أنه خلق الأرواح والأجساد معا وذلك في الأرض

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r5.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say God stroked Adam's back between Mecca and Taif: white particles emerged on the right, the people of the right; black particles emerged on the left, the people of the left, and all testified before being returned.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r5.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل : وذلك أن الله مسح ظهر آدم بين مكة والطائف فخرج من صفحة ظهره اليمنى ذرية كالذر بيض

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r6.claim: Another interpretation says God brought the offspring out generation after generation, age after age.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r6.anchor: أنه أخرج الذرية قرنا بعد قرن وعصرا بعد عصر

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r7.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r7.claim: Some theologians say God showed people their own selves and His power, thereby making them testify to His lordship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r7.anchor: أنه دلهم على أنفسهم بما شهدوه من قدرته , قاله بعض المتكلمين

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r8.claim: Alternatively, the testimony was their confession that God alone is Lord and one.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r8.anchor: هو إشهادهم على أنفسهم بما اعترفوا من ربوبيته ووحدانيته

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r9.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r9.claim: Ibn Bahr says the address was to Adam's fathers when their offspring were drawn from them, demonstrating that God created them after nonexistence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r9.anchor: أنه قال ذلك للآباء من بني آدم حين أخرج من ظهورهم ذرياتهم وأشهدهم على أنفسهم ألست بربكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r10.claim: The majority say the address was to the offspring when God took them from their fathers' backs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r10.anchor: أنه قال ذلك للذرية حين أخذهم من ظهور آبائهم , وهذا قول الأكثرين

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r11.claim: One view says God addressed them through prophets after their reason had matured.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r11.anchor: أنه قال لهم : { ألست بربكم } على لسان الأنبياء بعد أن كملت عقولهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r12.claim: Alternatively, God gave them reason by which they knew this and testified themselves.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r12.anchor: أنه جعل لهم عقولا علموا بها ذلك فشهدوا به على أنفسهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r13.claim: The word dhurriyya may derive from their emerging from the loins like tiny particles.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r14.claim: Alternatively, it derives from God bringing creation into being and making it manifest.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p277/r14.anchor: أنه مأخوذ من ذرأ الله الخلق إذا أحدثهم وأظهرهم

MUQATIL:7:172/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:172/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:172/r1.claim: God took Adam's descendants from their backs at Nuʿmān near ʿArafāt and made them acknowledge themselves.
MUQATIL:7:172/r1.anchor: يقول: وقد أخذ ربك من بنى آدم بنعمان عند عرفات

MUQATIL:7:172/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:172/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:172/r2.claim: God rubbed Adam's right back and brought out white descendants like moving specks, then his left and brought out black descendants like specks, comprising a thousand communities.
MUQATIL:7:172/r2.anchor: مسح صفحة ظهر آدم اليمنى، فأخرج منه ذرية بيضاء كهيئة الذر يتحركون، ثم مسح صفحة ظهره اليسرى، فأخرج منه ذرية سوداء كهيئة الذر، وهم ألف أمة

MUQATIL:7:172/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:172/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:172/r3.claim: God told Adam these were his descendants and that their covenant required worshipping Him alone without partners, and concerned their provision; Adam assented.
MUQATIL:7:172/r3.anchor: يا آدم، هؤلاء ذريتك أخذنا ميثاقهم على أن يعبدوني ولا يشركوا بي شيئا وعلى رزقهم، قال آدم: نعم يا رب

MUQATIL:7:172/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:172/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:172/r4.claim: God asked whether He was their Lord, they answered yes, and the angels witnessed their acknowledgment.
MUQATIL:7:172/r4.anchor: قال الله للملائكة: اشهدوا عليهم بالإقرار، قالت الملائكة: قد شهدنا

MUQATIL:7:172/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:172/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:172/r5.claim: God invokes this covenant against Arab disbelievers in this world so they cannot claim on Judgment Day that they were unaware of it.

MUQATIL:7:173-174/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:173-174/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:173-174/r3.claim: God sorted Adam's descendants as by lots: the white were promised Paradise by His mercy and the right side, while the black were assigned the Fire and the left side.
MUQATIL:7:173-174/r3.anchor: ثم أفاضهم إفاضة القدح، فقال للبيض: هؤلاء في الجنة برحمتي، فهم أصحاب اليمين، وأصحاب الميمنة، وقال للسود: هؤلاء للنار، ولا أبالي

NASAFI-FULL:v2p45#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p45#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p45#3/r1.claim: The opening إذ means “remember when”; من ظهورهم is an apposition to بني آدم, meaning from the backs of Adam's descendants, and the offspring are extracted from their fathers' loins.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p45#3/r1.anchor: ومعنى أخذ ذرياتهم من ظهورهم إخراجهم من أصلاب آبائهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p45#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p45#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p45#3/r2.claim: The testimony is illustrative: God set evidence of His lordship and unity before them, and their implanted rational faculties witnessed it by distinguishing guidance from error, as though He had asked and they acknowledged His unity.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p45#3/r2.anchor: هذا من بابا التمثيل ومعنى ذلك أنه نصب لهم الأدلة على ربوبيته ووحدانيته وشهدت بها عقولهم التى ركبها فيهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p45#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p45#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p45#3/r3.claim: The purpose is to prevent them from claiming on Judgment Day that they were unaware, since the evidence and their reason had alerted them.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p45#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p45#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p45#3/r4.claim: إنا كنا عن هذا غافلين means they might claim they had not been alerted to it.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r1.claim: The audience is told to recall, alongside earlier covenant reminders in scripture, the covenant taken from servants on the primordial day.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r1.anchor: أي واذكر لهم مع ما سبق من تذكير المواثيق في كتابهم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi calls this a difficult verse that scholars have discussed in interpretation and implications.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r2.anchor: وقد تكلم العلماء في تأويلها وأحكامها،

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r3.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r3.claim: One group says God brought descendants forth from one another and creation showed His oneness, since every adult necessarily knows there is one Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r3.anchor: فقال قوم: معنى الآية أن الله تعالى أخرج

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r4.speaker: القفال
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r4.claim: Al-Qaffal treats God’s address as testimony and the response as confession, analogizing it to the heavens and earth answering willingly.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r5.claim: Another view says God created the souls before the bodies and placed in them knowledge by which they understood His address.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r5.anchor: إنه سبحانه أخرج الأرواح قبل خلق الأجساد،

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r6.claim: Al-Qurtubi says prophetic hadith gives another account: God brought forth bodily forms containing spirits from Adam’s back.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم غير هذين القولين

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r7.claim: In the report Umar heard the Prophet explain that God extracted descendants from Adam, assigning one group to Paradise and one to Hell; each is enabled to do the deeds of its destination until death.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172/r7.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسأل عنها. فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r1.claim: Abu Umar calls the Umar-to-Prophet report disconnected because Muslim ibn Yasar did not meet Umar.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عمر: هذا حديث منقطع الإسناد لأن مسلم بن يسار لم يلق عمر.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r2.speaker: يحيى بن معين
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r2.claim: Yahya ibn Maʿin says Muslim ibn Yasar is unknown and Nuʿaym ibn Rabiʿa is not known for transmitting knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r2.anchor: وقال فيه يحيى بن معين: مسلم بن يسار لا يعرف،

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r3.claim: Though that chain is weak, al-Qurtubi says the meaning is sound through many established routes from the Prophet via several Companions.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r3.anchor: لكن معنى هذا الحديث قد صح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r4.claim: A report al-Tirmidhi authenticates says Adam’s descendants were drawn from his back and marked by light; Adam recognized David and gave him forty years from his own lifespan.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r4.anchor: روى الترمذي وصححه عن أبي هريرة قال إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r5.claim: Adam later denied giving David forty years, and his descendants inherited his denial and forgetfulness.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r6.claim: A version outside al-Tirmidhi adds that God ordered the covenant to be written and witnesses to be present.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r6.anchor: في غير الترمذي: فحينئذ أمر بالكتاب والشهود.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r7.claim: Another version describes descendants as unequal in condition; Adam asks why they were not made equal, and God says He intended to be thanked.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r7.anchor: في رواية: فرأى فيهم الضعيف والغني والفقير والذليل

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r8.claim: Ibn Amr transmits the Prophet’s comparison that the descendants were taken from Adam’s back as hair is combed from a head.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r8.anchor: وروى عبد الله بن عمرو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r9.claim: The account says God gave them intellects like Solomon’s ant and took their acknowledgment that He alone is Lord and deity.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r9.anchor: وجعل الله لهم عقولا كنملة سليمان.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r10.claim: They accepted the covenant, were told that messengers would be sent, and testified for one another.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r10.anchor: وأعلمهم بأنه سيبعث إليهم الرسل فشهد بعضهم على بعض.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r11.speaker: أبي بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r11.claim: Ubayy ibn Kab says the seven heavens were witnesses and every person born through the end of time received the covenant.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r11.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب: وأشهد عليهم السموات السبع

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas places the covenant at Batn Nuʿman, a valley beside Arafa.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r12.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: ببطن نعمان، واد إلى جنب عرفة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r13.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas locates it at Rahba in India, where Adam descended.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r13.anchor: وروى عنه أن ذلك برهبا أرض بالهند

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas, quoted by Yahya ibn Sallam, says Adam was sent down in India and every soul destined to exist was extracted from his back.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r14.anchor: وقال يحيى بن سلام قال ابن عباس في هذه الآية:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r15.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r15.claim: Al-Hasan says the extracted descendants were then returned to Adam’s loins.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r15.anchor: قال يحيى قال الحسن: ثم أعادهم في صلب آدم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r16.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r16.claim: Al-Kalbi locates the covenant between Mecca and Taif.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r17.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r17.claim: Al-Suddi places it in the lowest heaven after Adam descended from Paradise; God drew white descendants from his right side for Paradise and black ones from his left for Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r17.anchor: وقال السدي: في السماء الدنيا حين أهبط من الجنة إليها

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r18.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r18.claim: Ibn Jurayj says every soul destined for Paradise emerged white and every soul destined for Hell emerged black.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r18.anchor: قال ابن جريج: خرجت كل نفس مخلوقة للجنة بيضاء

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r19.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172#2/r19.claim: Ibn al-Arabi poses the objection that God seems to punish people who have not sinned or punish them for what He decreed and led them to do.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r1.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r1.claim: Ibn al-Arabi answers that human limits come from a superior commander while God is answerable to none; creatures cannot be analogized to the Creator, all acts belong to God, and human objections arise from natural sympathy and hope of praise or benefit.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r1.anchor: قلنا: لأن فوقه آمرا يأمره وناهيا ينهاه،

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r2.claim: Some restrict the covenant to certain descendants: the wording excludes Adam’s direct offspring, while the later excuse about fathers excludes people without idolatrous ancestors.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r2.anchor: فقيل: الآية خاصة لأنه تعالى قال: { من بني آدم من ظهورهم } فخرج

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r3.claim: Another restriction confines it to those who received the covenant through the tongues of prophets.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r3.anchor: وقيل: هي مخصوصة فيمن أخذ عليه العهد على ألسنة الأنبياء.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r4.claim: Others say the covenant is general because everyone knows they began as a child who was fed and raised and must have a creator and governor.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r4.anchor: وقيل: بل هي عامة لجميع الناس لأن كل أحد يعلم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r5.claim: On the general reading, witnessing oneself means recognizing a creator, and saying yes is an admission of what is incumbent on everyone.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r6.claim: After people forgot their acknowledgment, God reminded them through prophets, culminating in the Prophet, to establish proof; the text cites the command to remind and says God then empowered him and established his religion on earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r6.anchor: فلما اعترف الخلق لله سبحانه بأنه الرب ثم ذهلوا عنه ذكرهم بأنبيائه

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r7.speaker: الطرطوشي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r7.claim: Al-Tartushi says the covenant remains binding even when people do not remember it, like a divorce witnessed against someone who later forgets it.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r7.anchor: قال الطرطوشي: إن هذا العهد يلزم البشر

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi says children who die young enter Paradise through their first-covenant acknowledgment; the view that children of polytheists are in Paradise is correct despite disputed reports.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r8.anchor: وهذا القائل يقول: أطفال المشركين في الجنة، وهو الصحيح في الباب.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r9.claim: Grammatically, from their backs is an appositional specification of from the children of Adam; Adam is omitted because all are known to be his descendants and drawn from his back.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r9.anchor: من ظهورهم } بدل اشتمال من قوله { من بني آدم }.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r10.claim: Kufan readers and Ibn Kathir read offspring in the singular, which can denote either one child or many.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:172-173/r10.anchor: { ذريتهم } قرأ الكوفيون وابن كثير بالتوحيد وفتح التاء، وهي تقع للواحد والجمع

QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r4.claim: The other readers use the plural because many successive generations came from Adam’s descendants, an immense number known only to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون «ذرياتهم» بالجمع، لأن الذرية لما كانت تقع للواحد

QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r6.claim: Abu Amr reads both so that you say and or you say with the third-person ya, matching the surrounding third-person wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r6.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو بالياء فيهما. ردهما على لفظ الغيبة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r7.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r7.claim: Other readers use second-person ta, matching the direct address and response earlier in the passage.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r7.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالتاء فيهما ردوه على لفظ الخطاب المتقدم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r8.claim: One reading makes the angels speakers of we testified: after people affirm, angels testify so they cannot later claim ignorance.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r9.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r9.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi say God told the angels to witness the people’s confession, preventing their later excuse.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ubayy ibn Kab instead take we testified as the children of Adam saying God is their Lord and deity.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وأبي بن كعب: قوله «شهدنا» هو من قول «بني آدم»

QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas also says the children witnessed for one another.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أشهد بعضهم على بعض فالمعنى

QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r12.claim: If angels speak, pause after bala; if Adam’s children speak, the pause is unsuitable because the purpose clause depends on God making them testify.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173-174/r12.anchor: فإذا كان ذلك من قول الملائكة فيوقف على «بلى» ولا يحسن الوقف عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:7:173/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173/r1.claim: The continued prophetic report compares descendants drawn from Adam to combing hair from the head, then has angels witness their affirmation so they cannot deny it later.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173/r1.anchor: أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذرياتهم كما يؤخذ بالمشط من الرأس

QURTUBI-FULL:7:173/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173/r2.speaker: مكي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173/r2.claim: Makkī selects the second-person reading because its meaning is sound and most readers use it.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173/r2.anchor: قال مكي: وهو الاختيار لصحة معناه،

QURTUBI-FULL:7:173/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173/r3.claim: Abu Malik says we testified is spoken by God and the angels, who bear witness to the people’s admission; al-Suddi also transmitted this view.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:173/r3.anchor: قاله أبو مالك، وروي عن السدي أيضا.

RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r1.claim: After Moses' story, Razi presents the covenant passage as establishing the proof against all morally responsible people.
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r1.anchor: لما شرح قصة موسى عليه السلام مع توابعها على أقصى الوجوه ذكر في هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r2.claim: Through Muslim ibn Yasar, Umar reports asking the Prophet about the verse: God extracted Adam's descendants, assigning some to paradise and its deeds and others to hell and its deeds; each is enabled in life for the destiny assigned.
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r2.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عنها فقال : ( إن الله سبحانه وتعالى خلق آدم

RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet said God passed His hand over Adam's back, and every soul of his descendants through the end of time fell from it.
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r3.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لما خلق الله آدم

RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r4.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r4.claim: Muqatil says God drew dustlike descendants from Adam, elicited their testimony; the white were destined for paradise by mercy and the black for hell, then all were returned to Adam's loins.
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل : ( إن الله مسح صفحة ظهر آدم سوداء كهيئة الذر فقال يآدم

RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r5.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك وعكرمة والكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r5.claim: Razi says many early commentators, including these authorities, adopted the literal primordial-covenant interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r5.anchor: وهذا القول قد ذهب إليه كثير من قدماء المفسرين كسعيد بن المسيب ، وسعيد بن جبير

RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Adam saw luminous descendants, including the prophets and the especially radiant David; Adam gave David forty years of his own thousand-year lifespan, later denying the gift when death came, after which each lifespan was recorded.
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أنه أبصر آدم في ذريته قوما لهم نور

RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r7.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r7.claim: The Mu'tazilites categorically reject interpreting the verse as a literal extraction of progeny and covenant from Adam's descendants.
RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r7.anchor: أما المعتزلة : فقد أطبقوا على أنه لا يجوز تفسير هذه الآية بهذا الوجه

RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r1.claim: Their first objection says the plural phrase from their backs means God took descendants from the backs of Adam's children, never saying He took them from Adam's own back.
RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r1.anchor: قوله : { من بنىءادم من ظهورهم } لا شك أن قوله : { من ظهورهم }

RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r2.claim: Their second objection says that if the extraction were from Adam alone, the verse would use singular back and descendants, not plural forms.
RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r2.anchor: أنه لو كان المرا أنه تعالى أخرج من ظهر آدم شيئا من الذرية لما قال : { من ظهورهم }

RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r4.claim: Their fourth objection says testimony requires rationality, and a rational person could not entirely forget such a momentous event; otherwise one must equally accept reincarnation despite no memory of previous bodies.
RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r4.anchor: أن أخذ الميثاق لا يمكن إلا من العاقل ، فلو أخذ الله الميثاق من أولئك الذر

RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r5.claim: They argue that the same no-memory reasoning used to refute reincarnation also refutes a forgotten primordial covenant, making the two positions alike.
RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r5.anchor: فإذا كان اعتمادنا في إبطال التناسخ ليس إلا على هذا الدليل

RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r1.claim: Their fifth objection is that the descendants of Adam together would occupy an immense volume that could not fit inside his small back.
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r1.anchor: أن جميع الخلق الذين خلقهم الله من أولاد آدم عدد عظيم وكثرة كثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r2.claim: Their sixth objection says bodily structure is necessary for life and reason, and that all descendants with the required bodies could not fit in the earthly space, much less Adam's loins.
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r2.anchor: أن البنية شرط لحصول الحياة والعقل والفهم

RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r3.claim: Their seventh objection asks whether the covenant was proof at the time or later: it could not entail reward or punishment then, and forgotten testimony cannot serve as proof during earthly life.
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r3.anchor: هذا الميثاق إما أن يكون قد أخذه الله منهم في ذلك الوقت ليصير حجة عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r4.speaker: الكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r4.claim: Al-Ka'bi argues that the descendants could not understand more than infants, who are not obligated, so they could not have been accountable at the covenant.
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r4.anchor: قال الكعبي : إن حال أولئك الذرية لا يكون أعلى في الفهم والعلم من حال الأطفال

RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r5.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj replies that God can grant understanding to creatures such as ants and mountains, citing their speech and praise, and likewise could make the primordial descendants rational.
RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r5.anchor: وأجاب الزجاج عنه فقال : لما لم يبعد أن يؤتى الله النمل العقل

RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r1.claim: Their ninth objection says that if the primordial descendants had full reason and ability, they were already accountable and would need a prior covenant, causing an impossible regress; if not, they could not receive the command.
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r1.anchor: أن أولئك الذر في ذلك الوقت إما أن يكونوا كاملي العقول والقدر

RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r2.claim: Their tenth objection cites the statement that humans were created from a gushing fluid: if they already existed as rational beings before that fluid, the Qur'anic claim would be false.
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى : { فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق * خلق من ماء دافق }

RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r3.claim: They reject the proposed reply that God made the descendants rational and later removed their faculties, because their emergence from sperm would then be a recreation, while Muslims agree it is initial creation.
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r3.anchor: قلنا : هذا باطل لأنه لو كان الأمر كذلك لما كان خلقه من النطفة خلقا على سبيل الابتداء

RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r4.claim: Their eleventh objection first says the extracted particles must be either these same people or others; the latter option is rejected by consensus.
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r4.anchor: أن تلك الذرات إما أن يقال هي عين هؤلاء الناس أو غيرهم والقول الثاني باطل بالإجماع

RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r5.claim: If they were the same people, they either remained conscious through sperm, embryo, and fetus, which is absurd, or did not; the latter entails four lives and three deaths, contrary to the Qur'an's two lives and two deaths.
RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r5.anchor: يقتضي أن يقال الإنسان حصل له الحياة أربع مرات

RAZI-FULL:v15p41#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p41#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p41#2/r1.claim: Rāzī's twelfth objection is that the accountable human is created through the reproductive stages named in scripture, not as primordial particles.
RAZI-FULL:v15p41#2/r1.anchor: فلو كان القول بهذا الذر صحيحا لكان ذلك الذر هو الإنسان لأنه هو المكلف المخاطب المثاب المعاقب

RAZI-FULL:v15p41#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p41#2/r2.speaker: أصحاب النظر وأرباب المعقولات
RAZI-FULL:v15p41#2/r2.claim: They take the extraction as ordinary offspring development, with God's signs making people answer as though they had spoken; this is figurative speech, not a voiced reply.
RAZI-FULL:v15p41#2/r2.anchor: فبالإشهاد صاروا كأنهم قالوا بلى ، وإن لم يكن هناك قول باللسان ، ولذلك نظائر

RAZI-FULL:v15p42/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p42/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p42/r1.claim: The covenant need not now be remembered: God creates necessary memories, and a pledge taken for an instant can be forgotten unlike experiences lasting for years.
RAZI-FULL:v15p42/r1.anchor: أما أخذ هذا الميثاق إنما حصل في أسرع زمان ، وأقل وقت فلم

RAZI-FULL:v15p42/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p42/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p42/r2.claim: The space objection fails if each particle is an indivisible living and rational substance; if the human is an immaterial rational soul, the spatial objection disappears altogether.
RAZI-FULL:v15p42/r2.anchor: عندنا البنية ليست شرطا لحصول الحياة ، والجوهر الفرد الذي لا يتجزأ ، قابل للحياة والعقل

RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r1.claim: God may do as He wills; as Muʿtazilites allow benefits from weighing deeds and speaking limbs, the pledge could help angels distinguish the blessed from the wretched.
RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r1.anchor: يفعل الله ما يشاء ويحكم ما يريد ، وأيضا أليس أن من المعتزلة إذا

RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r2.claim: Another answer is that God will remind people of the covenant on Resurrection Day.
RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r2.anchor: وقيل أيضا إن الله تعالى يذكرهم ذلك الميثاق يوم القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r3.claim: A sound report from the Messenger interprets the verse as the primordial extraction from Adam; Rāzī says this need not conflict with its wording.
RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r3.anchor: صحت الرواية عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه فسر هذه الآية بهذا الوجه

RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r4.claim: The Qur'an establishes extraction from successive descendants' backs, while the report adds extraction from Adam's back; accept both, since neither text excludes the other.
RAZI-FULL:v15p43/r4.anchor: وثبت إخراج الذرية من ظهر آدم بالخبر ، وعلى هذا التقدير : فلا منافاه بين الأمرين

RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r1.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r1.claim: These readers recite ذرياتهم as a plural; the remaining readers recite ذريتهم in the singular.
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر وأبو عمر و { * ذرياتهم } بالألف على الجمع

RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r2.speaker: الواحدي ويونس
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r2.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says dhurriyya can be singular or plural; either form is sound, and Yūnus prefers the plural, as broken plurals can themselves be pluralized.
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r2.anchor: قال الواحدي : الذرية تقع على الواحد والجمع

RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r3.claim: Those affirming the first covenant take the dialogue literally; those denying it understand the witnessing and answer as representation of the evidence for God's lordship.
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r3.anchor: أما على قول من أثبت الميثاق الأول فكل هذه الأشياء محمولة على ظواهرها ، وأما على قول من أنكره قال : إنها محمولة على التمثيل

RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r4.speaker: قائلون
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r4.claim: On one view, the offspring say “yes,” then God tells the angels to testify, so a pause after قالوا بلى is appropriate.
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r4.anchor: أنه من كلام الملائكة ، وذلك لأنهم لما قالوا { بلى } قال الله للملائكة اشهدوا فقالوا شهدنا

RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r5.speaker: الكوفيون والبصريون
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r5.claim: The Kufans supply an omitted “not” to mean “lest”; the Basrans read the clause as “for fear that,” explaining why the testimony was given.
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r5.anchor: هذا قول الكوفيين ، وعند البصريين تقريره : شهدنا كراهة أن يقولوا

RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r6.speaker: قائلون
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r6.claim: On the second view, شهدنا remains the offspring's speech and أن تقولوا attaches to God's making them testify, so no pause follows شهدنا.
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r6.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن قوله : { شهدنا } من بقية كلام الذرية

RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads أن يقولوا in the third person both times, following the preceding third-person discourse; both person choices are sound because the absent group is addressed in meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v15p43#2/r7.anchor: فقرأ أبو عمرو بالياء جميعا ، لأن الذي تقدم من الكلام على الغيبة

RAZI-FULL:v15p44/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p44/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p44/r4.claim: A third view says human spirits existed before bodies and inherently know God, without acquiring that knowledge through inquiry.
RAZI-FULL:v15p44/r4.anchor: وهو أن الأرواح البشرية موجودة قبل الأبدان ، والإقرار بوجود الإله من لوازم ذواتها

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r3.claim: The shared primordial human story is connected with the pretemporal covenant in which all humanity witnessed to God’s Lordship.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r3.anchor: where all human beings bear witness to God’s Lordship in a pretemporal covenant:

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r1.claim: The verse is central to Islamic sacred history and anthropology, locating humanity’s basic relation to God in direct recognition of His Lordship before earthly life.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r1.anchor: This verse is in many ways the cornerstone of Islamic sacred history and anthropology and establishes that the fundamental relationship between God and all human beings is premised upon the simple, unmediated recognition of His Lordship

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r2.claim: The event is widely called a pretemporal covenant or pact, though neither term occurs in the verse, and is made with all humanity before earthly existence.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r2.anchor: widely referred to as a pretemporal covenant

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r3.speaker: Commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r3.claim: Commentators connect it with God’s pretemporal covenant with the prophets.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r3.anchor: It is connected by commentators with a pretemporal covenant between God and the prophets (3:81; 33:7)

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r4.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r4.claim: Some consider the humanity-wide covenant subsequent to the prophets’ covenant.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r4.anchor: and considered by some to be subsequent to it (ST).

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r5.claim: The Quran also names covenants with believers generally.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r5.anchor: The Quran mentions covenants or pacts between God and the believers generally (5:1, 7; 6:152; 13:20, 25; 16:91, 95; 57:8)

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r6.claim: The Quran names covenants with Abraham and the Israelites.

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r7.claim: The Quran names covenants with Christians and the People of the Book collectively.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r7.anchor: the Christians (5:14), and the People of the Book collectively (3:187).

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r8.claim: This direct, universal covenant is unmediated and can ground later, specific covenants mediated by prophets.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r8.anchor: the making of the covenant described in the present verse is unmediated and universal—contracted directly between God and all humanity—and can thus be interpreted as the basis of all later and specific covenants mediated by the prophets.

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r9.speaker: Commentators
