STUDYQURAN:7:172/r9.claim: Commentators connect the verse to fiṭrah, the primordial nature originally given to all humans, in which innate recognition of God’s Oneness is humanity’s essence.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r9.anchor: This verse is also connected with the Quranic notion of the fiṭrah (IK,Ṭ), the primordial nature (30:30) with which all human beings were originally endowed, indicating that the innate recognition of God’s Oneness constitutes the essence of being human

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r10.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r10.claim: Although people do not remember the covenant, their testimony leaves an indelible imprint and establishes moral responsibility.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r10.anchor: Even though human beings do not remember the pretemporal covenant, their testimony to God’s Lordship is understood to have left an indelible imprint upon their souls and to have established moral responsibility for them

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r11.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r11.claim: At moral understanding, prophetic teachings, scriptures, and laws awaken innate knowledge for believers as reminders renewing their first covenant.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r11.anchor: When these souls are engendered in earthly bodies and reach the age of moral understanding and accountability, the innate knowledge is reawakened in those who believe by their encounter with prophetic teachings, scriptures, and Divine laws

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r12.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r12.claim: A child who dies before moral and religious responsibility is considered to die in the first covenant and original fiṭrah, morally pure.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r12.anchor: he or she is considered to have died according to the first covenant

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r13.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r13.claim: The first covenant does not benefit those who reject later prophetic and scriptural messages.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r13.anchor: for those who fail to affirm the original covenant by rejecting the later covenant—that is, by denying the messages brought to them by their prophets and scriptures—their initial covenant will not benefit them

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r14.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r14.claim: Some describe God as bringing forth Adam’s progeny specifically from his loins.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r14.anchor: Some describe this pretemporal event as one in which God brought forth all the progeny of Adam from his loins, specifically

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r15.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r15.claim: Some say this occurred immediately after God breathed His Spirit into Adam.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r15.anchor: some argue that this was done immediately after God had blown His Spirit into Adam (15:29; 32:9; 38:72; Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r16.speaker: Other commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r16.claim: Others debate whether the covenant event came before or after Adam’s fall to earth.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r16.anchor: others debate whether it occurred before or after his fall to earth (Mw, Q).

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r17.speaker: Many commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r17.claim: They stress that God takes progeny from the Children of Adam and their plural loins, meaning all generations through the end of time.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r17.anchor: Many observe, however, that God takes the progeny not from Adam, but from the Children of Adam and from their loins (plural; IK, R, Ṭ), indicating simply that He brought forth all future generations that have appeared and will appear until the end of time

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r18.claim: Dhurriyah, also read as the plural dhurriyāt, literally derives from a root for scattered particles, atoms, or seeds and also means progeny in many Quranic verses.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r18.anchor: which derives from a root that in its most literal sense denotes small particles

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r19.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r19.claim: Some say the progeny were drawn forth as particles or seeds, reflecting Adam’s children’s physically unformed state at the encounter.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r19.anchor: Some commentators indicate that the progeny were drawn forth in the form of “particles” or “seeds”

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r20.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r20.claim: Some objected that particles could not hear or answer God and questioned how they could know their words or be accountable before intellect developed.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r20.anchor: some questioned how it was possible for the progeny as “particles” to hear and respond to God’s question; and because the intellect was not considered to manifest itself in human beings until years after birth

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r21.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r21.claim: Some read the verse symbolically as an innate covenant.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r21.anchor: some commentators consider this verse a symbolic description of an innate covenant

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r22.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r22.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r22.claim: Others read it as the temporal process by which reflection and growing intellect disclose the One God inwardly through primordial nature.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r22.anchor: a symbolic description of the temporal process by which human beings realize Divine Oneness—arguing that as individuals grow in intellect and contemplate the world around them, the existence of a single God becomes innately clear to them

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r23.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r23.speaker: Other commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r23.claim: Rejecting the symbolic reading as contrary to the plain text, they say God temporarily gave the particles intellect, hearing, and speech, as with the heavens and earth; bodily organs also testify.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r23.anchor: Others, however, reject this interpretation as against the plain meaning of the text

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r24.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r24.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r24.claim: Bearing witness about oneself can also mean bearing witness against oneself.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r24.anchor: God causes the Children of Adam to bear witness concerning themselves, or “against themselves.”

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r25.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r25.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r25.claim: The Quran describes humans bearing witness against themselves through deeds and bodies in this world and the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r25.anchor: The Quran mentions human beings bearing witness against themselves, in both this world and the Hereafter, through their deeds and their very bodies

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r26.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r26.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r26.claim: A-lastu bi-rabbikum is a declarative statement phrased as a question, requiring testimony to its truth.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r26.anchor: understood to be a declarative statement in the form of a question, requiring the hearers to bear witness to its truth.

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r27.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r27.speaker: Rūmī and some Muslim authors
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r27.claim: They poetically call the event the Day of Alast, a timeless day named from the opening of God’s question.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r27.anchor: Poetically, some Muslim authors, such as Rūmī, have described the event in this verse as the “Day of Alast,” referring to the first part of the question Am I not your Lord?

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r28.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r28.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r28.claim: Balā is a classical affirmative that conveys certainty.

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r29.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r29.speaker: Some reports
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r29.claim: Some reports assign “we bear witness” to other witnesses—angels, Adam, heaven and earth, or God—though most commentators find this less likely.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r29.anchor: Some reports consider we bear witness to have been spoken by other witnesses to their testimony—identified variously as the angels, Adam, the heavens and the earth, or God Himself

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r30.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r30.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r30.claim: The testimony prevents people from claiming on Resurrection Day that they were unaware of God’s Lordship or their duty to worship Him.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r30.anchor: The verse ends by explaining that the purpose of this questioning and witnessing was so that human beings could not come on the Day of Resurrection claiming to have been unaware of God’s Lordship or their duty to worship Him.

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r31.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r31.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r31.claim: Some question how earthly people can be accountable for a testimony from before birth that they cannot remember.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r31.anchor: One may question how one can be responsible, during earthly life, for a testimony one cannot remember having made prior to coming into this world

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r32.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r32.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r32.claim: Some reject the literal covenant as the basis of binding responsibility because humans cannot recall it, taking the verse symbolically instead.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r32.anchor: Some commentators have argued that it is precisely this human inability to remember the event described in this verse that points to its symbolic nature and thus reject the idea that a pretemporal covenant

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r33.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r33.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r33.claim: In Quranic and prophetic context, the pretemporal recognition creates an innate disposition to worship God and accept prophetic reminders of inwardly known truths.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r33.anchor: this pretemporal recognition of God’s Lordship can be understood as creating an innate disposition in human beings toward recognizing and worshipping God during earthly life and toward accepting the prophets and the messages they bring as “reminders”

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r34.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r34.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r34.claim: Those who reject prophets are willfully ignorant, denying truths that should resonate with the deep but forgotten knowledge in an uncorrupted soul.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r34.anchor: Those who reject the prophets, therefore, are considered willfully ignorant, denying truths that should, in any sincere and morally uncorrupted soul, resonate with a deep but forgotten knowledge of God

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r35.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r35.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r35.claim: Kuffār commonly means “disbelievers,” but etymologically means covering over innate awareness of God’s Lordship and Oneness.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r35.anchor: etymological meaning signifies the“covering over” of something

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r36.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r36.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r36.claim: Together with messengers sent to all peoples, the covenant serves as proof against those who knowingly and capriciously deny prophetic messages.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r36.anchor: The pretemporal covenant, then, in conjunction with God’s sending of messengers to all people serves as a “proof” against the disbelievers who capriciously or cynically deny prophetic messages

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r37.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r37.speaker: Some reports attributed to the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r37.claim: Some narrations use the verse to connect the pretemporal covenant with predestinarian ideas.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r37.anchor: This verse is also the basis for more elaborate narrations, some of which are attributed to the Prophet, that connect the pretemporal covenant with predestinarian notions.

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r38.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r38.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r38.claim: The verse’s literal reading suggests all people made the same covenant and therefore share the same possibility of recognizing God in earthly life.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r38.anchor: the literal reading of this verse suggests that all human beings have made the same covenant recognizing God’s Lordship and therefore have the same possibility for realizing it in earthly life

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r39.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r39.speaker: Some reports
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r39.claim: Some reports say progeny from Adam’s right side or God’s Right Hand were destined for the Garden, while those from the left or other Hand were destined for Hell.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r39.anchor: Some reports assert that God removed some progeny from the right side of Adam or with His Right Hand, and these human beings were destined for the Garden, while others were removed from Adam’s left side or with God’s other Hand and were thus destined for Hell

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r40.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r40.speaker: Some reports
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r40.claim: Other reports say some covenant witnesses answered reluctantly or deceptively.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r40.anchor: Still other reports indicate that some covenanters bore witness only reluctantly or deceptively

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r41.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r41.speaker: Other authorities
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r41.claim: Other authorities reject the claim that some covenant witnesses answered reluctantly or deceptively.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r41.anchor: although this interpretation is rejected by other authorities.

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r42.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r42.speaker: Some early Twelver Shiite traditions
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r42.claim: These traditions say covenant witnesses were also asked to attest Muhammad’s prophethood and the Shiite Imams’ authority, but only some accepted the latter.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r42.anchor: Some early Twelver Shiite traditions indicate that the covenanters on this day were also asked to bear witness to the prophethood of Muhammad and the spiritual authority of the Shiite Imams, but that only some accepted the latter

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r43.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r43.speaker: Some early Sufi authors, including al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r43.claim: They describe the covenant as distinguishing the spiritual elect from the common people.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r43.anchor: some early Sufi authors, including al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī (third/ninth century), referred to the pretemporal covenant as

STUDYQURAN:7:172/r44.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r44.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r44.claim: Although the covenant may shape moral destiny by giving humans innate capacity to recognize religious truth, the plain meaning more plausibly affirms universal potential for spiritual attainment and accepting revelation.
STUDYQURAN:7:172/r44.anchor: indicates the universal potential in all human beings for moral and spiritual attainment

SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r1.claim: من ظهورهم is an appositive with a repeated preposition for من بني آدم; the apposition may be of inclusion or part to whole, and the latter is the apparent reading, as in striking someone's back or cutting his hand.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r1.anchor: بدل من قوله " من بني آدم " بإعادة الجار كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ considers the apposition one of inclusion.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r2.anchor: قولان، الأول لأبي البقاء، والثاني للزمخشري، وهو الظاهر

SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī considers it part-to-whole apposition, which the author calls apparent.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r3.anchor: والثاني للزمخشري، وهو الظاهر كقولك: ضربت زيدا ظهره،

SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r4.claim: ذريتهم is the direct object; the Kufans and Ibn Kathīr read it singular, while the remaining readers use the plural ذرياتهم.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r4.anchor: و { ذريتهم } مفعول به. وقرأ الكوفيون وابن كثير " ذريتهم " بالإفراد،

SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r5.claim: For the plural reading, the Shaykh allows an omitted object understood as the covenant, with ذرياتهم as apposition to the pronoun in ظهورهم; taking the covenant from the descendants' backs is metaphorical language for a weighty binding pledge of monotheism.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ويحتمل في قراءة الجمع أن يكون مفعول " أخذ " محذوفا لفهم المعنى،

SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r6.claim: The Shaykh says the singular reading must be the object of أخذ with an omitted annexed noun, meaning the covenant of their descendants; unlike the feminine plural, its accusative ending cannot also mark genitive apposition.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r6.anchor: قال الشيخ في قراءة الإفراد في هذه السورة: " ويتعين أن يكون مفعولا ب " أخذ " وهو على حذف مضاف،

SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r7.claim: Across Yā Sīn and al-Ṭūr, the Kufans and Ibn Kathīr use the singular, Ibn ʿĀmir uses the plural, and Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ mix them; Abū ʿAmr agrees in Yā Sīn, while Nāfiʿ agrees only with al-Ṭūr's first occurrence.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172/r7.anchor: وكذلك قرأ الكوفيون وابن كثير في سورة يس وفي/ الطور في الموضعين: " ذريتهم " بالإفراد،

SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r1.claim: بلى answers the negative question ألست; Arabic answers a negative proposition affirmatively with بلى when the intent is to affirm it.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r1.anchor: وإنما المانع من جهة اللغة: وهو أن النفي مطلقا إذا قصد إيجابه أجيب ب بلى،

SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to say that saying نعم would have made them disbelievers.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: " لو قالوا: نعم لكفروا " يريد أن النفي إذا أجيب ب نعم

SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r3.claim: The author questions Ibn ʿAbbās's report: because the negative question already asserts the proposition, affirming that assertion would not cause disbelief; the obstacle is linguistic convention, which normally requires بلى.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r3.anchor: وفيه نظر إن صح عنه، وذلك أن هذا النفي صار مقررا، فكيف يكفرون بتصديق التقرير؟

SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#2/r4.claim: Only poetry may answer نعم by meaning rather than by the negative wording; a poem answers أليس with نعم because it means an affirmation.

SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r1.claim: شهدنا is variously attributed to God, the angels, both together, or the descendants; if the descendants speak, al-Wāḥidī says there is no pause at بلى and أن تقولوا attaches to وأشهدهم.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r1.anchor: هذا من كلام الله تعالى. وقيل: من كلام الملائكة. وقيل: من كلام الله تعالى والملائكة. وقيل: من كلام الذرية.

SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r2.speaker: الواحدي
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r2.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says that if شهدنا is spoken by the descendants, أن تقولوا cannot attach to it; it attaches to وأشهدهم, so one should not pause at بلى.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r2.anchor: قال الواحدي: " وعلى هذا لا يحسن الوقف على قوله " بلى " ولا يتعلق " أن تقولوا " ب " شهدنا "

SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r3.speaker: البصريون
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r3.claim: The Basrans parse أن تقولوا as purpose governed by شهدنا: they testified to prevent people from saying they were unaware.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r3.anchor: والعامل فيه: إما شهدنا، أي: شهدنا كراهة أن تقولوا، هذا تأويل البصريين،

SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r4.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r4.claim: The Kufans supply an omitted negation, meaning lest you say, and allow the purpose clause to depend on either شهدنا or وأشهدهم; a poem similarly omits لا in أن تباعا.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r4.anchor: وأما الكوفيون فقاعدتهم تقدير لا النافية، تقديره: لئلا تقولوا،

SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r5.speaker: الواحدي
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r5.claim: Al-Wāḥidī argues that if the descendants said شهدنا, أن تقولوا must attach to وأشهدهم, since شهدنا أن تقولوا would make the witnesses themselves say that they might say it; the author replies that some descendants can testify that others will say it.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r5.anchor: وقد تقدم أن الواحدي قد قال: " إن شهدنا إذا كان من قول الذرية يتعين أن يتعلق

SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r6.speaker: الجرجاني
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r6.claim: Al-Jurjānī transmits another view: the covenant story ends at قالوا بلى, and شهدنا begins a new report meaning we witness, as in al-Ḥuṭayʾa's line using شهد for يشهد; then أن تقولوا depends on that verb.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r6.anchor: وذكر الجرجاني لبعضهم وجها آخر وهو أن يكون قوله " وإذ أخذ ربك " إلى قوله: " قالوا بلى " تمام قصة الميثاق،

SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads يقولوا in both places in the third person, while the others read تقولوا in the second person; the third person suits شهدنا as God's speech, while another analysis makes it attach to وأشهدهم and treats قالوا شهدنا as an interruption, with the second person as a shift in address.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو " يقولوا " في الموضعين بالغيبة جريا على الأسماء المتقدمة، والباقون بالخطاب،

SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r8.claim: One view, held by many, takes the covenant literally: God brought Adam's descendants out like particles, made them testify, and all recognized Him; believers spoke truth in pre-eternity while polytheists spoke dissemblingly.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r8.anchor: وهل هذا من باب الحقيقة وأن الله أخرج الذرية من ظهره بأن مسح عليه فخرجوا كالذر

SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r9.claim: Another view, including al-Zamakhsharī's, treats the testimony as representation rather than a literal primordial scene, comparing it to the speaking heavens and earth in 41:11.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#3/r9.anchor: أو من باب التمثيل، قاله جماعة منهم الزمخشري، وجعله كقوله تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:7:172#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#4/r1.claim: The continuation illustrates the reported representational reading with a scriptural example and poems in which saddle straps address a camel's belly and the east wind speaks.
SAMIN-DURR:7:172#4/r1.anchor:
وقول الشاعر:
2336 إذ قالت الأنساع للبطن الحقي

TAB-FULL:v10p547/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p547/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p547/r1.claim: God tells Muhammad to remember when He brought Adam’s descendants from their fathers’ loins, made them affirm His oneness, and had some witness to the others’ testimony and confession.
TAB-FULL:v10p547/r1.anchor: آبائهم، فقررهم بتوحيده، وأشهد بعضهم على بعض شهادتهم بذلك، وإقرارهم به

TAB-FULL:v10p547/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p547/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v10p547/r2.claim: The Prophet says God took the covenant from Adam’s back at Nuʿman near Arafah, produced all his descendants like particles, spread them before Him, and addressed them with this verse.
TAB-FULL:v10p547/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: " أخذ الله الميثاق من ظهر آدم بنعمان يعني عرفة

TAB-FULL:v10p547/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p547/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p547/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God stroked Adam’s back at Nuʿman, brought forth every soul destined to exist until the Resurrection, and took their covenant.
TAB-FULL:v10p547/r3.anchor: سألت عنها ابن عباس، فقال: " مسح ربك ظهر آدم، فخرجت كل نسمة هو خالقها إلى يوم القيامة بنعمان هذا

TAB-FULL:v10p547/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p547/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p547/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas also locates the event at Dajni in India when Adam was first sent down, saying God extracted every future soul and took their covenant.
TAB-FULL:v10p547/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، قال: " أول ما أهبط الله آدم، أهبطه بدجني، أرض بالهند، فمسح الله ظهره

TAB-FULL:v10p549/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p549/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p549/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when Adam descended, God extracted every future soul from his back, then asked whether He was their Lord; the decree for all events through the Resurrection was already fixed.
TAB-FULL:v10p549/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " أهبط آدم حين أهبط، فمسح الله ظهره، فأخرج منه كل نسمة هو خالقها إلى يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v10p549/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p549/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p549/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that God took two handfuls from Adam’s descendants, assigning one group to Paradise and the other to Hell.
TAB-FULL:v10p549/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم} [الأعراف: 172] قال: " لما خلق الله آدم، أخذ ذريته من ظهره مثل الذر

TAB-FULL:v10p549/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p549/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p549/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God placed all the good offspring in His right hand and all the evil in the other.
TAB-FULL:v10p549/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: «مسح الله ظهر آدم، فأخرج كل طيب في يمينه، وأخرج كل خبيث في الأخرى»

TAB-FULL:v10p549/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p549/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p549/r4.claim: A further report from Ibn Abbas locates the extraction at Dajni and says the decree was fixed for what would occur until the Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v10p549/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم} [الأعراف: 172] قال: لما خلق الله آدم مسح ظهره بدجني

TAB-FULL:v10p551/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God covenanted with Adam, decreed his offspring’s lifespans, provisions, and afflictions, then extracted them like particles and took their covenant.
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم} [الأعراف: 172] قال: لما خلق الله آدم، أخذ ميثاقه

TAB-FULL:v10p551/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas locates the event in the valley of Nuʿman near Arafah, where Adam’s descendants emerged like particles and testified that God was their Lord.
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r2.anchor: عن أبيه عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: " {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم وأشهدهم على أنفسهم} [الأعراف: 172] قال: مسح الله ظهر آدم عليه السلام وهو ببطن نعمان

TAB-FULL:v10p551/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r3.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas describes Adam’s offspring emerging like particles while he was amid water.
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r3.anchor: عن أبي هلال، عن أبي جمرة الضبعي، عن ابن عباس، قال: « أخرج الله ذرية آدم عليه السلام من ظهره كهيئة الذر

TAB-FULL:v10p551/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r4.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says even a six-day-old infant is questioned in the grave about the primordial covenant made in Adam’s loins.
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r4.anchor: مات ابن للضحاك بن مزاحم، ابن ستة أيام، قال: فقال: يا جابر إذا أنت وضعت ابني في لحده

TAB-FULL:v10p551/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God extracted every soul and covenanted that they worship Him alone; fulfilling the later covenant benefits one, while a child dying before it dies upon the first covenant and natural disposition.
TAB-FULL:v10p551/r5.anchor: ثني ابن عباس «أن الله مسح صلب آدم، فاستخرج منه كل نسمة هو خالقها إلى يوم القيامة، وأخذ منهم الميثاق أن يعبدوه

TAB-FULL:v10p552/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p552/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v10p552/r1.claim: The Prophet objects when combatants take children after killing the fighters, and says every newborn begins on the natural disposition until speech develops and parents make the child Jewish or Christian.
TAB-FULL:v10p552/r1.anchor: فبلغ ذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فاشتد عليه، ثم قال: «ما بال أقوام يتناولون الذرية؟»

TAB-FULL:v10p552/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p552/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v10p552/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the covenant verse is the scriptural statement of the Prophet’s teaching about every newborn’s original disposition.
TAB-FULL:v10p552/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: والله لقد قال الله ذلك في كتابه، قال: {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم}

TAB-FULL:v10p552/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p552/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
TAB-FULL:v10p552/r3.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr describes God taking the descendants from Adam’s back like a comb drawn through hair and their answering that God is their Lord.
TAB-FULL:v10p552/r3.anchor: عن منصور، عن مجاهد، عن عبد الله بن عمرو، في قوله: " {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم} [الأعراف: 172] قال: أخذهم كما يأخذ المشط من الرأس

TAB-FULL:v10p552/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p552/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v10p552/r4.claim: In a report from Umar, the Prophet says God assigned one group of Adam’s descendants to Paradise and one to Hell, and each is made to act until death in keeping with that destiny.
TAB-FULL:v10p552/r4.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " إن الله خلق آدم ثم مسح ظهره بيمينه فاستخرج منه ذرية

TAB-FULL:v10p555/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p555/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v10p555/r1.claim: The Prophet tells Umar that God created Adam, breathed into him, extracted descendants for Paradise and Hell, and decreed their deeds and final outcomes.
TAB-FULL:v10p555/r1.anchor: سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عنه كما سألتني، فقال: " خلق الله آدم بيده، ونفخ فيه من روحه، ثم أجلسه

TAB-FULL:v10p555/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p555/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p555/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God extracted Adam’s descendants like particles, asked who their Lord was, and returned them to his loins so each would be born without any increase or decrease in their number.
TAB-FULL:v10p555/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم} [الأعراف: 172] قال: " إن الله خلق آدم، ثم أخرج ذريته من صلبه مثل الذر

TAB-FULL:v10p555/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p555/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p555/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that God made Adam’s descendants speak and testify, gave some a light, and told Adam to take their covenant to worship God alone; David’s lifespan was sixty, and Adam gave him forty years from his own thousand-year term.
TAB-FULL:v10p555/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: " إن الله لما خلق آدم مسح ظهره، وأخرج ذريته كلهم كهيئة الذر، فأنطقهم فتكلموا

TAB-FULL:v10p558/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God drew future people from Adam's right and left shoulders, assigning pure white souls to Paradise and black souls to Fire, then took their covenant of faith and knowledge, which they affirmed; they were tiny like mustard seeds.
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " إن الله تبارك وتعالى ضرب منكبه الأيمن، فخرجت كل نفس مخلوقة للجنة بيضاء نقية

TAB-FULL:v10p558/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r2.claim: Mujahid says God summoned the extracted people to answer, meaning obey; they pledged obedience, Adam's back was struck at his creation, and Abraham's pilgrimage talbiya derives from their reply.
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: إن الله لما أخرجهم قال: يا عباد الله أجيبوا الله والإجابة: الطاعة فقالوا: أطعنا

TAB-FULL:v10p558/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Adam's descendants were drawn out like motes, spoke that God was their Lord, and returned to his loins; all creation is on the primordial nature God established until Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: خلق آدم، ثم أخرج ذريته من ظهره مثل الذر، فكلمهم

TAB-FULL:v10p558/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r4.speaker: سعيد بن حبير
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr places the covenant at Na'man behind Arafah, so people cannot claim at Resurrection that they were unaware of it.
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r4.anchor: قال سعيد بن حبير: أخذ الميثاق عليهم بنعمان ونعمان من وراء عرفة أن يقولوا يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v10p558/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r5.claim: Ubayy reports God assembled all future humanity, elicited their confession, warned against denying knowledge or following ancestral shirk, and promised messengers and scriptures to remind them of the covenant.
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r5.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، قال: " جمعهم يومئذ جميعا ما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة، ثم استنطقهم

TAB-FULL:v10p558/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r6.claim: In Ubayy's report, Adam saw his descendants' differing wealth and appearance and asked God to make them equal; God replied that He loves to be thanked.
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r6.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، قال: " جمعهم يومئذ جميعا ما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة، ثم استنطقهم

TAB-FULL:v10p558/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r7.claim: Ubayy says the prophets were like lamps among humanity and received a separate solemn covenant, linked to God's covenant with Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r7.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، قال: " جمعهم يومئذ جميعا ما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة، ثم استنطقهم

TAB-FULL:v10p558/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r8.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r8.claim: Ubayy's report links the primordial covenant to humanity's innate religion and earlier warnings, and says God's foreknowledge already distinguished those who would believe from those who would disbelieve.
TAB-FULL:v10p558/r8.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، قال: " جمعهم يومئذ جميعا ما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة، ثم استنطقهم

TAB-FULL:v10p559/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p559/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v10p559/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says Adam was allotted a thousand years, then gave David forty of them after admiring the light around him; at Adam's death he disputed the remaining forty.
TAB-FULL:v10p559/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في هذه الآية: " {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم

TAB-FULL:v10p559/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p559/r2.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v10p559/r2.claim: Sa'id reports that Adam saw his descendants' names, fathers, and lifespans; he gave David forty years from his own thousand, recorded while the pens were wet, but later disputed the gift when Death came.
TAB-FULL:v10p559/r2.anchor: عن سعيد، في قوله: {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم}

TAB-FULL:v10p559/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p559/r3.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v10p559/r3.claim: Ata says God extracted Adam's descendants, took their covenant, and then returned them to Adam's loins.
TAB-FULL:v10p559/r3.anchor: عن عطاء: " {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم}

TAB-FULL:v10p559/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p559/r4.speaker: نضر بن عربي
TAB-FULL:v10p559/r4.claim: Nadr ibn Arabi likewise says God drew the descendants from Adam, took their covenant, and returned them to his loins.
TAB-FULL:v10p559/r4.anchor: عن نضر بن عربي: " {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم}

TAB-FULL:v10p560/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says that when God created Adam's descendants for him, He created them and made them testify that He was their Lord; they answered yes.
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك، قال: " حيث ذرأ الله خلقه لآدم، قال: خلقهم وأشهدهم على أنفسهم

TAB-FULL:v10p560/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God spoke to Adam's extracted descendants, made them answer that He was their Lord, and returned them to his loins; Resurrection awaits the birth of all who testified then.
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: " خلق الله آدم، ثم أخرج ذريته من ظهره، فكلمهم الله وأنطقهم

TAB-FULL:v10p560/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r3.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the covenant day with the submission of heaven and earth and God's conclusive proof; the people were then presented to Adam.
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r3.anchor: عن السدي: " {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم وأشهدهم على أنفسهم ألست بربكم قالوا بلى}

TAB-FULL:v10p560/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says God drew white, pearl-like descendants from Adam's right side for Paradise and black descendants from his left for Fire, then took their covenant; some obeyed willingly and others under dissimulation.
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r4.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " أخرج الله آدم من الجنة، ولم يهبط من السماء، ثم مسح صفحة ظهره اليمنى

TAB-FULL:v10p560/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r5.claim: Al-Suddi adds that God and the angels witnessed the descendants' confession; everyone knows God, while polytheists justify following the religion and path of their ancestors.
TAB-FULL:v10p560/r5.anchor: عن السدي، بنحوه، وزاد فيه بعد قوله: " وطائفة على وجه التقية، فقال هو والملائكة: شهدنا أن يقولوا يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v10p563/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p563/r1.speaker: الكلبي
TAB-FULL:v10p563/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says God drew all future descendants from Adam, took their covenant that He is their Lord, and they assented; even a disbeliever answers that God is Lord when asked.
TAB-FULL:v10p563/r1.anchor: عن الكلبي: " {من ظهورهم ذرياتهم} قال: مسح الله على صلب آدم، فأخرج من صلبه من ذريته

TAB-FULL:v10p563/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p563/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v10p563/r2.claim: Al-Hasan gives the same account as al-Kalbi about extracting Adam's descendants and their covenant.

TAB-FULL:v10p563/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p563/r3.speaker: علي بن حسين
TAB-FULL:v10p563/r3.claim: Ali ibn Husayn practiced coitus interruptus and interpreted this verse as relevant to that practice.
TAB-FULL:v10p563/r3.anchor: عن علي بن حسين " أنه كان يعزل، ويتأول هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v10p563/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p563/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TAB-FULL:v10p563/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi says the spirits acknowledged God before their bodies were created.
TAB-FULL:v10p563/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي، في قوله: " {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم} [الأعراف: 172] قال: أقرت الأرواح قبل أن تخلق أجسادها

TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r1.claim: Answering whether deeds begin or destiny is already decreed, the Prophet says God took Adam's descendants, made them testify, divided them between Paradise and Fire, and facilitates each group for its destined deeds.
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r1.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن الله أخذ ذرية آدم من ظهورهم، ثم أشهدهم على أنفسهم، ثم أفاض بهم في كفيه

TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi reads the testimony as God and His angels witnessing the descendants' acknowledgment of His lordship, preventing them from claiming ignorance at Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r2.anchor: فقال السدي: هو خبر من الله عن نفسه وملائكته أنه جل ثناؤه قال هو وملائكته إذ أقر بنو آدم بربوبيته

TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r3.claim: Other interpreters read the testimony as some descendants witnessing against others after God had them acknowledge His lordship.
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: ذلك خبر من الله عن قيل بعض بني آدم لبعض، حين أشهد الله بعضهم على بعض

TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r4.claim: Al-Tabari conditionally prefers the report from the Prophet if authentic, but doubts it because reliable transmitters stop it at Abdullah ibn Amr and omit the disputed wording; otherwise the verse's apparent sense is descendants testifying to one another.
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب، ما روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن كان صحيحا، ولا أعلمه صحيحا

TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r5.claim: If the Prophetic wording is not sound, al-Tabari takes the apparent reading to mean witnesses told the confessors they had testified to their own acknowledgment, so they could not plead ignorance.
TAB-FULL:v10p563#2/r5.anchor: فكأنه قيل: فقال الذين شهدوا على المقرين حين أقروا، فقالوا: بلى شهدنا عليكم بما أقررتم به على أنفسكم

TABATABAI:7:172/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172/r1.claim: The verse's covenant concerning God's lordship is among the Qur'an's most subtle in meaning and remarkable in composition.
TABATABAI:7:172/r1.anchor: وهي من أدق الآيات القرآنية معنى، وأعجبها نظما

TABATABAI:7:172/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172/r2.claim: “Taking” something from another thing implies separation, but its precise sense varies by context; here it means extracting offspring from backs while the source remains whole, then making each child an independent person through successive generations.
TABATABAI:7:172/r2.anchor: وهو أخذ بعض المادة منها بحيث لا تنقص المادة المأخوذ منها بحسب صورتها ولا تنقلب عن تمامها واستقلالها ثم تكميل الجزء المأخوذ شيئا تاما مستقلا

TABATABAI:7:172/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172/r3.claim: The phrase “from their backs” specifies this mode of extraction; individuals become distinct from their parents and from one another, each with an independent soul and personal accountability.
TABATABAI:7:172/r3.anchor: فهذا مفاد قوله { وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم }

TABATABAI:7:172/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172/r4.claim: Witnessing people against themselves means showing them the reality of their own selves so they can experientially know it and testify when called upon; the question specifies that they witness God's lordship over them.
TABATABAI:7:172/r4.anchor: فإشهادهم على أنفسهم هو إراءتهم حقيقة أنفسهم ليتحملوا ما أريد تحملهم من أمرها ثم يؤدوا ما تحملوه إذا سئلوا

TABATABAI:7:172/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172/r5.claim: Human beings cannot own or govern their existence independently: they cannot protect themselves from death and suffering, and the cosmic causes on which they depend are themselves governed by an unseen authority.
TABATABAI:7:172/r5.anchor: ولو ملك نفسه لوقاها مما يكرهه من الموت وسائر آلام الحياة ومصائبها، ولو استقل بتدبير أمره لم يفتقر إلى الخضوع قبال الأسباب الكونية

TABATABAI:7:172#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172#2/r1.claim: Need for a Lord who owns and governs human beings is intrinsic to human nature; all people, regardless of knowledge, age, or status, can sense their dependence.
TABATABAI:7:172#2/r1.anchor: الحاجة إلى رب - مالك مدبر - حقيقة الإنسان، والفقر مكتوب على نفسه، والضعف مطبوع على ناصيته

TABATABAI:7:172#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172#2/r2.claim: One reading understands the testimony as worldly recognition of dependence upon God, expressed either by the self's state or by the logical implication of people's acknowledged need.
TABATABAI:7:172#2/r2.anchor: فعلى أحد هذين النوعين من القول أعني القول بلسان الحال والقول بالاستلزام يحمل اعترافهم المحكي

TABATABAI:7:172#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172#2/r3.claim: Between testimony through one's state and testimony by implication, he says the first is closer because testimony should state its object explicitly rather than merely imply it.
TABATABAI:7:172#2/r3.anchor: والأول أقرب وأنسب فإنه لا يكتفي في مقام الشهادة إلا بالصريح من

TABATABAI:7:172#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172#2/r4.claim: He also proposes a third possibility: divine creative speech discloses purposes through existence itself, so the question and answer may have occurred through creation as real speech in an analytical sense.
TABATABAI:7:172#2/r4.anchor: فإن الكلام الإلهي يكشف به عن المقاصد الإلهية بالفعل، والإيجاد كلام حقيقي

TABATABAI:7:172-173/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-173/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-173/r1.claim: The passage says the covenant and testimony were meant to complete God's proof by closing two excuses people might otherwise raise on Judgment Day for their polytheism.
TABATABAI:7:172-173/r1.anchor: وهو على ما يفيده السياق إبطال حجتين للعباد على الله وبيان أنه لولا هذا الأخذ والإشهاد

TABATABAI:7:172-173/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-173/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-173/r2.claim: If God had not made anyone testify, all people could plead that they were unaware of His lordship, and an unaware person is not liable to punishment.
TABATABAI:7:172-173/r2.anchor: لأقاموا جميعا الحجة علينا يوم القيامة بأنهم كانوا غافلين في الدنيا عن ربوبيتنا، ولا تكليف على غافل ولا مؤاخذة

TABATABAI:7:172#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172#3/r1.claim: If only descendants or some descendants had testified, the others would still be able to plead ignorance; untestified ancestors would neither knowingly shirk nor imitate an earlier example.
TABATABAI:7:172#3/r1.anchor: وأما الآباء الذين لم يشهدوا فليس عندهم إلا الغفلة المحضة عن أمر الربوبية فلا يستقلون بشرك إذ لم يشهدوا

TABATABAI:7:172#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172#3/r2.claim: Gradual growth in civilization concerns acquired theoretical knowledge, whereas awareness of needing a Lord is innate and foundational, so it does not arise later than other knowledge.
TABATABAI:7:172#3/r2.anchor: وأما حديث تكامل الإنسان في العلم والحضارة تدريجا فإنما هو في العلوم النظرية الاكتسابية

TABATABAI:7:172#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172#3/r3.claim: The two verses mean that God distinguished every descendant, made each testify to their own dependence, and took the covenant of His lordship so humanity cannot plead ignorance or inherited shirk.
TABATABAI:7:172#3/r3.anchor: فالمتحصل من الآيتين أن الله سبحانه فصل بين بني آدم بأخذ بعضهم من بعض ثم أشهدهم جميعا على أنفسهم

TABATABAI:7:172#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172#3/r4.speaker: عدة من المفسرين
TABATABAI:7:172#3/r4.claim: Several commentators take the time-setting as worldly life: God brings descendants through birth, displays His signs and their total dependence, and they acknowledge Him by the testimony of their state.
TABATABAI:7:172#3/r4.anchor: ذكر عدة من المفسرين أن المراد بهذا الظرف المشار إليه

TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r1.speaker: القوم
TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r1.claim: A number of reports are cited for a primordial world of particles in which God extracted Adam's descendants, made them recognize Him, and took their covenant of lordship as proof for Judgment Day.
TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r1.anchor: وقد طرح القوم عدة من الروايات تدل على أن الآيتين تدلان على عالم الذر

TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r2.claim: The first objection says that if the extracted descendants were not rational they could not understand God's address, but if rational they should remember the covenant for it to establish proof; people recall no existence before earthly life.
TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r2.anchor: أنه لا يخلو إما أن جعل الله هذه الذرية المستخرجة من صلب آدم عقلاء أو لم يجعلهم كذلك

TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r3.claim: A second objection deems it implausible that a vast multitude forgot a known event when the Qur'an depicts people in Paradise and Hell recalling worldly events; it says this could otherwise permit the transmigrationists' account of repeated bodies.
TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r3.anchor: أنه لا يجوز أن ينسي الجميع الكثير والجم الغفير من العقلاء أمرا قد كانوا عرفوه وميزوه حتى لا يذكره ولا واحد منهم

TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r4.claim: A third objection argues that the wording speaks of descendants from the backs of Adam's children, and the polytheist-ancestor excuse excludes Adam's immediate offspring from the primordial scene.
TABATABAI:7:172-173#2/r4.anchor: 3 - ما أورد على الأخبار الناطقة بأن الله سبحانه أخذ من صلب آدم ذريته وأخذ منهم الميثاق

TABATABAI:7:173/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:173/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:173/r2.claim: A fourth objection says a single collective existence in the primordial world would leave no parents whose earlier polytheism descendants could cite.
TABATABAI:7:173/r2.anchor: 4 - أن تفسير الآية بعالم الذر ينافي قولهم

TABATABAI:7:173/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:173/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:173/r3.claim: A fifth view accepts the primordial reports as a pre-birth event that fosters an innate disposition toward knowledge of God, but argues the verse itself cannot mean that because descendants could plead that God made them forget the witness and left them to fallible reasoning.
TABATABAI:7:173/r3.anchor: أن الروايات مقبولة مسلمة غير أنها ليست بتأويل للآية، والذي تقصه من حديث عالم الذر

TABATABAI:7:173/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:173/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:173/r4.claim: A sixth objection says the verse is not explicit and could be figurative, while the reports are either raised or stopped traditions and carry no probative force.
TABATABAI:7:173/r4.anchor: أن الآية لا صراحة لها فيما تدل عليه الروايات لإمكان حملها على التمثيل

TABATABAI:7:173/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:173/r5.speaker: المثبتون لنشأة الذر
TABATABAI:7:173/r5.claim: Defenders answer that forgetting the occasion and details of the covenant does not invalidate proof; the essential pledge and knowledge of God's oneness remain even if the scene is forgotten.
TABATABAI:7:173/r5.anchor: فالجواب عن الأول أن نسيان الموقف وخصوصياته لا يضر بتمام الحجة وإنما المضر نسيان أصل الميثاق

TABATABAI:7:173/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:173/r6.speaker: المثبتون لنشأة الذر
TABATABAI:7:173/r6.claim: They answer that the alleged impossibility of mass forgetting is only an unsupported intuition; essential knowledge of lordship remains, and transmigration has separate refutations, so forgetting a prior world is not logically impossible.
TABATABAI:7:173/r6.anchor: والجواب عن الثاني أن الامتناع من تجويز نسيان الجمع الكثير لذلك مجرد استبعاد من غير دليل على الامتناع

TABATABAI:7:172-174/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r1.claim: The wording ‘from the children of Adam’ itself implies taking Adam’s direct offspring from his loins, then their descendants from theirs, as in ordinary reproduction.
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r1.anchor: فإن قوله تعالى { وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم } كاف وحده في الدلالة عليه

TABATABAI:7:172-174/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r2.speaker: الرازي
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r2.claim: Al-Razi says reports establish extraction of Adam’s direct children, while the verse establishes later descendants from their fathers; together they prove the whole account.
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r2.anchor: وقد أجاب الرازي عنه في تفسيره بأن الدلالة على إخراج أولاده لصلبه من صلبه من ناحية الخبر

TABATABAI:7:172-174/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r3.claim: Al-Razi’s division of the proof between report and verse is unconvincing.
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r3.anchor: فبمجموع الآية والخبر تتم الدلالة على المجموع. وهو كما ترى

TABATABAI:7:172-174/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r4.claim: Reports about Adam’s descendants emerging from his loins and taking the covenant narrate the event; they are not attempts to explain the verse’s wording.
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r4.anchor: فهي في مقام شرح القصة لا في مقام تفسير ألفاظ الآية

TABATABAI:7:172-174/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r6.claim: In reply to the fourth objection, the verse and reports show God first separated fathers and children, then returned them to a collective state.
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r6.anchor: وقد دلت الآية والرواية على أن الله فصل هناك بين الآباء والأبناء ثم ردهم إلى حال الجمع

TABATABAI:7:172-174/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r7.claim: The fifth objection conflicts with the apparent meaning of some reports and the explicit wording of others; the forgetfulness issue was answered earlier.
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r7.anchor: أنه خلاف ظاهر بعض الروايات وخلاف صريح بعض آخر منها

TABATABAI:7:172-174/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r8.claim: For the sixth objection, a stable apparent meaning is authoritative without requiring explicit wording; a possible figurative reading is not preferred absent an impediment to the literal sense.
TABATABAI:7:172-174/r8.anchor: ولا يتوقف ذلك على صفة الصراحة، وإمكان الحمل على التمثيل لا يوجب الحمل عليه

TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r1.claim: Some reports in the debate are sound or reliable in transmission; the author says he will assess them in the following report discussion.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r1.anchor: فإن فيها ما هو الصحيح وفيها ما يوثق بصدوره

TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r2.speaker: المثبتون
TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r2.claim: Proponents picture Adam’s seminal substance divided across descendants into atoms, each made the same fully conscious future person, addressed about lordship, then returned to the loins until birth while retaining knowledge but forgetting the event.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r2.anchor: هذا ما يفهمه القوم من الخبر والآية ويرومون إثباته

TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r3.claim: This atom-person account is impossible and contradicted by Quran and hadith: it makes a tiny bodily particle identical to a later person with that person’s mind and senses, bearing obligations and recompense.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r3.anchor: وهو مما تدفعه الضرورة، وينفيه القرآن والحديث بلا ريب

TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r4.claim: Human identity is the soul, an entity beyond matter that comes into being with the present body; therefore a particle in Adam’s substance cannot already be the later accountable person.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#2/r4.anchor: أن إنسانية الإنسان بنفسه التي هي أمر وراء المادة حادث بحدوث هذا البدن الدنيوي

TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r1.claim: Both immediate and inferential knowledge, including assent that God is one’s sustaining Lord, arise through bodily development and ultimately depend on external and internal sensations.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r1.anchor: تتوقف على وجود التركيب الدنيوي المادي فهو حال العلوم الحصولية

TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r2.claim: If proof requires reason along with recognition, the primordial atom loses reason on returning to the loins; reason is also absent in childhood, disrupting accountability.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r2.anchor: فالعقل مسلوب عن الذرة حين أرجعت إلى موطنه الصلبي

TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r3.claim: If recognition alone completes proof, witnessing and covenant-taking seem unnecessary, although the verse presents them as serving that purpose; this collapses into the deniers’ interpretation.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r3.anchor: فأى حاجة إلى الإشهاد وأخذ الميثاق وظاهر الآية أن الإشهاد وأخذ الميثاق إنما هما لأجل إتمام الحجة

TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r4.claim: If proof requires testimony, instruction, and covenant together, forgetting them cancels proof; if they merely produce lasting recognition, proof would also bind fetuses, children, the mentally impaired, and the ignorant, contrary to reason and revelation.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r4.anchor: إن كانت الحجة إنما تتم بمجموع الإشهاد والتعريف وأخذ الميثاق سقطت بنسيان البعض

TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r5.claim: If primordial recognition only becomes probative after worldly reason and maturity, ordinary worldly causes already prepare it, so an earlier creation for completing proof serves no purpose.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#3/r5.anchor: وإذا كانت تحصل في ظرفنا هذا بأسبابها المعدة لها كالعقل فأي حاجة إلى تكوينه تكوينا آخر في سالف من الزمان

TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r1.claim: Practical reason develops only in social life through repeated choices, emotions, and experience distinguishing right from wrong; the proposed primordial realm lacks those conditions.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r1.anchor: هو العقل العملي الذي لا يحصل للإنسان إلا في هذا الظرف الذي يعيش فيه عيشة اجتماعية

TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r2.claim: Giving that realm the same conditions, prophets, and choices as worldly life makes it a second natural world, raising the same need for an earlier realm and leaving no principled difference.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r2.anchor: كان ذلك إثباتا لنشأة طبيعية قبل هذه النشأة الطبيعية في الدنيا

TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r3.claim: If prior existence is necessary for knowledge, Adam and Eve need explaining too: if they needed no such stage, their descendants could gain knowledge upon completing their own creation.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r3.anchor: فما بال آدم وحواء استثنيا من هذه الكلية؟

TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r4.claim: These objections cannot be resolved scientifically or by forcing the verse to fit an impossible report; a definitive report, like Quran, cannot assert an impossibility.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r4.anchor: لا طريق إلى حلها بالأبحاث العلمية

TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r5.speaker: الحشوية وبعض المحدثين
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r5.claim: Some traditionalists and hadith scholars reject necessary rational proof when it conflicts with a report and rely on solitary reports for matters of certain knowledge; the author declines debate with them.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#4/r5.anchor: وأما الحشوية وبعض المحدثين ممن يبطل حجة العقل الضرورية قبال الرواية

TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r2.claim: The worldly-life reading conflicts with the opening ‘when’: the story’s setting would coincide with the human species’ worldly existence, so the wording would lack its ordinary past-time force.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r2.anchor: فعبر عن ظرف هذه القضية بإذ وهو يدل على الزمن الماضي

TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r3.claim: The address may be to the Prophet or to him and others; if instead it addresses the verse’s worldly hearers, the narrative setting would be their worldly lifetime, which does not explain ‘when.’
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r3.anchor: { وإذ أخذ ربك } خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أو له ولغيره

TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r4.claim: No contextual reason licenses using ‘when’ merely to mark certainty of occurrence in the deniers’ reading.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r4.anchor: ولا عناية أخرى في المقام تصحح هذا التعبير من قبيل تحقق الوقوع ونحوه

TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r5.claim: The verse describes ordinary generational creation, each person emerging from another, yet indicates that this familiar process has a kind of precedence over observable worldly development.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r5.anchor: يدل على أن للقصة - وهي تنطبق على الحال المشهود - نوعا من التقدم على هذا المشهود

TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r6.claim: That precedence cannot mean a prior temporal extraction of atom-sized future people from Adam, each already bearing a complete worldly identity; the verse is unrelated to that account.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#5/r6.anchor: وقد تقدمت استحالة ما افترضوا لهذا التقدم من تقدم هذه الخلقة بنحو تقدما زمانيا

TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r1.claim: The rejected interpretation would make a person with one worldly identity exist twice in the same world, so that the repeated person would no longer be numerically the same.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r1.anchor: استلزامه وجود الإنسان بما له من الشخصية الدنيوية مرتين في الدنيا

TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r2.claim: Existence in multiple realms with different orders is possible: Quran affirms the same person in resurrection and in the distinct life of the barzakh.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r2.anchor: فقد أثبت الله الحياة الآخرة للإنسان وغيره يوم البعث

TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r3.claim: Quran 15:21 says every thing has an expansive existence with God in His treasuries before measured descent; humanity likewise has a prior existence there.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r3.anchor: أن لكل شيء عنده وجودا وسيعا غير مقدر في خزائنه

TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r4.claim: Quran 36:82–83 and 54:50 present creation as an instantaneous divine command; things thus have a gradual worldly aspect and a complete, non-gradual aspect toward God.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r4.anchor: فلوجود هذه الأشياء وجهان وجه إلى الدنيا وحكمه أن يحصل بالخروج من القوة إلى الفعل تدريجا

TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r5.claim: Humanity has a collective existence with God in which individuals are not hidden from one another or their Lord; this is the realm called malakut.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#6/r5.anchor: وهذا هو الذي يسميه الله سبحانه بالملكوت

TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r1.claim: The Qur’anic references to Abraham seeing the kingdom of the heavens and earth and to seeing hell with certainty point toward this divine aspect of existence.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r1.anchor: وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السماوات والأرض وليكون من الموقنين

TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r2.claim: The worldly aspect divides individuals and distributes actions across time, while sensory pleasures veil people from God; it branches from the prior aspect as ‘Be, and it is.’
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r2.anchor: وأما هذا الوجه الدنيوي الذي نشاهده نحن من العالم الإنساني وهو الذي يفرق بين الآحاد

TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r3.claim: Thus worldly human life is preceded by the same humanity in a realm where people directly witness God’s oneness in lordship and acknowledge truth; shirk and sin belong to worldly life.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r3.anchor: ويتبيّن بذلك أن هذه النشأة الإنسانية الدنيوية مسبوقة بنشأة أخرى إنسانية هي هي بعينها

TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r4.claim: Read with related verses, 7:172 details this prior realm: its precedence is like ‘Be, and it is,’ not temporal separation, so testimony and address remain literal without the atom theory’s difficulties or the deniers’ figurative paraphrase.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r4.anchor: فهي تشير إلى نشأة إنسانية سابقة فرق الله فيها بين أفراد هذا النوع

TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r5.claim: Some reports affirm the basic prior human realm; others say God disclosed it to Adam and showed him its malakut, as He showed Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and earth.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#7/r5.anchor: وبعضها يذكر أن الله كشف لآدم عليه السلام عن هذه النشأة الإنسانية

TABATABAI:7:173#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:173#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:173#2/r3.claim: The address and reply are real: the people understood God’s intended request for acknowledgment from what they witnessed; speech is any communication conveying an intended meaning.
TABATABAI:7:173#2/r3.anchor: وهو خطاب حقيقي لهم لا بيان حال وتكليم إلهي لهم

TABATABAI:7:173#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:173#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:173#2/r4.claim: The addressees of ‘lest you say’ are those who witnessed and acknowledged; worldly distractions veil the event, but resurrection removes the veils and restores their direct recollection.
TABATABAI:7:173#2/r4.anchor: فهم هناك يعاينون الإشهاد والتكليم من الله والتكلم بالاعتراف من أنفسهم

TABATABAI:7:173#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:173#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:173#2/r5.claim: Alternatively the warning may address the present hearers, but the author prefers the witnessed people as addressees, supported by the third-person reading ‘that they say.’
TABATABAI:7:173#2/r5.anchor: والأول أقرب ويؤيده قراءة { أن يقولوا } بلفظ الغيبة

TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r1.claim: The covenant covered prophethood and more, not only God's lordship, supporting the preceding argument.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r1.anchor: دلالة على أن الميثاق لم يؤخذ على الربوبية فحسب بل على النبوة وغير ذلك

TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r2.claim: God's proof encompasses all creatures; He took them at the covenant and demonstrated this by closing his hand.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r2.anchor: سألت أبا عبد الله عن قول الله { وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم } قال نعم لله الحجة على جميع خلقه

TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r3.claim: Al-Tabatabai reads the taking here as encompassing and ownership.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r3.anchor: وظاهر الرواية أنها تفسر الأخذ في الآية بمعنى الإحاطة والملك

TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r4.claim: The covenant was witnessed directly; knowledge was fixed, its scene forgotten, and some affirmed verbally without inward faith.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسكان عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله { وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم

TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r5.claim: This sound report refutes those who deny an actual primordial covenant and interpret the witness as merely learning signs of lordship.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r5.anchor: والرواية ترد على منكري دلالة الآية على أخذ الميثاق في الذر تفسيرهم قوله

TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r6.claim: Abu Ja'far recounts his father's account of Adam's clay being kneaded with sweet and bitter water, producing tiny descendants divided into right and left groups and tested by entry into fire.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r6.anchor: عن زرارة أن رجلا سأل أبا جعفر عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل { وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم } إلى آخر الآية، فقال

TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r7.claim: The order to enter the fire is a metaphor for entering servitude and obedience.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r7.anchor: وكأن الأمر بدخول النار كناية عن الدخول في حظيرة العبودية والانقياد للطاعة

TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r8.claim: God formed those He loved from paradise clay and those He hated from fire clay, then sent them in the shadow-world with prophets; their acknowledgment of God and the Imams' authority followed their divine love or hatred.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#8/r8.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال إن الله عز وجل خلق الخلق فخلق من أحب مما أحب فكان ما أحب أن خلقه من طينة الجنة

TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r1.claim: The shadow-world described by the Imams is this world in one respect and another world in another, with some rules like worldly life and others unlike it.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r1.anchor: وقد تكرر ذكر الظلال في لسان أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام والمراد به

TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r2.claim: Al-Ayyashi's addition that the answer occurred in the covenant is the narrator's explanation, not the Imam's wording.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r2.anchor: وما زاده العياشي من كلام الراوي

TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r3.claim: Asked how tiny particles could answer, the Imam says God made them such that they would answer when questioned.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r3.anchor: عن أبي بصير قال قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام كيف أجابوا وهم ذر؟ قال جعل فيهم ما إذا سألهم أجابوه

TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r4.claim: The report does not mean their condition merely signaled the answer; their eventual worldly speech explains how the answer was possible.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r4.anchor: وليس المراد بقوله " جعل فيهم ما إذا سألهم أجابوه " دلالة حالهم على ذلك

TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r5.claim: The Imam's wording says they answer when asked, not merely if they happen to speak, supporting a real exchange.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r5.anchor: ويؤيده قوله عليه السلام ما إذا سألهم، ولم يقل ما لو تكلموا ونحو ذلك

TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r6.claim: The descendants affirmed God's lordship with their tongues and hearts; when asked where they were, the Imam replied that God made them in a form sufficient for this.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r6.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قول الله { ألست بربكم } قالوا بألسنتهم؟ قال نعم

TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r7.claim: In that realm tongue and heart were one, so the verbal affirmation was true and accompanied by the heart; God created them in a way that made questioning and answering possible.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r7.anchor: القلب هناك واحد، ولذلك قال عليه السلام نعم وبقلوبهم فصدق اللسان

TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r8.claim: These reports explicitly establish that the address and speech in the verse are literal, not figurative.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#9/r8.anchor: صريح في أن التكليم والتكلم في الآية على الحقيقة دون المجاز بل هي صريحة فيه

TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r1.claim: The Prophet describes right and left groups affirming God's lordship, being mixed, returned to Adam's loins, and assigned their eventual homes; an interlocutor asks why they were mixed.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r1.anchor: فخلط بعضهم ببعض فقال قائل منهم رب لم خلطت بيننا؟ قال ولهم أعمال من دون ذلك هم لها عاملون

TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r2.claim: Asked what people should do, the Prophet replies that each group performs deeds suited to its dwelling.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r2.anchor: فقال قائل يا رسول الله فما الأعمال؟ قال يعمل كل قوم لمنازلهم

TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r3.claim: The Prophet's phrase about the Throne over water denotes that the covenant-taking preceded what follows, not that souls existed temporally before bodies as many proponents of the atom-world suppose.

TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r4.claim: Each eventual home calls for fitting worldly deeds: the people of Paradise do good and those of Hell do evil; inviting people to good remains meaningful even with a settled destination, as 2:148 shows.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r4.anchor: أي إن كل واحد من المنزلين يحتاج إلى أعمال تناسبه في الدنيا فإن كان العامل من أهل الجنة عمل الخير

TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r5.claim: There is no conflict between bliss or misery being determined relative to complete causes and remaining undetermined relative to human choice, which is itself only a partial cause; the author refers back to 7:29–30.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#10/r5.anchor: ولا منافاة بين تعين السعادة والشقاوة بالنظر إلى العلل التامة وبين عدم تعينها بالنظر إلى اختيار الإنسان

TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
