TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God took Adam's covenant, recorded his lifespan, provision, and afflictions, then brought his descendants out like tiny particles and took their covenant too.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله { وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم } الآية قال خلق الله آدم وأخذ

TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas's many versions vary in wording but share the extraction of Adam's descendants and their covenant as their core meaning.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r2.anchor: وقد روي هذا المعنى عن ابن عباس بطرق كثيرة في ألفاظ مختلفة لكن الجميع تشترك في أصل المعنى

TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r3.claim: A report says God drew white descendants from Adam's right and dark descendants from his left, declared their destinations, took their covenant, and made them witnesses so they could not plead ignorance or inherited shirk; it links this to 3:83 and 6:149.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة الهمداني عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة في قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r4.claim: The atom-covenant report is transmitted in both suspended and connected forms from many Companions and Imams through Sunni and Shi'a routes, making a claim of semantic mass-transmission plausible.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r4.anchor: وقد روى حديث الذر كما في الرواية موقوفة وموصولة عن عدة من أصحاب رسول الله

TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r5.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Qatada, a Companion, reports the Prophet saying God created Adam and drew creation from his back, some destined for Paradise and some for Hell; the continuation asks what deeds people should perform.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#11/r5.anchor: عن عبد الرحمان بن قتادة السلمي وكان من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يقول

TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r1.claim: When asked what to do after hearing that some were destined for Paradise and others for Hell, the Prophet answers: act according to the sites of destiny.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r1.anchor: فقال رجل يا رسول الله فعلى ماذا نعمل؟ قال على مواقع القدر

TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r2.claim: The Prophet's answer does not cancel choice: God decreed outcomes through our choices, so deeds remain ours while occurring in accordance with decree.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r2.anchor: فأجابه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بأن هذا قدر منه تعالى وأن أعمالنا في عين أنا نعملها وهي منسوبة إلينا

TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r3.claim: Abu Ja'far explains that the human fitra is innate knowledge of God; he says the descendants were brought from Adam like particles, shown God, and thereby came to know their Lord.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r3.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال سألته عن قول الله عز وجل { حنفاء لله غير مشركين }

TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r4.claim: The Prophet says every newborn is born with fitra, meaning knowledge that God is the child's Creator, and the author connects this to the Qur'anic statement that people identify God as creator.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#12/r4.anchor: وقال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r1.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits the middle of Zurarah's report in the same wording, supporting the author's account of the verse's literal witnessing and address against those who deny it.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r1.anchor: وروي وسط الحديث العياشي في تفسيره عن زرارة بعين اللفظ

TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r2.claim: In a version transmitted in al-Ma'ani, Abu Ja'far's wording is that God showed them His creation rather than Himself.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r2.anchor: عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام إلا أنه قال فعرفهم وأراهم صنعه بدل قوله فعرفهم وأراهم نفسه

TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r3.claim: Al-Tabatabai suspects that the alternate wording was deliberately paraphrased to avoid an imagined implication of corporeality; he calls the change corrupting and prefers the wording in al-Kafi and al-Ayyashi, which has no connection to corporeality.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r3.anchor: ولعله من تغيير اللفظ قصدا للنقل بالمعنى زعما أن ظاهر اللفظ يوهم التجسم وفيه إفساد اللفظ والمعنى جميعا

TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r4.claim: Zurarah reports that knowledge was fixed in people's hearts, they forgot the covenant scene but will recall it, and otherwise no one would know their Creator and Provider.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r4.anchor: عن ابن بكير عن زرارة قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن قول الله { وإذ أخذ ربك } الآية قال ثبتت المعرفة في قلوبهم

TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r5.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r5.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn saw no objection to coitus interruptus, citing the covenant: everyone from whom God took a covenant will emerge, even if conceived on a hard stone.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r5.anchor: قال كان علي بن الحسين عليه السلام لا يرى بالعزل بأسا

TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r6.claim: The author notes that the report is also transmitted from Ali ibn al-Husayn by Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn Jarir, and that a similar report is attributed to the Prophet through Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r6.anchor: وروى هذا المعنى أيضا عن سعيد بن منصور وابن مردويه عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r7.claim: Because the reports about the primordial realm are so numerous, the author omits most after citing enough to convey their meaning and reserves reports about the prophets' covenant for another section.
TABATABAI:7:172-174#13/r7.anchor: وأعلم أن الروايات في الذر كثيرة جدا وقد تركنا إيراد أكثرها لوفاء ما أوردنا من ذلك بمعناها

ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r1.claim: The temporal particle idh is accusative as the object of a command to remember the time God took the descendants of Adam.
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r1.anchor: المعنى واذكر (إذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم)

ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r2.claim: Min ẓuhūrihim is appositional to min banī Ādam; the phrase means God took all their descendants.
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r2.anchor: (من ظهورهم) بدل من قوله: (من بني آدم)

ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r3.claim: One view says God created people as tiny particles from Adam's loins and made them testify to His oneness.
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم: خلق الله الناس كالذر من صلب آدم

ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r4.claim: This could mean that God gave beings like particles the understanding needed to grasp His command, as in the ant's speech and the mountains' praise.
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r4.anchor: وهذا جائز أن يكون جعل لأمثال الذر فهما تعقل به أمره

ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r5.claim: Every child is born with monotheism in the heart, until the parents make the child Jewish or Christian.
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r5.anchor: وكل مولود يولد على الفطرة معناه أنه يولد وفي قلبه توحيد الله

ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r6.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r6.claim: Another view takes the verse to mean that God brought Adam's descendants out of one another's backs.
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r6.anchor: وقال قوم: معناه أن الله جل ثناؤه

ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r7.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r7.claim: On this view, every adult knows God is one because creation proves His oneness; otherwise disbelievers would have no proof against them, and God has shown His unity through creation.
ZAJJAJ:v2p389/r7.anchor: أن كل بالغ يعلم أن الله واحد، لأن كل ما خلق الله تعالى دليل على توحيده

TABRISI:7:173/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:173/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and the Kufans read dhurriyyatahum in the singular form; the remaining readers use the plural.
TABRISI:7:173/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأهل الكوفة ذريتهم على التوحيد والباقون ذرياتهم على الجمع

TABRISI:7:173/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
TABRISI:7:173/r2.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads أن يقولوا in the third person, while the other readers use the second person.
TABRISI:7:173/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو أن يقولوا أو يقولوا بالياء والباقون بالتاء

TABRISI:7:173/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:7:173/r3.claim: Abu ʿAli explains that dhurriyya can be collective or singular; he cites the plural use in 7:173 and 17:3 and singular use in 3:38–39 and 19:5–6.
TABRISI:7:173/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: الذرية قد يكون جمعا وقد يكون واحدا فمما جاء فيه جمعا قوله

TABRISI:7:173/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:7:173/r4.claim: Abu ʿAli's plural example is the phrase “offspring after them” (7:173).

TABRISI:7:173/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173/r5.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:7:173/r5.claim: Abu ʿAli's singular example is a prayer for good offspring (3:38).
TABRISI:7:173/r5.anchor:
رب هب لي من لدنك ذرية طيبة
[آل عمران: 38]

TABRISI:7:173/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
TABRISI:7:173/r6.claim: Abu ʿAmr uses the third-person reading because the preceding discourse is in the third person; the second-person reading is also apt because the verse directly addresses the people, and the absent are its addressees in meaning.
TABRISI:7:173/r6.anchor: فلأن الذي تقدم من الكلام على الغيبة ومن قرأ بالتاء فلأنه جرى في الكلام خطاب أيضا

TABRISI:7:173/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:173/r7.claim: “From their backs” is an apposition to “from the children of Adam,” meaning God took their descendants from human backs.
TABRISI:7:173/r7.anchor: من ظهورهم بدل من قوله من بني آدم والمعنى أخذ ربك من ظهور بني آدم ذريتهم

TABRISI:7:173/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:173/r8.claim: أن تقولوا is understood as “lest you say” or “for fear that you say,” as in similar constructions discussed earlier.
TABRISI:7:173/r8.anchor: تقديره كراهة أن تقولوا أو لئلا تقولوا

TABRISI:7:173/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:173/r9.claim: After discussing scriptural covenants, God now mentions covenants made through reason, combining revealed and rational proofs to establish the case.
TABRISI:7:173/r9.anchor: ما أخذ على الخلق من المواثيق بعقولهم عقيب ما ذكره من المواثيق التي في الكتب جمعا بين دلائل السمع والعقل

TABRISI:7:173/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173/r10.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
TABRISI:7:173/r10.claim: One interpretation says God extracted Adam's descendants from his loins as tiny particles, presented them to Adam, and covenanted that they worship Him alone; He also assigned their provisions.
TABRISI:7:173/r10.anchor: أن الله تعالى أخرج ذرية آدم من صلبه كهيئة الذر فعرضهم على آدم

TABRISI:7:173/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173/r11.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
TABRISI:7:173/r11.claim: In this account the descendants affirm God's lordship, the angels witness, and God makes the descendants intelligent enough to hear and understand His address.
TABRISI:7:173/r11.anchor: ثم قال لهم ألست بربكم قالوا بلى شهدنا أنك ربنا

TABRISI:7:173/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173/r12.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
TABRISI:7:173/r12.claim: The account says the particles returned to Adam's loins; those who remained Muslim preserved the original fitra, while unbelievers changed from it, supported by both raised and stopped reports.
TABRISI:7:173/r12.anchor: وكل من ثبت على الإسلام فهو على الفطرة الأولى ومن كفر وجحد فقد تغير عن الفطرة الأول

TABRISI:7:173/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173/r13.speaker: المحققون
TABRISI:7:173/r13.claim: The scholars who verify the issue reject particle-extraction as the verse's meaning because its wording says descendants came from Adam's children and their backs, not from Adam and his back.
TABRISI:7:173/r13.anchor: ورد المحققون هذا التأويل وقالوا: إنه مما يشهد ظاهر القرآن بخلافه لأنه تعالى قال وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم ولم يقل من آدم

TABRISI:7:172-174/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:172-174/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:172-174/r1.claim: The covenant was made so people could not plead ignorance or excuse their own shirk by saying their forefathers were polytheists and they merely followed them.
TABRISI:7:172-174/r1.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى بأنه فعل ذلك لئلا يقولوا إنهم كانوا عن ذلك غافلين أو يعتذروا بشرك آبائهم

TABRISI:7:172-174/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:172-174/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:172-174/r2.claim: The particle interpretation is problematic: unintelligent particles could not know monotheism, while intelligent ones should remember the covenant; that memory is needed for it to count as evidence.
TABRISI:7:172-174/r2.anchor: فإن لم يجعلهم عقلاء فلا يصح أن يعرفوا التوحيد وأن يفهموا خطاب الله تعالى وإن جعلهم عقلاء وأخذ عليهم الميثاق فيجب أن يتذكروا ذلك

TABRISI:7:172-174/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:172-174/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:172-174/r3.claim: It is implausible for a vast company of intelligent people to forget shared knowledge; people in Paradise remember worldly events, and allowing such forgetting invites transmigration.
TABRISI:7:172-174/r3.anchor: ولأنه لا يجوز أن ينسى الجمع الكثير والجم الغفير من العقلاء شيئا كانوا عرفوه وميزوه حتى لا يذكره واحد منهم

TABRISI:7:172-174/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:172-174/r4.speaker: علي بن عيسى عن أبي بكر بن الإخشيد
TABRISI:7:172-174/r4.claim: Ibn al-Ikhshid allows the particle report to be true but not the verse's interpretation; its benefit is to inspire noble habits of gratitude and recognition of God's lordship, like the report that people are born on fitra.
TABRISI:7:172-174/r4.anchor: وحكي عن علي بن عيسى عن أبي بكر بن الإخشيد أنه جوز أن يكون خبر الذر صحيحا غير أنه قال ليس تأويل الآية على ذلك

TABRISI:7:172-174/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:172-174/r5.speaker: أبو الهذيل
TABRISI:7:172-174/r5.claim: Abu al-Hudhayl says al-Hasan al-Basri and his companions held that children's bliss in Paradise rewards their faith in the particle covenant.
TABRISI:7:172-174/r5.anchor: وحكى أبو الهذيل في كتاب الحجة أن الحسن البصري وأصحابه كانوا يذهبون إلى أن نعيم الأطفال في الجنة ثواب عن الإيمان في الذر

TABRISI:7:172-174/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:172-174/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:172-174/r6.claim: A second interpretation takes the covenant as human development from parental loins through the womb, successive stages, and eventual life as morally responsible people.
TABRISI:7:172-174/r6.anchor: أن الله سبحانه أخرج بني آدم من أصلاب آبائهم إلى أرحام أمهاتهم ثم رقاهم درجة بعد درجة وعلقة ثم مضغة

TABRISI:7:172-174/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:172-174/r7.speaker: الرماني وأبو مسلم وابن الإخشيد
TABRISI:7:172-174/r7.claim: In the second interpretation, God's signs in human creation make people recognize His unity as though He had addressed them and they had answered; this is figurative witnessing, not a literal scene.
TABRISI:7:172-174/r7.anchor: دلهم بخلقه على توحيده وإنما أشهدهم على أنفسهم بذلك لما جعل في عقولهم من الأدلة الدالة على وحدانيته

TABRISI:7:173-174/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173-174/r1.speaker: الرماني وأبو مسلم وابن الإخشيد
TABRISI:7:173-174/r1.claim: The figurative interpretation is illustrated by God's command to heaven and earth, which they answered though no literal speech or reply occurred (41:11).
TABRISI:7:173-174/r1.anchor: فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين

TABRISI:7:173-174/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173-174/r2.speaker: الرماني وأبو مسلم وابن الإخشيد
TABRISI:7:173-174/r2.claim: Likewise, unbelievers “witness against themselves” by manifest conduct though they do not verbally confess unbelief (9:17).
TABRISI:7:173-174/r2.anchor: ومعلوم أن الكفار لم يعترفوا بالكفر بألسنتهم لكنه لما ظهر منهم ظهورا لا يتمكنون من دفعه

TABRISI:7:173-174/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173-174/r3.speaker: شاعر
TABRISI:7:173-174/r3.claim: An unnamed poem gives eyes a speaking role: they say “we hear and obey” and shed tears, illustrating figurative testimony.
TABRISI:7:173-174/r3.anchor: وقالت له العينان سمعا وطاعة وحدرتا كالدر لما يثقب

TABRISI:7:173-174/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173-174/r4.speaker: خطيب
TABRISI:7:173-174/r4.claim: A preacher's example says to ask the earth who split its rivers and planted its trees: if it does not answer in speech, it answers through reflection.
TABRISI:7:173-174/r4.anchor: سل الأرض من شق أنهارك وغرس أشجارك وأينع ثمارك فإن لم تجبك حوارا أجابتك اعتبارا

TABRISI:7:173-174/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173-174/r5.speaker: الجبائي والقاضي
TABRISI:7:173-174/r5.claim: A third view says God gave a particular group of Adam's descendants mature intellect and had messengers address them about knowing God and obeying Him; they affirmed the covenant.
TABRISI:7:173-174/r5.anchor: أنه تعالى إنما عنى بذلك جماعة من ذرية آدم خلقهم وأكمل عقولهم وقررهم على ألسن رسله ع بمعرفته وبما يجب من طاعته

TABRISI:7:173-174/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173-174/r6.speaker: الجبائي والقاضي
TABRISI:7:173-174/r6.claim: This view concerns only some people, not all: they had polytheist ancestors, and children directly from Adam were not taken from the backs of human ancestors.
TABRISI:7:173-174/r6.anchor: وهذا يكون في قوم خاص من بني آدم ولا يدخل جميعهم فيه لأن المؤمن لا يدخل فيه لأنه بين أن هؤلاء المأخوذ ميثاقهم كان لهم سلف في الشرك

TABRISI:7:173-174/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173-174/r7.speaker: الأزهري عن بعضهم
TABRISI:7:173-174/r7.claim: One grammatical view makes “we witnessed” the angels' words, so people would not claim ignorance; al-Azhari attributes this to some authorities.
TABRISI:7:173-174/r7.anchor: ذكره الأزهري عن بعضهم وقال إن قوله قالوا بلى تمام الكلام

TABRISI:7:173-174/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173-174/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:173-174/r8.claim: The angel interpretation conflicts with the apparent reading: “they said yes” is complete, the people themselves then say “we witnessed,” and angels have not been mentioned.
TABRISI:7:173-174/r8.anchor: وهذا خلاف الظاهر وما عليه المفسرون لأن الكل قالوا شهدنا من قول من قال بلى

TABRISI:7:173-174/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:173-174/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:173-174/r9.claim: “Lest you say at Resurrection that we were unaware” means you failed to notice the proof, had no established argument, or lacked mature reasoning.
TABRISI:7:173-174/r9.anchor: لم نتنبه عليه ولم تقم لنا حجة به ولم تكمل عقولنا فنفكر فيه

THALABI:v4p302#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p302#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v4p302#2/r1.claim: The commentators say God created Adam, wiped his back, and brought out all of his descendants for the covenant.
THALABI:v4p302#2/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: لما خلق الله عز وجل آدم مسح ظهره وأخرج منه ذريته كلهم

THALABI:v4p302#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p302#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p302#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās locates the covenant in Wādī Nuʿmān beside ʿArafa.
THALABI:v4p302#2/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: يسكن نعمان واد إلى جنب عرفة

THALABI:v4p302#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p302#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p302#2/r3.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās locates it at Barhābā in India, where Adam descended.
THALABI:v4p302#2/r3.anchor: وروي فيه أيضا أن ذلك [برهبا] أرض بالهند وهو الموضع الذي أهبط الله فيه آدم

THALABI:v4p302#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p302#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v4p302#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī locates the covenant between Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif.

THALABI:v4p302#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p302#2/r5.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v4p302#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says God brought Adam out of Paradise, wiped his back, and drew out his descendants, placing dark descendants from his left side among those sentenced to the Fire.
THALABI:v4p302#2/r5.anchor: وقال السدي: أخرج الله آدم من الجنة ولم يهبط من السماء ثم مسح ظهره وأخرج ذريته

THALABI:v4p302#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p302#2/r6.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v4p302#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says God declared Himself the only Lord, promised messengers and a revealed book, and all descendants testified, some sincerely and some under dissimulation.
THALABI:v4p302#2/r6.anchor: وقال لهم: جميعا أعلموا أن لا إله غيري وأنا ربكم لا رب لكم غيري فلا تشركوا بي شيئا

THALABI:v4p302#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p302#2/r7.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v4p302#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddī adds that each person's lifespan, provision, and account were specified at the covenant.
THALABI:v4p302#2/r7.anchor: فأخذوا بذلك مواثيقهم وسميت آجالهم وأرزاقهم وحسابهم

THALABI:v4p302#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p302#2/r8.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v4p302#2/r8.claim: When Adam saw unequal wealth and appearance, he asked God why they were not made equal; God said He wished to be thanked.
THALABI:v4p302#2/r8.anchor: فنظر إليهم آدم، ورأى منهم الغني والفقير وحسن الصورة ودون ذلك، فقال: رب لولا سويت بينهم

THALABI:v4p303/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p303/r1.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v4p303/r1.claim: The covenant report says prophets appeared among Adam's descendants like lamps; Adam recognized David's light, learned his lifespan was sixty years, and donated forty of his own years to him.
THALABI:v4p303/r1.anchor: قالوا: وفيهم الأنبياء يومئذ أمثال السرج فرأى آدم نورا ساطعا فقال: من هذا؟ فقال: هذا داود نبي من ذريتك

THALABI:v4p303/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p303/r2.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v4p303/r2.claim: Adam later denied giving David forty years; the report says his descendants inherited his denial, forgetfulness, and error.
THALABI:v4p303/r2.anchor: فلما استكمل آدم تسعمائة وستين سنة جاء ملك الموت

THALABI:v4p303/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p303/r3.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v4p303/r3.claim: After affirming monotheism, God returned the descendants to Adam's loins; everyone bound by the covenant will be born, with no increase or decrease.
THALABI:v4p303/r3.anchor: فلما قررهم بتوحيده وآثر بعضهم على بعض أعادهم إلى صلبه فلا تقوم الساعة حتى يولد كل من أخذ ميثاقه

THALABI:v4p303/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p303/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p303/r4.claim: The verse's syntax means God took descendants from the backs of Adam's children; Adam's back is omitted because the descendants came through successive generations in the same way.
THALABI:v4p303/r4.anchor: ونظم الآية: وإذا أخذ ربك من ظهر بني آدم ذريتهم، ولم يذكر أمر آدم

THALABI:v4p303/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p303/r5.speaker: أهل مكة والكوفة
THALABI:v4p303/r5.claim: Readers of Mecca and Kufa read ذريتهم as a singular; the other readers use the plural form ذرياتهم.
THALABI:v4p303/r5.anchor: قرأ أهل مكة والكوفة: ذريتهم بغير ألف على الواحد، وقرأ الباقون على الجمع بالألف

THALABI:v4p303/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p303/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p303/r6.claim: God's question ألست بربكم is a question that confirms the testimony.
THALABI:v4p303/r6.anchor: وأشهدهم على أنفسهم وقال لهم ألست بربكم سؤال تقرير

THALABI:v4p303/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p303/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وابن محيصن وأبو عمرو
THALABI:v4p303/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Muḥayṣin, and Abū ʿAmr read يقولوا, while other readers use تقولوا to match the preceding address.
THALABI:v4p303/r7.anchor: قرأ ابن عباس وابن محيصن وأبو عمرو: (يقولوا) بالباء، والباقون بالتاء كقوله: ألست بربكم

THALABI:v4p303/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p303/r8.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v4p303/r8.claim: Al-Suddī says شهدنا is God's report that He and His angels witnessed humanity's acknowledgment.
THALABI:v4p303/r8.anchor: فقال السدي: خبر من قوله تعالى عن نفسه وعن ملائكته أنهم شهدوا على إقرار بني آدم

THALABI:v4p303/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p303/r9.speaker: آخرون
THALABI:v4p303/r9.claim: Others say شهدنا records the descendants' own acknowledgment as God made some of them witnesses over others.
THALABI:v4p303/r9.anchor: وقال الآخرون: بل ذلك على إقرار بني آدم حين أشهد بعضهم على بعض

THALABI:v4p303/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p303/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p303/r10.claim: The testimony prevents people from pleading ignorance of the covenant or blaming inherited polytheism and asking to be punished for their ancestors' falsehood.
THALABI:v4p303/r10.anchor: يعني أن لا يقولوا يوم القيامة إنا كنا عن هذا الميثاق والإقرار غافلين أو تقولوا إنما أشرك آباؤنا من قبل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses idh as accusative and supplies an imperative: remember when your Lord took the covenant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r1.anchor: موضع {إذ} نصب، المعنى (¬3) واذكر {وإذ أخذ ربك}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats from their backs as an appositive clarifying from the children of Adam, meaning from the backs of Adam's descendants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r2.anchor: {من ظهورهم} بدل من قوله {من بني آدم}، والمعنى: وإذ أخذ ربك من ظهور بني آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r3.speaker: الكناني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r3.claim: Al-Kinānī says Adam's back is left unstated because all people are his descendants, extracted from his back through successive generations from one another.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r3.anchor: لم يذكر ظهر آدم، وإنما أخرجوا جميعا من ظهره؛ لأن الله تعالى أخرج ذرية آدم بعضهم من ظهور بعض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r4.claim: The word dhurriyya is read in a plural form; its discussion was given under God's words about Abraham's offspring.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r4.anchor: وقرئ (¬3) {ذريتهم} جمعا، وقد ذكرنا معنى الذرية والكلام فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r5.claim: Dhurriyya can denote one person or a group, like bashar; this explains why a singular form can carry collective meaning without a plural ending.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r5.anchor: وبينا أن الذرية تقع على الواحد والجمع، فمن أفردها هاهنا فلأنه قد استغنى عن جمعه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r6.claim: The unpluralized word bashar likewise applies to one or many, so the same usage accounts for an unpluralized dhurriyya.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r6.anchor: وكما لم يجمع (بشر) بتصحيح ولا تكسير كذلك لا تجمع الذرية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r7.claim: Those who read dhurriyyāt argue that pluralizing is sound whether dhurriyya is singular or collective, just as broken plurals themselves can take a further plural.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r7.anchor: ومن جمع قال: إن الذرية إن كان واحدا فلا إشكال في جواز الجمع فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r8.speaker: مسلم بن يسار الجهني عن عمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r8.claim: The first interpretation, held by commentators and traditionists, cites ʿUmar reporting the Prophet: God wiped Adam's back, extracted descendants, assigned some to Paradise and some to Hell, and each was made to do the corresponding people's deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r8.anchor: مسلم (¬1) بن يسار الجهني: (أن عمر - رضي الله عنه - سئل عن هذه الآية فقال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r9.claim: The Prophet's reported answer describes God creating Adam, wiping his back, extracting descendants, and assigning them to Paradise or Hell with deeds matching their destination.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p441/r9.anchor: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - سئل عنها فقال: "إن الله خلق آدم ثم مسح ظهره فاستخرج منه ذرية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r1.claim: When asked what deeds are for, the Prophet says God employs the person destined for Paradise in its people's deeds until death, and likewise the person destined for Hell in its people's deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r1.anchor: فقال رجل: يا رسول الله ففيم العمل؟ فقال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: "إن الله إذا خلق العبد للجنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that when God created Adam and wiped his back, every descendant's soul to be created until the Resurrection fell from him; the source notes that the report continues at length.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r2.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: "لما خلق الله آدم مسح على ظهره فسقط من ظهره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that God shook Adam and showed him all the descendants He had created through the Resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء في: قوله: {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم} (يريد: نفض (¬3) آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God extracted Adam's descendants from his loins like tiny particles, asked who their Lord was, received their affirmation, then returned them to his loins until each was born without addition or loss.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: (إن الله خلق آدم ثم أخرج ذريته من صلبه مثل الذر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r5.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says God gathered and formed them, made them speak, and took their covenant; He promised messengers and scriptures to remind them, and they confessed that He alone is God and Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r5.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: (جمعهم يومئذ، ثم صورهم، ثم استنطقهم وأخذ عليهم العهد والميثاق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says God struck Adam's back and brought out every soul destined for Paradise pure and white, and every soul destined for Hell black, as specks.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r6.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: (ضرب الله ظهر آدم فخرجت كل نفس مخلوقة للجنة بيضاء نقية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r7.speaker: القرظي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r7.claim: Al-Quraẓī says the spirits acknowledged faith and knowledge of God before their bodies were created.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r7.anchor: وقال القرظي: (أقر له بالإيمان والمعرفة الأرواح قبل أن يخلق أجسادها)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r8.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r8.claim: Muqātil describes white descendants drawn from Adam's right back and black ones from his left, the former promised Paradise by mercy and the latter Hell, before all were returned to Adam's loins until the covenant generations emerge from men and women.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r8.anchor: وقال مقاتل: (إن الله مسح صفحة ظهر آدم اليمنى فأخرج منه ذرية بيضاء كهيئة الذر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r9.claim: Muqātil links those who broke the first covenant to God's statement that He found most of them without a covenant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p444/r9.anchor: قال الله تعالى فيمن نقض العهد الأول: {وما وجدنا لأكثرهم من عهد}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r1.speaker: عكرمة والكلبي وسعيد بن جبير وسعيد بن المسيب والضحاك وأبو صالح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r1.claim: The source says these authorities also hold the previously described extraction-of-descendants interpretation, identifying it as the position of the exegetes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r1.anchor: وهذا أيضا قول عكرمة (¬3) والكلبي وسعيد بن جبير و [سعيد (¬4) بن المسيب] والضحاك (¬5) وأبي صالح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r2.claim: Abū Isḥāq allows that God gave the tiny particles understanding, as in the speech of the ant and the mountains and birds glorifying with David.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r2.anchor: جائز أن يكون الله تعالى جعل لأمثال (¬7) الذر فهما يعقل به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r3.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī attributes to hadith scholars and senior scholars the view that descendants emerged from Adam's and their fathers' loins as particles, accepted God's covenant with intellects implanted in them, as other creatures were made to understand speech or respond.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r3.anchor: مذهب أصحاب الحديث وكبراء أهل العلم في هذه الآية هو: أن الله عز وجل أخرج ذريات آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r4.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r4.claim: The author of the نظم says the Prophet's report about extracting descendants from Adam does not conflict with the verse's mention of descendants' backs, since they descend from one another.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r4.anchor: ليس بين قول النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -:"إن الله مسح ظهر آدم فأخرج منه ذريته" و [بين] (¬2) الآية اختلاف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r5.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r5.claim: The covenant establishes proof against every person, including those who did not reach maturity; adults also receive proof through signs, messengers, warnings, exhortations, and transmitted lessons.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r5.anchor: قد أثبت الحجة على كل منفوس ممن بلغ، وممن لم يبلغ بالميثاق الذي أخذه عليهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r6.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r6.claim: Some commentators say the blessed descendants acknowledged willingly while the wretched acknowledged under pressure, connecting this to submission by choice or compulsion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r6.anchor: إن أهل السعادة من الذرية أقروا طوعا، وإن أهل الشقاوة أقروا تقية وكرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r7.claim: Muqātil says a child who dies young enters Paradise through knowledge of the first covenant, while a person reaching reason still must believe; the covenant remains proof against them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل: من مات صغيرا دخل الجنة بمعرفته بالميثاق (¬2) الأول، ومن بلغ العقل لم يغن عنه الميثاق الأول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r8.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says Muqātil's account represents the view that children of polytheists enter Paradise; those rejecting that outcome say the wretched acknowledged unwillingly, which did not benefit them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r8.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره مذهب من يقول: إن أطفال المشركين يدخلون (¬4) الجنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r9.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the question Aren't I your Lord? as an affirmative demand that they acknowledge His lordship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p447/r9.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬5): (المعنى قال: {ألست بربكم} وهو إيجاب للإقرار عليهم بربوبيته)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says their yes is an answer to God, affirming His lordship and their own servanthood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (هو جواب منهم له وإقرار له بالربوبية ولأنفسهم بالعبودية)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī says that after the descendants acknowledged, God told the angels to bear witness, and the words We have witnessed record that command.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: (8) (لما أقروا، قال الله للملائكة: اشهدوا. فقال: {شهدنا})

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r3.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, Ibn ʿAbbās says the angels declared that they witnessed the descendants' acknowledgment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (قالت (¬3) الملائكة: شهدنا على إقراركم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r4.claim: Al-Suddī takes the verse as God's report that He and His angels witnessed Adam's descendants acknowledge Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: (هذا خبر من الله تعالى عن نفسه وملائكته أنهم شهدوا على إقرار بني آدم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r5.claim: On these interpretations, pausing after their yes is appropriate because the descendants' speech has ended.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r5.anchor: فعلى هذه الأقوال (¬6) يحسن الوقف على قوله: {بلى}؛ لأن كلام الذرية قد انقطع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r6.claim: The Kufan analysis attaches lest you say to We have witnessed, supplying the omitted negative particle; the example from al-Quṭāmī means lest it be sold.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r6.anchor: أي شهدنا عليهم بالإقرار لئلا تقولوا، فأسقط (لا) (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r7.speaker: القطامي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r7.claim: Al-Quṭāmī's line uses the construction with an understood not: its phrase means that it should not be sold.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r7.anchor: رأينا ما يرى البصراء فيها ... فآلينا عليها أن تباعا (¬9)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r8.claim: The Basran analysis instead supplies an omitted noun: they witnessed from aversion to your saying this, rather than omitting la.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r8.anchor: وعند البصريين المحذوف مضاف بتقدير: شهدنا كراهة أن تقولوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r9.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r9.claim: Abū Bakr also allows attaching lest you say to He made them testify; he calls this clearer and says the pause after We have witnessed is then invalid.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r9.anchor: ويمكن أن تعلق {أن} ب (أشهدهم) وهذا أوضح في التأويل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r10.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r10.claim: Some take We have witnessed as the descendants' own words, meaning they testified about themselves; on this view it does not attach to their yes, but lest you say attaches to He made them testify.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم: قوله: {شهدنا} من كلام الذرية، والمعنى: شهدنا على أنفسنا بهذا الإقرار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r11.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r11.claim: The author of the نظم gives another view: the covenant story ends at their yes, then God begins a report of what the polytheists will say at Judgment, with We have witnessed meaning We testify.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p450/r11.anchor: وذكر صاحب النظم] (¬3) وجها آخر في قوله: {شهدنا} عن بعضهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r1.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r1.claim: On the نظم author's alternative, We testify anticipates the polytheists' Judgment-day words; the covenant passage concerns all creatures, while the following story singles out polytheists.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r1.anchor: شهد الخطيئة حين يلقى ربه (¬5) # أي: يشهد، فيكون تأويله نشهد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads both lest you say and or you say with third-person yāʾ because the preceding wording speaks about them; the other readers use second-person tāʾ because the passage has shifted to direct address. Both are sound.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r2.anchor: واختلف القراء في قوله: {أن تقولوا} [الأعراف:172]، {أو تقولوا} [الأعراف: 173]، فقرأ (¬3) أبو عمرو بالياء (¬4) جميعا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r3.claim: The commentators call the covenant a reminder and proof for all morally responsible people, preventing unbelievers from claiming they were unaware of it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون: (هذه (¬7) الآية تذكير بما أخذ على جميع المكلفين من الميثاق، واحتجاج عليهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r4.claim: Forgetting the covenant does not invalidate the proof once God has disclosed it through a miracle-bearing Messenger; a truthful report stands in the mind as recollection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r4.anchor: نسيانهم لذلك لا يسقط الاحتجاج بعد أن أخبر الله تعالى عن أخذ ذلك عليهم على لسان صاحب المعجزة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r5.speaker: عوف
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p453/r5.claim: ʿAwf says people will remember the covenant on the Day of Resurrection.

ASAD-NOTES:7:171#n139/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:171#n139/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:171#n139/r1.claim: Although the original uses past tense, Asad renders the exchange in present tense to show the metaphorical question and answer continually recurring.
ASAD-NOTES:7:171#n139/r1.anchor: this passage is in the past tense ("He brought forth", "He asked them", etc.), thus stressing the continuous recurrence

ASAD-NOTES:7:171#n139/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:171#n139/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:171#n139/r2.claim: Every sane person has inborn awareness of the Supreme Power through fitrah; self-indulgence or harmful surroundings may later obscure this instinctive cognition.
ASAD-NOTES:7:171#n139/r2.anchor: the ability to perceive the existence of the Supreme Power is inborn in human nature (fitrah)

ASAD-NOTES:7:171#n139/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:171#n139/r3.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:171#n139/r3.claim: God's speaking and humanity's answer are metonyms for God's creative act and each person's existential response to it.
ASAD-NOTES:7:171#n139/r3.anchor: God's "speaking" and man's "answering" is a metonym for the creative act of God and of man's existential response to it

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r1.claim: God brought Adam's descendants out from one another's backs, generation by generation as children are born from parents, ultimately drawing them all from Adam's loins like particles.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r1.anchor: أخرج الله تعالى ذرية آدم بعضهم من ظهور بعض على نحو ما يتوالد الأبناء من الآباء، وجميع ذلك أخرجه من صلب آدم مثل الذر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r2.claim: God took their covenant that He is their Creator and they are created beings; they acknowledged and accepted it after being endowed with reason.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r2.anchor: وأخذ عليهم الميثاق أنه خالقهم، وأنهم مصنوعون، فاعترفوا بذلك وقبلوا ذلك بعد أن ركب فيهم عقولا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r3.claim: God's testimony against them was His asking whether He was their Lord.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r3.anchor: وأشهدهم على أنفسهم ألست بربكم } أي: قال: ألست بربكم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r4.claim: The angels' statement that they witnessed refers to witnessing the people's acknowledgment of God's lordship.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:172-173/r4.anchor: قالوا بلى } فأقروا له بالربوبية، فقالت الملائكة عند ذلك { شهدنا } أي: على إقراركم

BURHAN:v4p262/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p262/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p262/r3.claim: In the covenant question, which is an interrogative for affirmation rather than a genuine question, the negative form is answered as ordinary negation with balā.
BURHAN:v4p262/r3.anchor: فان الاستفهام هنا ليس على حقيقته بل هو للتقرير

BURHAN:v4p262/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p262/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BURHAN:v4p262/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they would have disbelieved had they answered naʿam, since naʿam confirms what follows the interrogative hamza, whether negative or affirmative.
BURHAN:v4p262/r4.anchor: وكذلك قال ابن عباس لو قالوا نعم لكفروا ووجهه إن نعم تصديق لما بعد الهمزة نفيا كان أو اثباتا

BURHAN:v4p262/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p262/r5.speaker: السهيلي وغيره
BURHAN:v4p262/r5.claim: Al-Suhaylī and others object that a confirmatory question is certainly affirmative, so naʿam should confirm it as it would confirm ‘Did I not give you a dirham?’
BURHAN:v4p262/r5.anchor: ونازع السهيلي وغيره في المحكى عن ابن عباس من وجه أن الاستفهام التقريري اثبات قطعا وحينئذ فنعم في الايجاب تصديق له

BURHAN:v4p262/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p262/r6.speaker: الصفار
BURHAN:v4p262/r6.claim: Al-Ṣaffār answers that naʿam after a negative question is ambiguous: it can deny the premise or affirm it, so the respondents followed the wording with balā.
BURHAN:v4p262/r6.anchor: ذكره الصفار إن المقرر قد يوافقه المقرر فيما يدعيه وقدلا فلو قيل في جواب الم أعطك نعم لم يدر

BURHAN:v4p262/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p262/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p262/r7.claim: The basic rule is that balā answers a negation, including a negation understood from context rather than stated explicitly.
BURHAN:v4p262/r7.anchor: ماذكرنا من كون بلى انما يجاب بها النفي

BURHAN:v4p262/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p262/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
BURHAN:v4p262/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya restricts balā to following a negation that is confirmatory; other grammarians simply say it answers negation.
BURHAN:v4p262/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عطية حق بلى إن تجيء بعد نفي عليه تقرير وهذا القيد الذي ذكره في النفي لم يذكره غيره

BURHAN:v4p353/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p353/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p353/r6.claim: As a response particle, la contradicts yes or bala; after a confirming question the answer is bala, while a genuine question takes la or naʿam.
BURHAN:v4p353/r6.anchor: الثالثة إن تكون جوابية اي رد في الجواب مناقض

BURHAN:v1p373#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r1.claim: For ten occurrences, many readers and linguists prefer stopping at بلى because it answers the preceding statement without syntactic dependence on what follows; some allow beginning there.
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r1.anchor: أحدها ما يختار فيه كثير من القراء وأهل اللغة الوقف عليها لأنها جواب لما قبلها غير متعلق بما بعدها

BURHAN:v2p334/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p334/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p334/r1.claim: The verse is an example of a negative interrogative used as a confirming question whose intended sense is affirmative: I am your Lord.
BURHAN:v2p334/r1.anchor: وأمثلته كثيرة كقوله تعالى ﴿ ألست بربكم ﴾

BURHAN:v2p334/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p334/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p334/r2.claim: The example raises a response problem: if the statement means affirmation, نعم seems possible, though it is said that answering نعم would have been unbelief.
BURHAN:v2p334/r2.anchor: واعلم ان في جعلهم الآية الاولى من هذا النوع اشكالا لانه لو خرج الكلام عن النفي لجاز ان يجاب بنعم

BURHAN:v2p334/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p334/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p334/r3.claim: A question about whether the negation exists keeps the negative sense and takes بلى; a confirming question has negative wording but affirmative meaning, allowing بلى by wording or نعم by meaning.
BURHAN:v2p334/r3.anchor: فان كان بالمعنى الاول لم يجز دخول نعم في جوابه اذا اردت ايجابه بل تدخل عليه بلى وان كان بالمعنى الثاني

BURHAN:v2p334/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p334/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p334/r5.claim: This interrogative construction can express bare affirmation, affirmation with boasting, or affirmation with rebuke.
BURHAN:v2p334/r5.anchor: واعلم ان هذا النوع ياتي على وجوه الاول مجرد الاثبات

BURHAN:v3p217/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p217/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p217/r5.claim: The author notes the differing formulations: al-A'raf says بلى شهدنا, while al-An'am has the addressed jinn and humans say they bear witness against themselves.
BURHAN:v3p217/r5.anchor: يقصون عليكم آياتي وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا

BURHAN:v4p259/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p259/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p259/r4.claim: In its first use, بلى rejects a preceding negation, affirming the act denied or denying the negation, as in these examples.
BURHAN:v4p259/r4.anchor: لها موضعان أحدهما أن تكون ردا لنفى يقع قبلها

BURHAN:v4p259/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p259/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p259/r5.claim: In its second use, بلى answers a question containing an actual negation by affirming the proposition implied by that question.
BURHAN:v4p259/r5.anchor: والثاني أن تقع جوابا لاستفهام دخل عليه نفى حقيقة

BURHAN:v4p259/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p259/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p259/r6.claim: Thus the answer means that God is their Lord; the same rule is illustrated by the question whether the interlocutor had been a friend.
BURHAN:v4p259/r6.anchor: فهى في هذا الأصل تصديق لما قبلها وفي الأول رد لما قبلها وتكذيب

BURHAN:v2p236/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p236/r1.speaker: المبرد
BURHAN:v2p236/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad says a singular created being should not use a first-person plural pronoun, even inclusively, because it conveys arrogance reserved for God.
BURHAN:v2p236/r1.anchor: وقال المبرد في الكامل لاينبغي ان يستعمل ضمير الجمع في واحد من المخلوقين

BURHAN:v2p236/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p236/r2.speaker: الحريري
BURHAN:v2p236/r2.claim: Al-Hariri recounts an unusual opinion forbidding any created person to say نحن because it implies exaltation.
BURHAN:v2p236/r2.anchor: حكاه الحريري في شرح الملحة عن بعضهم انه منع من اطلاق لفظه نحن

BURHAN:v2p236/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p236/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p236/r3.claim: One explanation makes the divine plural a mark of majesty unavailable to creatures, making royal نحن objectionable; another attributes it to acts carried out through God's creatures, allowing it for those who do not act directly.
BURHAN:v2p236/r3.anchor: فقيل جاءت للعظمة يوصف بها سبحانه وليس لمخلوق ان ينازعه فيها

BURHAN:v2p236/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p236/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p236/r4.claim: A scholar may say نحن نبين because the plural can refer to the scholar together with members of his school.
BURHAN:v2p236/r4.anchor: فأما قول العالم نحن نبين ونحن نشرح فمفسوح له فيه

ITQAN:v2p465/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p465/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p465/r1.claim: The particle بلى is said to have an original alif; alternatives derive it from بل plus an added alif or treat the alif as feminine, citing its imāla.
ITQAN:v2p465/r1.anchor: حرف أصلي الألف وقيل الأصل بل والألف زائدة وقيل هي للتأنيث بدليل إمالتها

ITQAN:v2p465/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p465/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p465/r2.claim: In its first use, بلى answers a preceding denial and reverses it, affirming the proposition the denial rejected.
ITQAN:v2p465/r2.anchor: أحدهما أن تكون ردا لنفي يقع قبلها نحو

ITQAN:v2p465/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p465/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p465/r3.claim: When an interrogative is put to a negative proposition, بلى cancels the negation; this can answer genuine, reproachful, or confirmatory questions.
ITQAN:v2p465/r3.anchor: الثاني أن تقع جوابا لاستفهام دخل على نفي فتفيد إبطاله سواء كان الاستفهام حقيقيا

ITQAN:v2p465/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p465/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
ITQAN:v2p465/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say that answering نعم would have been disbelief: نعم would affirm the negative wording, while بلى rejects it and means, “You are our Lord.”
ITQAN:v2p465/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره لو قالوا نعم كفروا ووجهه أن نعم تصديق للمخبر بنفي أو إيجاب فكأنهم قالوا لست ربنا بخلاف بلى فإنها لإبطال النفي

ITQAN:v2p465/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p465/r5.speaker: السهيلي وغيره
ITQAN:v2p465/r5.claim: Al-Suhayli and others object that a confirmatory question is an affirmative statement, so نعم after it would affirm that statement.
ITQAN:v2p465/r5.anchor: ونازع في ذلك السهيلي وغيره بأن الاستفهام التقريري خبر موجب ولذلك امتنع سيبويه من جعل أم متصلة

ITQAN:v2p465/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p465/r6.speaker: ابن هشام
ITQAN:v2p465/r6.claim: Ibn Hisham says the account faces a problem: بلى is never used to answer an affirmative proposition.
ITQAN:v2p465/r6.anchor: قال ابن هشام ويشكل عليهم أن بلى لا يجاب بها عن الإيجاب اتفاقا

ITQAN:v4p511/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p511/r2.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
ITQAN:v4p511/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet said God took the covenant from Adam at Nuʿman on the Day of ʿArafa, brought out all his descendants, spread them before Him, and asked whether He was their Lord.
ITQAN:v4p511/r2.anchor: وأخرج أحمد والنسائي والحاكم وصححه عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ( إن الله أخذ الميثاق من ظهر آدم بنعمان يوم عرفة فأخرج من صلبه كل ذرية

ITQAN:v4p511/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p511/r3.speaker: ابن عمر عن النبي
ITQAN:v4p511/r3.claim: A weak-chain report from Ibn Umar says the descendants were taken from Adam's back as hair is combed from a head; they answered بلى and the angels testified.
ITQAN:v4p511/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير بسند ضعيف عن ابن عمر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه الآية ( أخذ من ظهره كما يؤخذ بالمشط من الرأس

ITQAN:v1p47#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p47#2/r1.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p47#2/r1.claim: Ibn Hajar notes scholarly attention to Medinan verses found within Meccan suras, while the reverse case—Meccan material in a sura whose revelation concluded in Medina—is rare.
ITQAN:v1p47#2/r1.anchor: وقال ابن حجر في شرح البخاري قد اعتنى بعض الأئمة ببيان ما نزل من الآيات بالمدينة في السور المكية

ITQAN:v1p47#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p47#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p47#2/r2.claim: The author says he will comprehensively list the exceptions he has found, using the first convention for classifying suras and referring readers to his Asbab al-Nuzul for abbreviated evidence.
ITQAN:v1p47#2/r2.anchor: قلت وها أنا أذكر ما وقفت على استثنائه من النوعين مستوعبا ما رأيته من ذلك على الاصطلاح الأول دون الثاني

ITQAN:v1p47#2/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p47#2/r12.speaker: قتادة وغيره
ITQAN:v1p47#2/r12.claim: Qatada says al-Aʿraf is Meccan except the verse about the town; another view says the passage from there through the covenant verse is Medinan.
ITQAN:v1p47#2/r12.anchor: الأعراف أخرج أبو الشيخ بن حيان عن قتادة قال الأعراف مكية إلا آية ﴿ واسألهم عن القرية ﴾ وقال غيره من هنا إلى ﴿ وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم ﴾ مدني

KHATTABI:v1p31/r1.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p31/r1.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p31/r1.claim: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl’s distinction is valid when contrasted: “sit” follows reclining, whereas “sit down” follows standing; the paired terms are not interchangeable in every context.
KHATTABI:v1p31/r1.anchor: فقد حكى لنا النضر بن شميل أنه دخل على المأمون عند مقدمه من مرو

KHATTABI:v1p31/r2.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p31/r2.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p31/r2.claim: “Balā” answers a negatively framed question and affirms its denied proposition, as in the covenant; “naʿam” answers a question framed with “hal,” as in the question about God’s promise.
KHATTABI:v1p31/r2.anchor: فإن بلى جواب عن استفهام بحرف النفي كقول القائل: ألم تفعل كذا؟

KHATTABI:v1p31/r3.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p31/r3.speaker: الفراء
KHATTABI:v1p31/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says “balā” only answers a question containing negation; had the primordial offspring answered “naʿam,” they would all have disbelieved.
KHATTABI:v1p31/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: بلى لا يكون إلا جوابا عن مسألة يدخلها طرف من الجحد.

KHATTABI:v1p31/r4.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p31/r4.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p31/r4.claim: The demonstrative “dhāk” points to something near the speaker, whereas “dhālik” is used for something farther away.
KHATTABI:v1p31/r4.anchor: وأما قولك: ذاك وذلك فإن الإشارة بذلك إنما تقع إلى الشيء القريب منك , وذلك إنما يستعمل فيما كان متراخيا عنك.

KHATTABI:v1p31/r5.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p31/r5.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p31/r5.claim: “Min” and “ʿan” differ in common usage: taking money is from someone, taking knowledge is on their authority; hearing speech from someone is direct, while hearing a report about them is mediated, though the particles sometimes overlap.
KHATTABI:v1p31/r5.anchor: وأما من وعن فإنهما يفترقان في مواضع كقولك: أخذت منه مالا , وأخذت عنه علما

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p188/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p188/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p188/r1.claim: Only three declarative negative clauses with laysa lack the prefixed bā on the predicate, according to her survey of the Qur’an.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p188/r1.anchor: وهذه الآيات الثلاث فحسب، هي التي لم يقترن خبر ليس فيها بالباء، في الكتاب العربي المبين

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p188/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p188/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p188/r2.claim: Interrogative laysa clauses regularly place bā before the predicate; they turn apparent negation into emphatic affirmation, often answered by balā or left unanswered.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p188/r2.anchor: وأما الجمل الاستفهامية، فيطرد مجئ الخبر فيها مقترناً بالباء، لا يتخلف

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p198/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p198/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p198/r5.claim: This example illustrates that Qur’anic expression needs no conjectured deleted particle; she compares it with verses about God holding the heavens and earth and taking humanity’s testimony.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p198/r5.anchor: ذلك مثل مما قالوا فيه بحذف الحرف، يمكن أن يصدق على حروف أخر قالوا فيها بالتأويل على الحذف

NASHR:v2p273/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p273/r3.speaker: ابن كثير والكوفيون
NASHR:v2p273/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir and the Kufans read ذرية in the singular without alif and with fatḥa on tāʾ at all three locations.
NASHR:v2p273/r3.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير، والكوفيون بغير ألف على التوحيد في الثلاثة مع فتح التاء

NASHR:v2p273/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p273/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p273/r4.claim: Abu Amr joins that singular reading only at the Yasin occurrence.
NASHR:v2p273/r4.anchor: وافقهم أبو عمرو على حرف يس

NASHR:v2p273/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p273/r5.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p273/r5.claim: The remaining readers use a plural with alif and kasra on tāʾ at all three locations.
NASHR:v2p273/r5.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالألف على الجمع مع كسر التاء في المواضع الثلاثة

NASHR:v2p273/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p273/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p273/r6.claim: Abu Amr reads both أن تقولوا and أو تقولوا in the third person.

NASHR:v2p273/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p273/r7.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p273/r7.claim: The remaining readers address the audience directly in both expressions.

AZRAQI:v1p323/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p323/r1.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
AZRAQI:v1p323/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ says the Corner is a stone from Paradise and would remain as it descended if impurities had not touched it.
AZRAQI:v1p323/r1.anchor: حدثنا عبد الله بن يحيى السهمي قال سمعت عطاء بن أبي رباح يقول الركن حجر من حجارة الجنة

AZRAQI:v1p323/r2.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p323/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
AZRAQI:v1p323/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes the Corner as God's right hand on earth, through which He shakes hands with His servants as one greets a brother.
AZRAQI:v1p323/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال الركن يمين الله في الأرض يصافح بها عباده كما يصافح أحدكم أخاه

AZRAQI:v1p323/r3.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p323/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
AZRAQI:v1p323/r3.claim: At the Kaaba, ʿUmar says he knows the Stone can neither harm nor benefit, but kisses it because he saw the Messenger of God kiss it.
AZRAQI:v1p323/r3.anchor: قال خرجنا مع عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه إلى مكة فلما دخلنا الطواف قام عند الحجر

AZRAQI:v1p323/r4.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p323/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
AZRAQI:v1p323/r4.claim: ʿAlī answers that the Stone does benefit and harm by God's Book: God extracted Adam's progeny, elicited their covenant, recorded it on a scroll placed in the Stone, and made it a witness for visitors.
AZRAQI:v1p323/r4.anchor: قال له علي عليه السلام بلى يا أمير المؤمنين هو يضر وينفع قال وبم ذلك قال بكتاب الله تعالى

AZRAQI:v1p323/r5.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p323/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
AZRAQI:v1p323/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God will raise the Stone on Judgment Day with two seeing eyes and a speaking tongue, to testify for whoever touched it rightly.
AZRAQI:v1p323/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال ليبعثن الله عز وجل هذا الحجر يوم القيامة وله عينان يبصر بهما ولسان ينطق به

AZRAQI:v1p323/r6.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p323/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
AZRAQI:v1p323/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās again calls the Black Stone God's right hand on earth, by which He greets His servants as a man greets his brother.
AZRAQI:v1p323/r6.anchor: قال سمعت ابن جريج يقول سمعت محمد بن عباد بن جعفر يقول سمعت ابن عباس يقول إن هذا الركن الأسود

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r1.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r1.claim: The Prophet says that fire would not touch a Qur'an contained in a hide; an anonymous gloss explains this as meaning that a person who carries and recites the Qur'an will not be touched by Hellfire on Judgment Day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r1.anchor: قال: سمعت عقبة بن عامر يقول: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r2.claim: An anonymous gloss says that whoever carries and recites the Qur'an will not be touched by the Fire on Judgment Day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r2.anchor: قيل معناه من حمل القرآن وقرأه لم تمسه النار يوم القيامة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd calls the Qur'an God's banquet, rope, clear light, healing, protection, and salvation; it does not mislead or warp, its wonders never end or wear out through repetition, and each letter recited earns ten good deeds, with alif, lām, and mīm counted separately.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: " [إن هذا القرآن مأدبة الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r4.claim: Baghawī notes that some transmit Ibn Masʿūd's Qur'an report as a Prophetic report; he also gives a separate chain in which the Prophet states its meaning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r4.anchor: ورواه بعضهم عن ابن مسعود مرفوعا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r5.speaker: أبو الطفيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r5.claim: ʿUmar approves appointing the freedman Ibn Abzā over Mecca because he recites Qur'an, knows inheritance law, and judges; he invokes the Prophet's statement that God raises people through the Qur'an, though the excerpt ends mid-report.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p39/r5.anchor: عن عامر بن واثلة أبي الطفيل " أن نافع بن عبد الحارث لقي عمر بن الخطاب

ABUDAWUD:4703/r1.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:4703/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUDAWUD:4703/r1.claim: Umar reports the Prophet’s explanation: God brought Adam’s descendants forth as two groups destined for Paradise or Fire; each is enabled to perform the matching deeds until death, which lead to that end.
ABUDAWUD:4703/r1.anchor: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم سُئِلَ عَنْهَا

IBNHIBBAN:6166/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:6166/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNHIBBAN:6166/r1.claim: Umar reports that God drew two groups of descendants from Adam’s back, assigning one to Paradise and the other to Hell, each to act in keeping with that destiny.
IBNHIBBAN:6166/r1.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عنها، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن الله خلق آدم ثم مسح على ظهره بيمينه فاستخرج منه ذرية، فقال: خلقت هؤلاء للجنة

IBNHIBBAN:6166/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:6166/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:6166/r2.claim: Asked why people should act if their destinies are fixed, the Prophet says God enables each person to do the deeds of the destination assigned to him and die upon such a deed.
IBNHIBBAN:6166/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن الله إذا خلق العبد للجنة استعمله بعمل أهل الجنة حتى يموت على عمل من أعمال أهل الجنة فيدخله به الجنة

IBNHIBBAN:165/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:165/r1.speaker: معاوية بن الحكم السلمي
IBNHIBBAN:165/r1.claim: Muʿāwiya reports that the Prophet judged a maid a believer after she affirmed God is in heaven and Muhammad is God’s Messenger, then instructed him to emancipate her.
IBNHIBBAN:165/r1.anchor: أخبرنا الفضل بن الحباب حدثنا محمد بن المثنى حدثنا بن أبي عدي عن حجاج الصواف حدثنا يحيى بن أبي كثير عن هلال بن أبي ميمونة عن عطاء بن يسار عن معاوية بن الحكم السلمي قال: كانت لي غنيمة ترعاها جارية

IBNHIBBAN:2247/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:2247/r1.speaker: معاوية بن الحكم السلمي
IBNHIBBAN:2247/r1.claim: Muʿāwiya reports that omens are inner feelings that do no harm, Muslims must avoid soothsayers, and a prophet practiced line drawing, whose method is not otherwise identified.
IBNHIBBAN:2247/r1.anchor: حدثنا معاوية بن الحكم السلمي قال قلت يا رسول الله إنا كنا حديث عهد بجاهلية فجاء الله بالإسلام وإن رجالا منا يتطيرون

IBNHIBBAN:2247/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:2247/r2.speaker: معاوية بن الحكم السلمي
IBNHIBBAN:2247/r2.claim: After Muʿāwiya spoke to a man during prayer, the Prophet taught that ordinary human speech does not belong in prayer, which consists of glorification, magnification, and Quran recitation.
IBNHIBBAN:2247/r2.anchor: ولكن قال صلى الله عليه وسلم "إن صلاتنا هذه لا يصلح فيها شيء من كلام الناس إنما هو التسبيح والتكبير

IBNHIBBAN:2247/r3.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:2247/r3.speaker: معاوية بن الحكم السلمي
IBNHIBBAN:2247/r3.claim: The repeated account says the Prophet emancipated Muʿāwiya’s maid after she affirmed God’s location in heaven and identified Muhammad as God’s Messenger, taking her affirmation as evidence of faith.
IBNHIBBAN:2247/r3.anchor: وأطلقت غنيمة لي ترعاها جارية لي قبل أحد والجوانية فوجدت الذئب قد ذهب منها بشاة وأنا رجل من بني آدم آسف كما يأسفون

MALIK:1624/r1.author: MALIK
MALIK:1624/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MALIK:1624/r1.claim: Asked by Umar about the verse, the Prophet says God drew descendants from Adam twice, assigning one group to Paradise and another to the Fire and their respective deeds.
MALIK:1624/r1.anchor: فقال عمر بن الخطاب سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسأل عنها فقال رسول الله

MALIK:1624/r2.author: MALIK
MALIK:1624/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MALIK:1624/r2.claim: When asked what deeds matter, the Prophet says God uses each destined servant in the deeds of that destination until death, then admits him to it.
MALIK:1624/r2.anchor: فقال رجل يا رسول الله ففيم العمل قال فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUSNAD-AHMAD:310/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:310/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:310/r1.claim: Umar reports the Prophet saying that God extracted Adam's descendants, assigning some to Paradise and others to Fire; each is enabled to do the deeds of their destination and dies on that course.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:310/r1.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عنها، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن الله خلق آدم ثم مسح ظهره بيمينه

MUSNAD-AHMAD:21227/r5.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21227/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21227/r5.claim: Ubayy reports that God gathered Adam's descendants as spirits, made them testify to His exclusive lordship, forbade shirk, and promised to send messengers and books to remind them of the covenant.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21227/r5.anchor: عن رفيع أبي العالية، عن أبي بن كعب، في قول الله عز وجل: (وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذرياتهم (1)

MUSNAD-AHMAD:21227/r6.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21227/r6.speaker: الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21227/r6.claim: Adam saw that the people differed in wealth and appearance and asked why they were not made equal; God answered that He desired gratitude.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21227/r6.anchor: فقال: رب لولا سويت بين عبادك؟ قال: إني أحببت أن أشكر

MUSNAD-AHMAD:21227/r7.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21227/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21227/r7.claim: Ubayy adds that the prophets shone like lamps and received a distinct covenant of prophethood and messengership; Jesus was among them, sent to Mary.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21227/r7.anchor: عن رفيع أبي العالية، عن أبي بن كعب، في قول الله عز وجل: (وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذرياتهم (1)

MUSNAD-AHMAD:2455/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2455/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2455/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet identifying Naʿmān (Arafah) as the site where God extracted Adam's descendants, scattered them like specks, and addressed them, citing the warning against later claiming ignorance or ancestral shirk.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2455/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " أخذ الله الميثاق من ظهر آدم بنعمان

TIRMIDHI:3075/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3075/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TIRMIDHI:3075/r1.claim: In the report Umar transmits, the Prophet explains the verse as God bringing descendants from Adam’s back and assigning one group to Paradise and one to Fire, each doing the deeds of its destination.
TIRMIDHI:3075/r1.anchor: فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ آدَمَ ثُمَّ مَسَحَ ظَهْرَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَاسْتَخْرَجَ مِنْهُ ذُرِّيَّةً

TIRMIDHI:3075/r2.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3075/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TIRMIDHI:3075/r2.claim: Asked what use deeds have if destinies are set, the Prophet says God enables the person destined for Paradise to do its deeds until death, and likewise the person destined for Fire.
TIRMIDHI:3075/r2.anchor: فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ إِذَا خَلَقَ الْعَبْدَ لِلْجَنَّةِ اسْتَعْمَلَهُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ حَتَّى يَمُوتَ

TIRMIDHI:3075/r3.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3075/r3.speaker: أبو عيسى
TIRMIDHI:3075/r3.claim: Tirmidhi grades the report hasan but notes Muslim b. Yasar did not hear directly from Umar; some versions insert an unnamed intermediary.
TIRMIDHI:3075/r3.anchor: قال أبو عيسى هذا حديث حسن

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p266/r8.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p266/r8.speaker: زهير عن خصيف
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p266/r8.claim: Zuhayr from Khuṣayf reads ذرئيتهم as a singular with hamza; the author says this establishes derivation from ذرأت, meaning created, rather than ذرّ or ذروت/ذريت.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p266/r8.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة زهير عن خصيف: "من ظهورهم ذريئتهم"2 واحدة مهموزة.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p266/r9.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p266/r9.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p266/r9.claim: Deriving the unhamzated form from ذرّ while treating it as فعليّة and adding hamza like قطا جؤني is too anomalous to be heard or used as an analogy.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p266/r9.anchor: هذا من الشذوذ؛ بحيث لا يسمع أصلا، فضلا عن "65و" أن يتخذ قياسا.
